units.tr: To the illustrious and noble Count and Lord, Lord Friedrich, Count of Solms, Lord of Muntzenberg, Sonnenwald and Wildenfels, Knight, and chief commander of the soldiers of the confederated maritime cities, my gracious lord,

units.la: GRATIAM ET PACEM A DEO PATRE per Dominum nostrum JESUM CHRISTUM.
units.tr: GRACE AND PEACE FROM GOD THE FATHER through our Lord JESUS CHRIST.

units.la: Illustris ac generose Domine Co-mes, domine benignissime. Multi & magni sunt ecclesiae Christi tituli: dicitur enim vinea Domini, domus Domini viventis; columna veritatis; caelestis Jerusalem; sponsa, corpus, sors, regnum & hereditas Filii Dei Domini nostri Jesu Christi; mater fidelium; columna & firmamentum veritatis. Oportet etiam, ut omnes & singuli fideles, quotquot salvari volunt, sese illi adjungant. At ardua & diffi-
units.tr: Most illustrious and noble Count, most kind lord. The Church of Christ has many and great titles. It is called the vineyard of the Lord, the house of the living God, the pillar of truth, the heavenly Jerusalem, the bride, body, portion, kingdom and inheritance of the Son of God our Lord Jesus Christ, the mother of believers, the pillar and foundation of truth. It is also necessary that all and each of the faithful, as many as wish to be saved, join themselves to her. But the arduous and diffi-

units.la: Præfatio.
units.tr: Preface.

units.la: & difficilis quæstio est, ubi & apud quos ecclesia vera reperiatur: et hodie imprimis id quæritur inter orthodoxos Protestantes, & pontificios Romanenses.
units.tr: It is a difficult and hard question where and among whom the true Church is to be found, and today this is asked above all among the orthodox Protestants and the Roman Papists.

units.la: Magniloqui Romanensium oratores multis prædicant ecclesiæ suæ laudes: in eâ sola dicunt omnes promissiones, quæ in S. literis de pulcherrima Christi sponsa exstant, esse completas; illam ajunt esse verissimè Christianam, apostolicam, catholicam, antiquissimam, atq; inde ab apostolis semper durasse, & fidem salvificam, deficientibus aliis quamplurimis, sanctè semper asservasse; ad illam etiam omnes veteres patres confugisse, imò verò totum orbem Christianum in hunc usq; diem cum illa communicasse. In illa porrò sola reperiri veræ fidei propagationem, veros episcopos ac fidos Dei servos; Illam solam esse verè & absolutè sanctam, inq; ea doceri nihil falsum, nihil turpe; summam item in doctrina ejus animadverti efficaciam, ab eaq; quam plurimas et diversas gentes ad religionem Christianam conversas esse. In ea sola salutem æternam esse quærendam; atq; infœlicem semper fuisse exitum illorum, florum, qui eam oppugnare sint ausi. Omnia autem adornant atq; adeo prædicant hoc consilio et fine, ut suas adulterationes, quas in ecclesiam invexerunt, invitis et Deo et hominibus, possint retinere et propagare, atq; ita simpliciores suis fumis, licet jamdudum per Dei gratiam S. scriptura luce sint discussi, iterum fascinare, vel Panico terrore ab agenda verbi divini veritate proturbare.
units.tr: The boastful orators of the Romanists praise their Church with many words. They say that in it alone are fulfilled all the promises that Scripture makes about the most beautiful bride of Christ. They say she is most truly Christian, apostolic, catholic and most ancient, that she has lasted from the apostles until now, and that she has always kept the saving faith sacred when many others fell away. They add that all the ancient Fathers fled to her, and indeed that the whole Christian world has communed with her down to this day. Only in her, they say, is the true faith propagated, and true bishops and faithful servants of God are found. She alone is truly and absolutely holy, and nothing false or shameful is taught in her. They also point to the great efficacy of her doctrine, by which very many and diverse nations have been converted to the Christian religion. Eternal salvation is to be sought in her alone, and those who have dared to attack her have always come to an unhappy end. They adorn and proclaim all these things with this aim and purpose: that they may retain and spread the corruptions they have introduced into the Church, against the will of both God and men, and so bewitch the simpler folk again with their smoke, though by the grace of God the Scripture of God has long since been brought into the light, or drive them away from embracing the truth of the divine Word by a Panic terror.

units.la: Contrà debacchantur in ecclesias protestantium eorumq; doctores: atq; hos dicunt hæreticos, schismaticos, sectarios, Deo & omnibus sanctis invisos: utpote qui ab auctoribus suis, puta Luthero, Calvino, Zvinglio et similibus nomina induerint, à communi antiquitatis consensu discesserint, pastoribus & doctoribus suis ordinariis debita obsequia denegarint; et contrà novas ac horrendas opiniones confinxerint, hominib; improbis ac male feriatis ad omnis generis scelera januâ aperuerint: et sexcenta alia.
units.tr: On the other side they rage against the churches of the Protestants and their teachers. They call these heretics, schismatics and sectaries, hateful to God and to all the saints, since they have taken their names from their authors, namely Luther, Calvin, Zwingli and the like; since they have departed from the common consent of antiquity; since they have denied due obedience to their ordinary pastors and teachers; and since, on the contrary, they have invented new and horrible opinions and opened the door to every kind of crime for wicked men who are ill at ease. And they say six hundred other things.

units.la: Illorum emissarii atq; oratores cernuntur insuper passim in regum et principum aulis, eosq; omnibus modis obtrectâdo, calumniando in odium orthodoxarum ecclesiarum inflammant, & ad propugnāda armis ferrog; pōt ficis[?] Romani auctoritate vel potius tyrannide incitāt. Et ut illud quod volunt facilius ac facilius obtineant, prædicant superiorum seculorū tranquillitatem, concordiam & fœlicissimum statum, quibus videlicet in toto orbe regnavit sedes Romana; & contra conquer[illegible, ~1 letter] de nostri temporis infelicitate, bellis, turbis, odiis, insidiis, condemnationibus, proscriptionibus, cædibus, & undique circumstantibus rerum et vitæ periculis, omniumq; illorum malorum culpam imputant ecclesiarum reformationi.
units.tr: Their emissaries and orators are also seen everywhere in the courts of kings and princes, and by disparaging them, slandering them in every way, they inflame them against the orthodox churches, and urge them to take up arms and sword in defence of the authority, or rather the tyranny, of the Roman Pontiff. And so that they may more easily obtain what they want, they proclaim the tranquillity, the harmony and the most happy state of earlier centuries, when of course the Roman See reigned over the whole world. And on the other hand they complain of the unhappiness of our own time, its wars, disturbances, hatreds, plots, condemnations, proscriptions, slaughters, and the dangers to goods and life that surround us on every side. They impute the blame for all these evils to the reformation of the Churches.

units.la: Offenduntur multi: infirmiores admodum turbantur: quamplurimi fluctuantur animis: quidam ad tumidam Iesuitarum maledicentiam taceri volunt: nonnulli autem partim ob publici status ruinam, partim ob suarum opum et commodorum jacturam fremunt: alii nondum satis de doctrinā confirmati admirantur et cogitant, quam ob causam ecclesiarum reformationem tanta consequatur malorum moles, omniaq; ruant in deterius, quā religionis emendatione videbantur futura meliora. At quicunque attentius communem piorum exaedificationem consideraverint, agnoscent apprime necessarium esse, si piè & maturè adversus improborum tela nos atque alios muniamus, omnibusque demonstremus, quàm multa technâ[?], quamque varia fraudes in synagogâ Romanâ occultetur, de quibus viri boni vix suspicari possent, si ab[?]iter illorum ordines, constitutiones et decreta inspiciant.
units.tr: Many are offended; the weaker ones are greatly disturbed; very many waver in their minds; some wish the Jesuits' swollen slander to be silenced; and some grumble, partly over the ruin of the public state and partly over the loss of their wealth and advantages. Others, not yet sufficiently confirmed in doctrine, marvel and wonder for what reason such a mass of evils follows the reformation of the Churches, and why everything collapses for the worse, when by the emendation of religion better things were thought to be coming. But whoever will consider more attentively the common edification of the pious will recognise that it is most necessary, if we arm ourselves and others devoutly and in good time against the missiles of the wicked, and show to all how many and how various frauds are hidden in the Roman synagogue, frauds which good men could scarcely suspect if they did not examine the orders, constitutions and decrees of that party.

units.la: Quia itaque Romanenses variis conatibus veritatem Christianam studeant opprimere, omni studio in id incumbent fidi Dei servi, ne aut supinâ negligentiâ aut horrendo beneficii divini contemtu cœlestis doctrinæ puritatem, parētum[?] nostrorum seculo ex densissimis tenebris in lucem revocatam, Satanicis Romanensium erroribus ac commētis inquinari patiantur. Et quoniam ab ipsa ecclesia nos excludunt, non erit absre[?], si illorum impietatem ac figmenta detegamus, et de jure Protestantium adversus pontificem eiusque fulmina et ac[?]edlas[?] infirmiores erudiamus. Illud autem commodissimè fiet, si non[?] de nomine neq; ex vestitu tantum, sed ad præscriptum Christi ex voce doctrinæ ecclesiam veram et pastores veros à falsis discernere discamus; simulq; ex scripturâ S. demonstremus, synagogam pontificiam, licet vetus ecclesia Romana, si ad tempora apostolorum et quæ proximè eos secuta sunt suspexerimus, inter reliquas sicuti Luna inter stellas, virtute ac doctrinâ præluxerit, multoq; insuper sanguine veritatem evangelicâ obsignarit, postea turpissimè à pristinâ fide & virtute Christiana defecisse, ita ut verè illi competat illud Esaja, Quomodo facta est meretrix civitas fidelis; ac proinde omnibus et singulis piis illius communionem fugiendam esse.
units.tr: Since therefore the Romanists strive by various efforts to oppress the Christian truth, faithful servants of God will apply every zeal to see that neither by a idle negligence nor by a horrible contempt of the divine benefit do they allow the purity of heavenly doctrine, recalled into the light from the thickest darkness in the age of our fathers, to be defiled by the Satanic errors and inventions of the Romanists. And since they exclude us from the Church itself, it will not be out of place if we expose their impiety and fictions, and instruct the weaker ones about the right of Protestants against the Pontiff and his thunderbolts. This will be done most conveniently if we learn not by name nor by clothing alone, but according to Christ's prescription, from the voice of doctrine, to distinguish the true Church and true ministers from false ones; and at the same time we show from Holy Scripture that the Papist synagogue, though it is the old Roman Church, if we look back to the times of the apostles and those immediately following them, shone among the rest, as the moon among the stars, in virtue and doctrine, and sealed the evangelical truth with much blood besides, but afterwards most shamefully fell away from its former faith and Christian virtue, so that the saying of Isaiah truly applies to it: "How has the faithful city become a harlot!"; and therefore all and each of the pious must flee from its communion.

units.la: Argumentum hoc tractarunt prolixè et nervosè multi viri magni et præstantes inter Dei servos: quia autem juniores ad hæc studia sæpius excitari debet, visū[?] fuit meū[?] auditorib, id brevius repetere, pro eā quantulacūq; facultate, quā pro suā bonitate Deus largiri voluit, atq; instituti & muneris mei ratione. Materia satis est ardua, sed tamen Dei beneficio nunc talis, de qua ex principiis justis cuivis pio facile sit judicare.
units.tr: Many great and outstanding men among the servants of God have treated this subject at length and vigorously. But since younger men ought to be stirred up to these studies more often, it seemed good to me to repeat it more briefly for my audience, according to whatever small ability God in his goodness has been pleased to bestow, and according to the plan of my office and duty. The matter is difficult enough, but by God's benefit it is now of such a kind that anyone may easily judge it from just principles.

units.la: Præfatio.
units.tr: Preface.

units.la: Methodum, quam observavi, volo commendare pluribus. Nihil novi in tota hac scriptione affero, sed tantum antiqua, hoc est usitatam ecclesiarum orthodoxarum doctrinam repeto, eamq; vere catholicum piorum consensum esse non dubito. Abstineo autem à calumniis, probris & scommatis; atq; orthodoxam sententiam sincerè, breviter & perspicuè propono; ac S. scripturæ, rationum & patrum firmamentis ipsorumq; pontificiorum assensionibus & suffragiis confirmo; adversariorum denique sophismata, calumnias & criminationes non minus perspicuè, quantum fert instituti nostri ratio, refuto.
units.tr: I wish to recommend to many the method I have followed. In this whole treatise I bring forward nothing new. I only repeat the ancient doctrine, that is, the doctrine customarily held by the orthodox churches, and I do not doubt that this is truly the universal consensus of the pious. I abstain, however, from calumnies, insults and jests. I set forth the orthodox opinion sincerely, briefly and clearly, and I confirm it by the support of Holy Scripture, of reasons and of the Fathers, and by the very assents and votes of the Papists themselves. Finally, I refute the sophisms, calumnies and accusations of the adversaries no less clearly, as far as the nature of my plan allows.

units.la: Quum verò dispicerem, cui potissimum hanc exercitationum nostrarum particulam more recepto dedicarem, vestra virtutes illustris & generosæ Comes, domine clementissime, ad se allicientes dubitationem omnem exemerunt. Nam quum ante annos XVII in Generosæ tuæ comitatum incidissem, ea non vulgarem favorem mihi, homini ignoto, probavit. Itaq; non tantum ex eo me semper illi de-vinctum[?]
units.tr: But when I considered to whom I should dedicate this part of my exercises, as is the accepted custom, your illustrious and noble virtues, most gracious Count and lord, drew me to themselves and removed every doubt. For when I came into your Nobility's company some seventeen years ago, it showed a not ordinary favour toward me, a man unknown to it. Therefore, not only for that reason have I always been bound to him

units.la: Præfatio.
units.tr: Preface.

units.la: vinctum duxi, verùm etiam occasionem commodam exoptavi, ut aliquando debitæ meæ gratitudinis & observantiæ testimonium aliquod pro ingenii & virium mearum modulo exstaret. Accedunt cùm illustris ac perantiquæ familiæ tuæ splendor, tùm generosa indoles & virtutes haud vulgares: nam præterquam quod inde à teneris tuo merito inter lumina & exem-pla pietatis, eruditionis, humanitatis ac modestiæ fueris numeratus, nec minorem laudem tibi multarum rerum experientiâ & linguarum cognitione apud omnes comparaveris; testatur Belgiũ[?], & confirmat communis patria nostra Germania T. Gene-rositate, ubi vix ex ephebis fuisset egres-sa, præclarorum majorum vestigiis insi-stentem in ipsis tyrociniis rei militaris sub illustrissimo atq; expertissimo polemarcho & incomparabili Heroë principe Mauricio Nassovico, eximia ac præclara magna-nimitatis et fortitudinis signa edidisse, postmodum, non diu in secundis vel ter-tiis perstitisse, sed ad majora et summa munera in Hungaricis Belgicis & Germanicis expeditionibus ascendisse, easq;
units.tr: but I considered it a debt, and I also longed for a fitting occasion to give some public testimony of my gratitude and respect, as far as my talent and strength allow. Your illustrious and very ancient family's renown adds to this, as do your noble character and uncommon virtues. From your earliest years you have been counted by all among the lights and models of piety, learning, courtesy and modesty, and you have won no smaller praise from everyone for your wide experience and your knowledge of languages. Belgium bears witness to this, and our common fatherland Germany confirms it. Your Generosity, scarcely out of boyhood and following in the footsteps of your distinguished ancestors, showed signs of extraordinary and remarkable magnanimity and courage in the very first stages of your military training, under the most illustrious and most experienced commander, the incomparable hero Prince Maurice of Nassau. Afterwards you did not remain long in junior or middle ranks, but rose to greater and highest commands in the Hungarian, Belgian and German campaigns, and these

units.tr: Preface.

units.la: summa cum laude sustinuisse, atque ab ipso augustissimo ROMANORUM IMPERATORE, in solemni sua inaugurationis & coronationis actu, equestri dignitate condecoratam fuisse: insuper vero etiam tuam famam ad hac ora Saxoniæ & ad has antiquissimo ac celeberrimo sedere Hanseatico iunctas civitates ita percrebescere cœpisse, ut illæ civitates, quæ ex ipsis arctius confederatæ sunt, summam apud se rerum militarium curam, summique militum Ducis officium (quod antè ex ducali, quin imò regali prosapia oriundi Principes sibi honori duxerunt) Generosi tuæ committendum unanimi consensu decreverint. Quàm sagacem autē, magnanimum, fidum ac prudentem ducem in munere tibi commisso, cùm in aliis plurimis rebus, tum nuper quoq; cum singulari fortitudinis & sapientia tua prædicatione demonstraveris, agnoscunt omnes boni. Nos etiam tua studia & piam voluntatem in communi salute nostra promovenda, nisi velimus ingratissimo esse animo, sanè dicè laudare ac sincerè prædicare merito nunquam desistimus.
units.tr: ...to have sustained with the highest distinction, and to have been honoured with knighthood by the most august Emperor of the Romans himself at the solemn act of his inauguration and coronation. Moreover, your fame has begun to spread so widely along this coast of Saxony and among these most ancient and renowned Hanseatic cities that those cities which are more closely bound to one another have unanimously resolved to entrust to your Nobility the supreme care of military affairs and the office of commander of their soldiers. Princes of ducal, indeed royal, lineage have formerly counted this office an honour. How wise, magnanimous, faithful and prudent a commander you are in the office committed to you, you have shown in many other matters and lately too with a singular display of your courage and wisdom, as all good men acknowledge. We also, unless we wish to be most ungrateful, never cease to praise your zeal and sincerely to proclaim your pious will in promoting our common welfare.

units.la: Has igitur altasq; eximias tui animi corporisq; dotes & virtutes (plura enim in laudem tuam verè et absq; omni palpo dici possent) quum perpenderem, neq; minus animo recolligerem quanto Generos tua amore ac favore comprimis hanc rèpublicam nostram, quam Deus pro sua infinita misericordia diutissime incolumem ac florentem nobis conservet, prosequatur; quam etiam mihi humanitatè & benevolentiam exhibuerit: speravi Generos tua non ingratum futurum, si hæc nostra scholastica exercitia in debitæ gratitudinis atq; observantiæ testimonium sub illius patrocinio divulgarem; eaq; animi mei declaratione testatum facerem, me seriis atq; ardentibus votis divinæ gratiæ ac tutelæ illam commendare, comprimis vero ut pergat, sicuti à primis annis asuevit, osculari Filium, suscipere nu-tricationem ecclesiæ Christi, atque odisse synagogas malignantium.
units.tr: Therefore, when I weighed these lofty and remarkable endowments and virtues of your mind and body (for much more could truly be said in your praise, and without any flattery), and when I called to mind how greatly your Generosity, by its love and favour, protects this our commonwealth, which God in his infinite mercy keep safe and flourishing for us for a very long time, and how much kindness and goodwill it has shown me, I hoped that your Generosity would not find it unwelcome if I published these our scholastic exercises under its patronage, as a testimony of due gratitude and respect. By this declaration of my mind I would also show that I commend it with earnest and ardent prayers to the divine grace and protection, and especially that it may continue, as it has been accustomed from its earliest years, to kiss the Son, to take up the nurture of the Church of Christ, and to hate the synagogues of the wicked.

units.tr: I therefore offer this declaration of my respect to your Generosity, in return for that singular inclination which you hold toward theological studies, the school, and our commonwealth, and I offer it with a calm and favourable

And I pray to God the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ that He may guide your Generosity's holy endeavours, and your whole life and welfare, with His fatherly grace and blessing, and keep you safe from all dangers.

units.la: ORDO CAPITVM vel quaestionum in hoc opusculo breviter & perspicuè tractatarum:
units.tr: Order of the chapters, or of the questions briefly and clearly treated in this little work:

units.la: 1. An iure Protestantium ecclesiae oppugnent pontificem Romanum, eiusque sectatores & iuratos: iure item ab eorum communione sese segregaverint? pag.1. & seq. item pag.51. & seq.
units.tr: 1. Whether by right the Protestant churches attack the Roman pontiff and his adherents and sworn followers, and whether by right they have separated themselves from their communion? pp. 1 ff., also pp. 51 ff.

units.la: 2. An pii, qui sub magistratu pontificio latent, coetus clandestinos, exercendae verae religionis nomine, contra illius edictum, instituere & fovere queant? pag.33.
units.tr: 2. Whether the pious, who lie hidden under the papal magistracy, may set up and foster secret assemblies in the name of exercising true religion, against its edict? p. 33.

units.la: 3. An iure Protestantes rejiciant auctoritatem concilii Tridentini, & reliquorum, quae ad praescriptum Romanensium instituuntur? pag.65. & seq. item pag.99.
units.tr: 3. Whether the Protestants by right reject the authority of the Council of Trent and of the other councils that are held according to the Roman prescription? pp. 65 ff., also p. 99.

units.la: 4. An pii moveri debeant banno atque anathematis Romanensium? p.92. etc. item p.121 & seq.
units.tr: 4. Whether the pious ought to be moved by the ban and anathema of the Romanists? p. 92 etc., also p. 121 ff.

units.la: 5. Qua ratione viri pii certi esse possint de veritate professionis suae? | p.131
units.tr: 5. By what reasoning can godly men be certain of the truth of their profession? | p. 131

units.la: 6. An principibus & aliis politicis viris concedi debeat judicium de rebus fidei? | pag.134
units.tr: 6. Should judgment on matters of faith be granted to princes and other political men? | p. 134

units.la: 7. Utrum Protestantes sint hæretici vel schismatici: an verò Romani pontifi-cii? pag.149.
units.tr: 7. Whether the Protestants are heretics or schismatics, or rather the Papists? p. 149.

units.la: 8. Quæ sit tutissima cum pontificiis disputandi, eosque convincendi ratio? pag.163
units.tr: 8. What is the safest method of disputing with the Papists and convincing them? p. 163

units.la: 9. Quinam possint judicare controversias theologicas. p.167
units.tr: 9. Who may judge theological controversies? p. 167

units.la: 10. Unde certò confirmentur pii de religionis Christianæ capitibus. p.169
units.tr: 10. Whence the pious may be surely confirmed concerning the chief heads of the Christian religion? p. 169

units.la: 11. An pastores & doctores Protestantiū sint legitimis Dei servis annumerandi. p.171
units.tr: 11. Whether the ministers and teachers of the Protestants are to be counted among the lawful servants of God? p. 171

units.la: 12. An præsules Romani sint habendi in numero fidorum Dei servorum? pag. 195
units.tr: 12. Are the Roman prelates to be regarded as among the faithful servants of God? p. 195

units.la: 13. An miracula Romanensium demonstrent illorum ecclesiam esse verâ Christi sponsam? p.213
units.tr: 13. Do the miracles of the Romanists show that their church is the true bride of Christ? p. 213

units.la: 14. Quæ sit tutissima via promovendi pacem & concordiam ecclesiarum? pag. 223.
units.tr: 14. What is the safest way of promoting peace and concord among the churches? p. 223.

units.tr: Psalm 119, vv. 113 ff.

units.la: Cogitationes alias odi, legem autem tuam diligo. Latebra & scutum meum es, in verbo tuo exspectationem habeo. Recedite à me malefici, ut custodiam præcepta DEI mei. Sustenta me secundùm sermonem tuum, ut vivam.
units.tr: I hate vain thoughts, but I love your law. You are my hiding place and my shield; I wait for your word. Depart from me, you evildoers, that I may keep the commandments of my God. Uphold me according to your word, that I may live.

units.la: Conculcas omnes errantes à statutis tuis: quia falsus est dolus eorum.
units.tr: You trample underfoot all who stray from your statutes, for their deceit is false.

units.la: DE JURE PROTESTANTIUM ORTHODOXORUM contra pontificem Romanum & ejus imperium.
units.tr: Concerning the Right of the Orthodox Protestants against the Roman Pontiff and his Government.

units.la: QUæritur, an jure ecclesiæ orthodoxæ protestantes oppugnent pontificem Romanum cum suis seductoribus, & juratis, quos vocant, tam doctoribus, quam auditoribus, qui illius traditiones & idololatriam approbant & tuentur: atq; ab eorum communione sese bonâ cōscientiâ segregarint? Romani pontifici negant. Orthodoxi protestantes affirmant.
units.tr: The question is whether, by the right of the orthodox Church, Protestants may oppose the Roman pontiff together with his seducers and his so-called sworn men, both teachers and hearers, who approve and defend his traditions and idolatry, and whether they may with a good conscience separate themselves from their communion. The Roman pontiff denies it. The orthodox Protestants affirm it.

units.la: Hæc est quæstio comprimis inter orthodoxos & pontificios controver-sia. Nota enim, nos neutiquâ deseruisse ecclesiam, quam Deus sibi in genere humano collegit & servat passim; atque adeo etiam in medio papatus, tum Romæ tum alibi: sed hoc profitemur, nos jure deseruisse, & ab omnibus piis deserendum esse papatum vel papam Romanum cum omnibus suis asseclis & juratis; corúmq; traditiones ex toto pecto-re atque animo aversari oportere. Nō enim intelligimus antiquam il-lam Romanā; neq; etiam simplici-ter quicquid in hodiernā Romana reperitur(quippe in quâ non pauci, ingemiscūt quotidie ad Dominum propter abominationes, quas illic vident & audiunt)sed propriā istius hodiernæ Romanę pontificię syna-gogæ doctrinam; seu religionem & professionem merè pontificiā. Non igitur etiam intelligimus omnes il-los, qui sunt vel vivunt in ecclesiā Romanā, sed qui in dictā doctrinā pontificiā integrè profitendā, & de-fendendā mordicus adhærent pon-tifici, & doctoribus pontificiis.
units.tr: This is above all the controversy between the orthodox and the Papists. For note that we have by no means deserted the Church, which God has gathered for himself from the human race and preserves everywhere, and so also in the midst of the papacy, both at Rome and elsewhere. What we profess is this: that we have rightly deserted the papacy, or the Roman pontiff with all his adherents and sworn men, and that all the pious ought to desert it, and that their traditions must be turned away from with the whole heart and mind. For we do not mean that ancient Roman Church, nor simply whatever is found in the present Roman Church (since in it not a few groan daily before the Lord because of the abominations which they see and hear there), but the proper doctrine of that present Roman pontifical synagogue, or its religion and profession, which is purely papal. Therefore we do not mean all those who are, or live, in the Roman Church, but those who cling stubbornly to the pontiff and the papal teachers, and who integrally profess and defend the said papal doctrine.

units.la: Quo iure affirmativam sententiam, as-seramus, liquidò apparet omnibus piis & sanæ mentis hominibus, ex argumentis se-quentibus.
units.tr: By what right we assert the affirmative opinion is clear to all pious and sound-minded people from the following arguments.

units.la: Nam patriarchę, prophetæ, apo-stoli ab idololatris & hypocritis, to-lo ecclesiæ titulo gloriatibus sæpis-sime secessionem fecerunt. diserte etiam illud omnes pii facere juben-tur. tur. Ita r. Reg. 18. 21 alloquitur Elias propheta huc in modum Israelitas. Si DOMINUS est Deus ipse, sequimini eum, sin autem istorum Baal, sequimini eum. Esa. 52. [?] ita ait Dominus: Discedite, discedite, exite illinc, & immundum ne attingitote: exite e medio istius &c. Hos. 4. 15. & 16. 8. dixit Dominus Judæis. Ne ascendatis Bethaven: nam licet fuerit Bethel, id est, domus Dei, nomine, tamen erat Bethaven, id est, domus vanitatis, te. act. 19. 9. legitur de Paulo, quòd, quum quidam ex Judæorum antistitibus indurarentur & non assentirentur sermoni, male loquentes de via illa Dei in conspectu multitudinis, abscedens ab illis separaverit discipulos. 2. Cor. 6. 14. & seq. generale hoc exstat mandatum: Ne impari jugo copulamini cum infidelibus: quod enim consortium justitiæ cum legis transgressione? & quæ communio lucis cum tenebris? & quæ concordia Christo cum Belial? aut quæ portio fideli cū infideli? & quæ cōsensio tēplo Dei cum simulacris. &c. Quapropter exite e medio eorum,& separamini, dicit Dominus, & impurum ne attingite, tum ego excipia vos. Similis locus occurrit. apoc. 18.2. et seq. Exclamavit (angelus) vehementer voce magna, dicés, cecidit, cecidit Babylon illa magna, & facta est domicilium dæmoniorū, & custodia omnis spiritus impuri, & custodia omnis volucris immundæ & exosæ: quia ex vino excandescentiæ fcortationis ejus biberūt omnes gentes; & reges terræ cum eâ fcortati sunt, & mercatores terræ opibus luxus ejus ditati sunt. Et audivi aliam vocem è cœlo dicentem, exite ex eâ, populę mi, ne participes fitis peccatorum ejus, & ex plagis ejus accipiatis. Plura id genus f. scripturæ & Spiritus f. effata vide 1. Cor. 6. 9. 10. & 10. 14. & seq. Gal. 5. 19. 1. Tim. 6. 3. 5. apoc. 14. 9. & seq.
units.tr: For the patriarchs, prophets and apostles very often withdrew from idolaters and hypocrites, though they gloried in the title of the Church. It is also expressly commanded that all the pious do this. Thus in 1 Kings 18:21 the prophet Elijah addresses the Israelites in this manner: "If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him." In Isaiah 52 the Lord says: "Depart, depart, go out from there, and touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of it," etc. In Hosea 4:15 and 16:8 the Lord said to the Jews: "Do not go up to Beth-aven; for although it bears the name Bethel, that is, the house of God, it was nevertheless Beth-aven, that is, the house of vanity." In Acts 19:9 we read of Paul that, when some of the leaders of the Jews were hardened and would not assent, speaking evil of that way of God before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples. In 2 Corinthians 6:14 and following there is this general command: "Do not be yoked together with unbelievers; for what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness? And what communion has light with darkness? And what concord has Christ with Belial? Or what part has the believer with the unbeliever? And what agreement has the temple of God with idols?" etc. "Therefore come out from among them, and be separate, says the Lord, and touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you." A similar passage occurs in Revelation 18:2 and following: "He cried mightily with a loud voice, saying, Fallen, fallen is that great Babylon, and has become the dwelling of demons, and the prison of every unclean spirit, and the cage of every unclean and hateful bird; for all nations have drunk of the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth have been enriched by the wealth of her luxury." And I heard another voice from heaven saying, "Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues." For more passages of this kind of Scripture and the sayings of the Spirit, see 1 Corinthians 6:9-10 and 10:14 and following; Galatians 5:19; 1 Timothy 6:3, 5; Revelation 14:9 and following.

units.la: Præterea verę ecclesię v[?] l cætuū ecclesiasticorum hic finis statuitur 1 Chron. 16. 8. 11. Psal. 42. 5. & 63. 3. et 84. 5. act. 2. 42. et alibi. Ut requiramus Jehovam, ejusque nomē celebremus.
units.tr: Moreover, this is the purpose appointed for the true Church and for ecclesiastical assemblies: "that we may seek Jehovah and celebrate his name" (1 Chronicles 16:8, 11; Psalm 42:5; 63:3; 84:5; Acts 2:42, and elsewhere).

units.la: Ex his manifestum fit, secedendū esse nobis, omnibusque piis ab illo cœtu, qui aut puram Dei cognitionē non tradit, aut purum ejus cultum non exercet: & contrà, errores capitales vel cum fidei fundamento & disertis scripturæ s. effatis pugnantes pertinaciter profitetur ac defendit.
units.tr: From these things it is evident that we and all the pious must secede from that assembly which either does not hand down the pure knowledge of God or does not practise his pure worship, and, on the contrary, stubbornly professes and defends capital errors, whether they are opposed to the foundation of the faith and to the plain sayings of Holy Scripture.

units.la: At hodierna Romana pontificia puram Dei cognitionē, purumque ejus cultum negligit, & contrà errores capitales pertinaciter defendit: videlicet traditiones suas s. scriptu-ræ testimoniis, & fundamento fidei è diametro repugnantes; cultúsque non tantùm falsos & fictitios, verum etiam impios atque idololatricos.
units.tr: But the present Roman papal church neglects the pure knowledge of God and his pure worship, and on the contrary stubbornly defends capital errors, namely its traditions, which are diametrically opposed to the testimonies of Holy Scripture and to the foundation of faith; and its worships are not only false and feigned, but also impious and idolatrous.

units.la: Itaque merito concludimus, protestantes orthodoxos jure ab illâ secessisse, & sacrilegii reos non sine ratione argui debere, nisi secessis-sent.
units.tr: Therefore we rightly conclude that orthodox Protestants have by right separated themselves from it, and that they ought not without reason to be accused as guilty of sacrilege, unless they had seceded.

units.la: Quàm manifestè autem & pertinaciter pontifices Romani cum suis asseclis scripturæ s. & capitibus religi-onis Christianæ adversentur, ab-unde constat ex inspectione omnium & singulorum locorum theologico-rum, de quibus inter orthodoxos & pontificios à multis annis conten-ditur, quosque consule. comprimis locum de verbo Dei & scriptura s.[?] de Christo mediatore; de lege, de evangelio: libero arbitrio: justifica-tione: bonis operibus: precibus: de ecclesia: pontifice Romano. & si-milia.
units.tr: How clearly and stubbornly, moreover, the Roman pontiffs with their adherents oppose Holy Scripture and the chief articles of the Christian religion is plain from the examination of all and each of the theological topics about which the orthodox and the Papists have been contending for many years, and which you may consult: especially the topic of the Word of God and Holy Scripture; of Christ the mediator; of the law and of the gospel; of free will; of justification; of good works; of prayers; of the Church; of the Roman pontiff; and similar matters.

units.la: Catalogum traditionum pontificiarum proposuimus in medulla papismi, de arce ac judice omnium controversiarum theologicarum pag. 182. 183, et aliquot sequentibus: & demonstravimus, illas è diametro scripturæ divinæ; atque adeo veri Dei & Domini nostri Jesu Christi gloriæ adversari.
units.tr: We have set out a catalogue of the papal traditions in the Medulla papismi, in De arce ac judice omnium controversiarum theologicarum, pp. 182, 183 and some following pages, and we have shown that they are diametrically opposed to the divine Scripture, and therefore to the glory of the true God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Quantaitem sit impietas pontificum Romanorum: quàm intrepidè scripturæ divinæ canone aspernentur, quamque graviter in hunc usque diem prope modum in omnibus & singulis doctrinæ Christianæ articulis à veritate evangelicâ aber-rent, docuimus pag. 197. 298 et seq. ac proproinde summo iure porrò asserui- mus, atque argumentis firmis con- firmavimus, Romanam synagogam neutiquam ecclesiæ Christi nomen promereri pag. 371. 372. et seq. Item pag. 385. et seq. quia in eâ publicè atque impunè vigeant idololatria, ty- rannis, atque omnis generis flagitia.
units.tr: How great is the impiety of the Roman pontiffs, how boldly they spurn the canon of divine Scripture, and how gravely they have to this day strayed from evangelical truth in almost all and each of the articles of Christian doctrine, we have taught at pp. 197, 298 and following; and therefore we assert with the highest right, and have confirmed by firm arguments, that the Roman synagogue by no means deserves the name of the Church of Christ, at pp. 371, 372 and following, and likewise at p. 385 and following, because idolatry, tyranny and every kind of wickedness flourish in it publicly and with impunity.

units.la: Ita manifestū fecimus omnibus vera luce præditis, à pontifice, atque ecclesiā repræsentativa Romana neque fidem Christi orthodoxè tradi, neque sacramenta rite admi- nistrari & celebrari, neq; preces piè ac religiosè concipi; neque disciplinam euangelicam sanctè & salubri- ter exerceri: & contrà, puram Dei cognitionem & cultum non tātum impiis superstitionibus contamina- ri, verūm etiam palàm & pertinaci- ter profanari.
units.tr: Thus we have made it manifest to all who possess the true light that from the pontiff and the Roman representative Church neither is the faith of Christ rightly handed down, nor are the sacraments duly administered and celebrated, nor are prayers devoutly and religiously framed, nor is the evangelical discipline holily and wholesomely exercised; and on the contrary, the pure knowledge and worship of God are not only defiled by impious superstitions, but also openly and stubbornly profaned.

units.la: Laborat enim Romana illa, de qua controvertitur, pestiferarum hæresium gangrena quaquaversum pervagante, & longè plurimorum fidem subvertente. Verbum Dei adul- terat multis modis, sicuti peculiari loco demostravimus. Cultum di-vinum nō minūs variis sordibus cō-spurcat ac evertit, puta Missalibus, Breviariis, Antiphonariis, & id ge-nus aliis ethnicorum excrementis: de quibus ipse pontifex Pius Quin-tus (in summar. constitut. praefix. isti[?] of-ficio, in edit. Plantiniana) ait, illa ossi-cia vanis erroribus superstitionum referta es se.ac pinde[?] revera imple-tur apud pontificios illud apostoli 2. Tim. 4,3. Erit tempus, quum sana doctrinam nō tolerabunt, sed aures ad fabulas divertent. Praeterea Dei cultum & honorem cum angelis & hominibus communicat: Imò cum imaginibus, ferrò, ligno &c. Spem salutis in suis aliorumq; hominum meritis ponit, non absq; insigni cō-tumelia in D. N. Iesum Christum. Sacramenta variis & profanis erro-rum atq; abusuum spurcitiis inqui-nat. Religionem deniq; omnem in miserrimam servitutem & merca-turam convertit.
units.tr: For that Roman church, of which there is dispute, is afflicted with the gangrene of pestilent heresies spreading on every side, and subverting the faith of very many. It corrupts the Word of God in many ways, as we have shown in a special place. It no less defiles and overturns the divine worship with various filths, namely the Missals, Breviaries, Antiphonaries, and other such excrements of the heathens; of which Pope Pius V himself (in the summary of the constitution prefixed to that office, in the Plantin edition) says that those offices are filled with vain errors of superstitions. And so in truth that saying of the apostle is fulfilled among the papists: 2 Timothy 4:3, "There will come a time when they will not endure sound doctrine, but will turn their ears to fables." Furthermore, it shares the worship and honour of God with angels and men; indeed, with images of iron, wood and so on. It places the hope of salvation in its own merits and those of other men, not without signal contumely against our Lord Jesus Christ. It defiles the sacraments with various profane filths of errors and abuses. Finally, it turns all religion into most wretched servitude and merchandise.

units.la: Atq; ut eo facilius hoc obtineat sacrificuli cum suo antistite, à scri-pturæ pturæ s. lectione auditores suos vi & fraude quovis modo arcent, atq; illius loco imagines, tanquam idiotarum libros, in templis collocant; lignum, eruditionem vanitatum, teste Jerem. cap. 10. 8. simulacrum, doctorem mendacii, teste Habac. cap. 2. 18.
units.tr: And so that they may more easily achieve this, the little sacrificers, together with their chief, keep their hearers from reading the holy Scripture by force and fraud in every way, and in its place set up images in the churches as books for the unlearned: "a wood, a teaching of vanities," as Jer. 10. 8 bears witness, "an image, a teacher of lies," as Hab. 2. 18 bears witness.

units.la: Et, ne quis eorum placitis contradicere audeat, spretâ Christi auctoritate, supremam in universâ ecclesiâ pontifici suo potestatem in ecclesiasticis & politicis causis tribuunt: Imò tantam, ut etiam contra apostolum, Christum ipsum & spiritum s. dispensare queat. Exempli gratia, ut sibi quis incestis nuptiis conjungat uxorem fratris sui, (sicuti Henricus VIII. rex Angliæ Catharinâ) aut sororis filiam (sicuti Philippus II. rex Hispaniæ Annam) contra disertum Dei interdictum Levit. 18. 12. 16. & 20. 21. de quo argumento prolixius item disseruimus in Medul-la papismi pag. 193. 194. et sequent. 331. et sequentibus. Si qui verò ex edicto apostoli Colos. 3. pio studio recondendi verbum Christi tenentur,
units.tr: And, lest anyone dare to contradict their decrees, they set aside the authority of Christ and grant their pontiff supreme power over the whole Church in ecclesiastical and political matters. Indeed they grant him so much that he can dispense even against the Apostle, against Christ himself and the Holy Spirit. For example, a man may take to himself in incestuous marriage his brother's wife (as Henry VIII, king of England, did with Catherine), or his sister's daughter (as Philip II, king of Spain, did with Anne), against God's plain prohibition, Lev. 18. 12, 16 and 20. 21. We have discussed this argument at greater length in our Medulla papismi, pp. 193, 194 and following, 331 and following. If, on the other hand, some are bound by pious zeal to store up the word of Christ, by the command of the Apostle in Col. 3,

units.la: atque ita interdictum pontificis violare praesumant, eos exquisitis tormentis, flammis, ferro, & crudelissima morte, sine omni conditionum, aetatum, & sexuum discrimine absumi decernunt. Consule annales, & innumera tyrannidis pontificia exempla reperies.
units.tr: and so presume to violate the pontiff's prohibition, they decree that such people be destroyed by exquisite torments, flames, the sword and the most cruel death, without regard to condition, age or sex. Consult the annals, and you will find countless examples of papal tyranny.

units.la: Ex his itaque denuo concludimus, non tantum licere nobis, verum etiam teneri nos ex conscientia, ut synagogam Romanam cum pontifice suo omni studio fugiamus, eorumque communione deseramus.
units.tr: From these things, therefore, we again conclude that it is not only lawful for us but that we are even bound in conscience to flee the Roman synagogue with its pontiff with all our zeal, and to forsake its communion.

units.la: Assentiuntur nobis patres. Ambrosius lib. 2. de Iacobo cap. 7. Ibi, inquit, ecclesia, in qua apparet Deus, & loquitur cum servis suis: ibi eripiuntur & absconduntur simulacra gentium.
units.tr: The Fathers agree with us. Ambrose, On Jacob, book 2, ch. 7. There, he says, is the Church in which God appears and speaks with his servants; there the images of the nations are taken away and hidden.

units.la: Augustinus tom. 7. epist. contra epist. Petiliani Donatistae cap. 2. 3. 4. Inter nos & Donatistas quaestio est, ubi sit ecclesia. Quid ergo facturi sumus? in verbis nostris eam quaesituri, an in verbis capitis sui, Domini nostri Jesu Christi? puto quod in illius potius verbis quaerere debemus, qui ve-ritas ritas est, & optimè novit corpus su-um. Chrysostomus supra Matth. cap. 7. è fructibus eorum cognoscetis eos) Fructus enim hominis est confessio fidei, & opera conversatio ipsius. Si ergo videris hominem Christianum, statim considera; si confessio ejus conveniat cū scripturis, verus est christianus: si autem non est, quemadmodum Christus mandavit; falsus est: judicium christianitatis non ad nomen retulit, sed ad confessionem: quia non solū nomen Christi christianum facit, sed veritas : quia in nomine Christi multi ambulant, in veritate autem pauci.
units.tr: Augustine, vol. 7, against the letter of Petilian the Donatist, chs. 2, 3, 4. Between us and the Donatists the question is where the Church is. What then shall we do? Shall we seek her in our own words, or in the words of her Head, our Lord Jesus Christ? I think we ought rather to seek her in the words of him who is the Truth and knows his own body best. Chrysostom on Matthew ch. 7, "By their fruits you shall know them." For a man's fruit is his confession of faith, and his conduct is his works. If therefore you see a Christian, consider at once whether his confession agrees with the Scriptures: if it does, he is a true Christian; if not, as Christ commanded, he is false. He did not refer the judgment of Christianity to the name but to the confession, for it is not the name of Christ alone that makes a Christian, but the truth; for many walk in the name of Christ, but few in the truth.

units.la: Idem sentiunt pontificii: Andradius defens. fid. Trident. lib. 1. affirmat quē-vis obedientiâ Deo debita obstringi, ut audacter repugnet pontificis Romani volūtati, si injusta imperet. Bellarm. lib. 2. de Rom. pontifice cap. 29. § Respondeo negando. Licet, inquit, resistere papæ invadenti corpus, vel turbanti rempub.; ita multo magis, si ecclesiam destruere conetur: licet (inquam) resistere ei, non faciendo quod jubet,& voluntatem ejus impediedo. Canisius catechef.cap.1. Christianum definit eum, qui baptismatis sacramento initiatus Jesu Christi veri Dei atque hominis salutarem doctrinam in ejus ecclesia profitetur; neq; sectis vel opinionibus ullis,ab ecclesia alienis, adhaeret. Enchiridion christianæ institutionis in concilio provinciali Coloniensi editum hæc habet,in expositione symboli in articul. Credo sanctam ecclesiam. Principio nemo negat in ecclesia sinceram doctrinā euangelicam & apostolicam esse oportere,& hanc præcipuam esse ecclesiæ notam ; juxta illud, oves meæ vocem meam audiunt:& quod est apud Paulum, si quis prædicaverit aliud euangelium, anathema sit. Parisiensis universitas vel Sorbona pridem ante Lutheri tempora Basiliensi synodo subscripsit,& negavit morem geri papæ oportere, si quid contra divina præcepta statuedū decrevit.
units.tr: The Papists themselves agree. Andradius, Defence of the Council of Trent, book 1, affirms that whatever obedience is owed to God binds us to resist boldly the will of the Roman pontiff if he commands unjust things. Bellarmine, On the Roman Pontiff, book 2, ch. 29, § "I answer by denying." "It is lawful," he says, "to resist a pope who attacks the body or disturbs the commonwealth; so much more if he tries to destroy the Church. It is lawful (I say) to resist him, by not doing what he orders and by hindering his will." Canisius, Catechism, ch. 1, defines a Christian as one who, initiated by the sacrament of baptism, professes in the Church the saving doctrine of Jesus Christ, true God and true man, and who does not cling to any sects or opinions alien to the Church. The Enchiridion of Christian Instruction, published by the provincial council of Cologne, in its exposition of the creed on the article "I believe the holy Church," contains this: "In the first place, no one denies that the sincere evangelical and apostolic doctrine ought to be in the Church, and that this is its chief mark, according to the saying, 'My sheep hear my voice'; and according to what is in Paul, 'If anyone preach another gospel, let him be accursed.'" The University of Paris, or the Sorbonne, long before Luther's time subscribed to the Council of Basel, and denied that the pope ought to be obeyed if he decreed anything against the divine precepts.

units.la: Infinitis vero passibus Romanā ecclesiam à veritate euangelicæ doctrinæ decessisse, similiter testantur comcomplures ex Iesuiticis doctoribus, de quo vide Medullam nostram papismi, dictis locis.
units.tr: Countless Jesuit teachers likewise testify that the Roman Church has in infinite steps departed from the truth of the evangelical doctrine. On this see our Medulla papismi, in the places cited.

units.la: Equidem non tantum remissio-res illi, Erasmus, Ferus, Vives, & si-miles, verum etiam quidam ex ma-ximè fervidis ecclesiæ Romanæ at-lantibus diserte profitentur, ecclesiam istam jam pridem laborare gravissimis ac pestiferis morbis. vide cõsilium delectorum Cardinalium tom. ult. conciliorum. Abbas Urspergensis Chron. in Philippo, filio Barbarosæ; Claudius Espensæus in Epist. ad Tit. c. 1. digress. 2. et alii dicunt illam sceleratam permultarum ecclesiarum præda-tricem, primariam causam schisma-tis, hæreticæ pravitatis, & vitiosæ cõ-versationis per orbem universum; quæ criminum omnigenorum, impudentissimorum, teterrimorum licentias palam nundinetur, quæ res sacras emat, vendat, turpi quæstu, profane, simoniacè &c. Adrianus papa VI. in legatione ad conventum Nuren-bergicum anno Domini 1522 in instru-ctione Francisci Cheregati. Scimus, in-quit quit, in hac sancta sede aliquot jam annis, multa abominanda fuisse, ab-usus in spiritualibus, excessus in mundanis, & omnia in perversum mutata. Franciscus de Victoria, relect. 4. de potest. papæ et concilii, propositione 6. et 12. vidimus, inquit, quotidie à Romana curia tam largas, imò omnino dissolutas dispensationes profectas, ut orbis ferre non posset; nec solùm in scandalum pusillorum, sed majorum: nullus dispensationem quærit, quin obtineat: & Romæ sunt exspectantes, an quis velit petere dispensationem omnium, quæ legibus sancita sunt: omnes, qui petunt, afferunt. Plura id genus testimonia vide in catalogo testium veritatis, qui ante nostram ætatem pontifici Romano atque papismi erroribus reclamarunt.
units.tr: Indeed, not only the more moderate men, Erasmus, Ferus, Vives and their like, but also some of the most fervent champions of the Roman Church, openly profess that this Church has for a long time been suffering from most grave and pestilent diseases. See the counsel of the chosen cardinals, in the last volume of the councils. The Abbot of Ursperg, Chronicle, under Philip, son of Barbarossa; Claude d'Espence, on Titus ch. 1, digression 2, and others say that this wicked plunderer of very many churches is the chief cause of schism, of heretical perversity and of corrupt living throughout the whole world; it openly sells licences for every sort of crime, most shameless and most foul; it buys and sells sacred things, profanely, simoniacally, for shameful gain, and so on. Pope Adrian VI, in his instruction to the legation to the Diet of Nuremberg in the year of the Lord 1522, in the instruction of Francesco Chieregati: "We know," he says, "that in this Holy See for some years many abominable things have been done: abuses in spiritual matters, excesses in worldly ones, and everything turned to the perverse." Francisco de Victoria, relection 4, On the Power of the Pope and of the Council, propositions 6 and 12: "We have seen," he says, "such broad and indeed wholly lax dispensations issuing every day from the Roman curia that the world cannot bear them, and not only to the scandal of the little ones but of their elders. No one seeks a dispensation without obtaining it; and at Rome men wait to see whether anyone wishes to ask for a dispensation from everything that is sanctioned by law. All who ask, bring something with them." Look for more testimonies of this kind in the catalogue of witnesses to the truth, who before our age protested against the Roman pontiff and the errors of Papism.

units.la: De tyrannide autem Romanorum consule historiam Indicam & similes. Acosta lib. 2. cap. 4. de procuranda Indorum salute. Quis non videt, inquit, quàm implacabile Christiani nominis odium apud barbaros excitetur: tur; quàm grave & immedicabile scandalum: tota res ista vergit in obstinatam quandam invidam & odium fidei, & certam perniciem hominum: Christus, quod non debet, tributum solvit, ne scandalizet: nos nullo modo debitas terras si spoliemus, vexemus, prædemur, nullum ne justum timebimus scandalū? res ipsa satis clamat per se; omnino verum est, quod Gregorius scribit: qui fidem asperitatibus propagari volunt, suas non Dei causas probantur attendere. Justus Lipsius lib.2.de constant.cap.22.de inaudita Romana feritate hæc habet, Pauculi Iberi ante annos 8o in vastas illas & novas terras delati, quæ funera (Deus bone) ediderunt: quas strages: nec de causis aut de jure belli dissero, tantùm de eventis. cerno ingens illud terrarum spatium (quod vidisse magnū sit, non dicam vicisse) à vicenis tricenisque militibus pervadi, & passim inermes illos greges sterni, ut segetem à falce. Ubi tu es insularum maxima Cuba? tu Haijtę? [?] tu Jucajæ?
units.tr: On the tyranny of the Romanists consult the history of the Indies and similar works. Acosta, book 2, ch. 4, On Procuring the Salvation of the Indians: "Who does not see," he says, "how implacable the hatred of the Christian name becomes among the barbarians, how grave and incurable a scandal this is? The whole affair tends toward a certain obstinate, envious hatred and detestation of the faith, and to the certain ruin of men. Christ paid tribute which he did not owe, lest he give offence. Shall we, then, plunder, harass and pillage lands that are in no way owed to us, and fear no scandal, not even a just one? The thing itself cries out enough. It is entirely true what Gregory writes: those who want the faith spread by harshness show that they are seeking not God's cause but their own." Justus Lipsius, On Constancy, book 2, ch. 22, on the unheard-of Roman savagery: "A few Spaniards, some eighty years ago, were carried into those vast and new lands. What deaths (good God) they caused, what slaughters! I am not speaking here of causes or of the right of war, only of events. I see that immense expanse of lands (it would be a great thing to have seen it, let alone conquered it) overrun by twenty or thirty soldiers, and those unarmed flocks laid low everywhere, like corn before the sickle. Where are you, greatest of islands, Cuba? You, Haiti? You, Jucaja?"

units.la: { } Left-margin notes on this page are cropped; fragments visible only. quæ olim quingentis aut sexcentis hominum millibus succinctæ, alibi vix quindecim ex iis retinuistis in semen. Ostende etiam te paululum tu Pervana, tu Mexicana ora. heu miram miseramque faciem! immensus ille tractus, & verè alter orbis vastus attritusque apparet, non aliter, quàm si cœlesti quodam igne conflagrasset. Franciscus de victoria relecta.
units.tr: Once girded by five or six hundred thousand men, you have scarcely kept fifteen of them elsewhere as seed. Show yourself a little too, you Peruvian and Mexican coast! Alas, what a strange and wretched sight! That immense tract, truly another world, appears wasted and ground down, as if it had been burned by some heavenly fire. Francisco de Victoria, relection.

units.la: ¶[?] Quum audiamus, apud Indos tot dominos, possessionibus, & ditionibus suis privatos: dubitari merito potest, jure an injuria hæc facta sint; timeo, ne ultra res progressa est, quàm jus fasque permittebat.
units.tr: When we hear that among the Indians so many lords have been deprived of their possessions and dominions, it may fairly be doubted whether this was done justly or unjustly. I fear the matter has gone further than law and right allowed. ## REFUTATION OF THE PAPISTS' ARGUMENTS.

units.la: REFUTATIO ARGU-MENTORUM PONTIFI-CIORUM.
PLerasque pontificiorum argu-mentationes attigimus in Medulla papismi, locis de ecclesia, & pontifice Romano: Itaque sufficit, si pro ratione instituti nostri paucula hic annotemus.
units.tr: We have touched on most of the Papists' arguments in the Medulla papismi, under the topics concerning the Church and the Roman pontiff. So, given the purpose of our work, it is enough to note a few points here.

units.la: Ajunt; Querelas Elia, Esaia, et similes pertinere ad synagogam Judæorum. Resp. At non immerito æque nunc de ecclesia Romana usurpari possunt.² Nullam unquam ecclesiam in toto terrarum orbe viguisse, quæ fide et charitate floruerit magis, quàm Romana: adeo ut apostolus in hæc verba erumpat Rom. 1. 8. Gratias ago Deo meo per Jesum Christum, super omnibus vobis, quod fides vestra annunciatur in toto mundo. Resp. Equidem, si ad tempora apostolorum respiciamus, ecclesia romana multis virtute præluxit: de eâ autem, quæ nunc est, merito dicitur illud Esaiæ 1. 21. quomodo facta est meretrix, civitas fidelis.³ Etiam post apostolorum tempora ecclesiam Romanam officii et honoris sui fuisse memorem, non tantum conservando fideliter veram fidem adversus hæreticos; verum etiam illam piâ vitâ atq; etiam suo sanguine obsignando: ac proinde venerandæ antiquitatis consensu semper obtinuisse laudem civitatis fidelis, vineæ Domini, domus Dei viventis, columnæ veritatis. &c. Resp. Lubenter & ultro antiquæ illi Romanæ istam laudem deserimus: at in ea, qualis nunc est, veteris illius fidem videmus hominum commentis, & charitatem omnis generis crudelitate permutatam: ita ut non amplius civitas fidelis, sed perfida: non vinea Domini, sed sodom: non domus Christi, sed Satanæ; non columna veritatis, sed schola errorum dici mereatur. * Deum ecclesiam suam nunquam repudii libello penitus abjecisse: Ergo neque Romanam. Resp. Equidem sicuti temporibus Eliæ, præter Eliæ opinionem septem millia hominum supererat, qui genua sua non incurvarant Baali; ita Deus etiam in papatu cōplures sibi servavit, atque etiam nunc dubio procul servat, qui aut omnino bona conscientia Deum colunt, aut, licet cum infirmitate aliqua, tamen fundamentum retinent, & tandem pontificis idololatriam ac traditiones ex animo aversantur. deinde, licet Deus ecclesiam suam nunquam repudii libello penitus abjiciat, tamen nullus ecclesiæ militatis status adeo firmus & stabilis est,
units.tr: They say that the complaints of Elijah, Isaiah and similar prophets pertain to the synagogue of the Jews. Reply: With no less justice these can now be applied to the Roman Church. No Church in the whole world has ever flourished more in faith and charity than the Roman, so much so that the apostle breaks out in these words, Rom. 1.8: "I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, because your faith is proclaimed throughout the whole world." Reply: Indeed, if we look to the times of the apostles, the Roman church shone forth in many virtues. But of the church as it now is, rightly is said that saying of Isaiah 1.21: "How the faithful city has become a harlot!" Even after the time of the apostles, the Roman church remained mindful of its duty and honour, not only by faithfully preserving the true faith against heretics, but also by sealing it with a godly life and even with its own blood; and therefore, by the consensus of venerable antiquity, it has always obtained the praise of the faithful city, the vineyard of the Lord, the house of the living God, the pillar of truth. etc. Reply: Gladly and readily we surrender that praise to the ancient Roman church. But in the church as it now is we see that old faith replaced by men's inventions, and charity replaced by cruelty of every kind. So it deserves to be called not the faithful city but the faithless, not the vineyard of the Lord but Sodom, not the house of Christ but of Satan, not the pillar of truth but a school of errors. God has never utterly cast off his church with a bill of divorce; therefore neither has he cast off the Roman. Reply: Indeed, just as in the time of Elijah, besides Elijah's supposition, there remained seven thousand men who had not bowed their knees to Baal, so God has also preserved for himself many in the papacy, and without doubt preserves them even now, who either worship God with a good conscience or, though with some weakness, nonetheless hold to the foundation, and at last from the heart abhor the pope's idolatry and traditions. Next, although God never casts off his church with a bill of divorce, no state of the militant church is so firm and stable

units.la: quin mutari possit: teste ecclesia Judaica; item Asiaticis & similibus. qua de re vide locum de ecclesia, in Medulla nostra pag. 349. & sequent. {5}Esa. 54.1. & alibi diserte satis promitti, unamquamq; ecclesiam, tanquam matrem, Deo filios parere. R. At teste Christo Matth. 13.24.25. inimicus hominis bonum semen in agro suo serentis zizania serit inter triticum; atque inde fit, ut, quae Deo filios parere deberet, efficiatur meretrix: vide Esai. 1. 21. & Ezech. 16.15. Gal. 1.6. 2. Cor. 11.3. apoc. 2. & 3. & similia loca. In epist. Judae v. 18.19. damnari irrisores illos, qui seipsos segregent; & diserte dici illos futuros in extremo tempore. Idq; revera cōpetere protestatib. [?] Ref. Utrū protestantes orthodoxi sint isti irrisores; an vero Romanenses pōtificii? judicetur secundum scripturas S.ex confessionibus & vitā ipsorum.
units.tr: that it cannot be changed: witness the Jewish church, and likewise the Asiatic churches and similar ones. On this matter see the locus on the church in our Medulla, p. 349 and following. Isa. 54.1, and elsewhere, promises quite plainly enough that each church, as a mother, bears sons to God. Reply: But as Christ witnesses in Matt. 13.24–25, the enemy of the man who sows good seed in his field sows tares among the wheat; and from this it comes about that she who ought to bear sons to God becomes a harlot. See Isa. 1.21, Ezek. 16.15, Gal. 1.6, 2 Cor. 11.3, Rev. 2 and 3, and similar passages. In the epistle of Jude, vv. 18–19, those scoffers who separate themselves are condemned, and it is plainly said that they will come in the last time; and this truly applies to the Protestants. Reply: Let it be judged, according to the Scriptures and from their confessions and life, whether the orthodox Protestants are those scoffers or rather the Roman papists.

units.la: {6}Praeterea dicunt, apud protestantes virtutis laudem promereri, si nihil non in ecclesia Romanā, templis, monasteriis, dogmatibus, ritibus, omnium denique ordi-num hominibus reprehendant, desideret; carpant &c.Illud autem esse alienum à vera pietatis ac modestiæ studio. Resp. Equidem optimo iure ac necessario fit; idq; ad exemplum prophetarum, apostolorum, & Christi ipsius, quos costat admodum multa in sui temporis idololatriæ ac hypocritis reprehendisse. consule Esaiam cap. [?] & reliquos scripturæ libros. Præterea, an vitio vertes medico, si multos in ægroto deprehendat morbos ac pravos humores, forte ex intemperantia & aliunde contractos? equidem rectius feceris, si potius ægroti culpam agnoscas. 7 Protestantes studere hac ratione palliare vel tegere sua latrocinia, atq; omnis generis sacrilegia; puta templorum direptiones, sacerdotum cædes &c. Resp. Equidem solent pontificii cum in modum nostris doctoribus imputare, si quæ uspiam à militari licentia patrantur; sed impium est, quæ milites vel miscellanea turba in æstubelli faciût, sic exprobrare, ut per eorum latera quasi confodiatur religio, quâ ecclesiæ vel principes fideles profitentur. deinde videbis apud Paulum Iovium & alios, quàm flagitiosè & barbarè sese gesserint sæpius exercitus Itali, Hispani, & alii. equidem diserte profitetur Jo-vius Romam protestantes vidisse multò humaniores quàm Hispanos & Italos, sub Carolo V. Germanus, inquit, à primo impetu, quo armatos deleverat, à gladiis temperabat; usque adeo remissâ animi ferociâ, ut exiguo facilè precio libertatem captivis daret, ac præsentibus tantùm spoliis & compotationi-bus lætaretur; verteretque demum furorem in templa & antiqui operis statuas, deformando cun-cta atque vastando, quòd plærique eorum, irrisis pontificum legibus, Lutherana dogmata sequerentur. Hispani autem astutâ & implacabi-li crudelitate acerbiores, ut abdita arcanaque familiarium irruerent, tormentis atque suppliciis in nobi-lisima corpora grassabantur: tantâ auri cupiditate, ut Julii pontificis cadaver, multâ exesum carie, erue-re, & anulo spoliare non dubitarint.
units.tr: {6}Besides, they say that among the Protestants one earns praise for virtue if one finds fault with almost everything in the Roman Church (temples, monasteries, dogmas, rites, and finally men of every rank), and carps at them; and that this is foreign to the true zeal of piety and modesty. Reply: Indeed, this is done with the best right and of necessity, and after the example of the prophets, the apostles and Christ himself, who plainly rebuked very many things of idolatry and hypocrisy in their own times. Consult Isaiah, chapter [?], and the remaining books of Scripture. Moreover, would you blame a physician who finds many diseases and bad humours in a sick man, perhaps contracted from intemperance and other causes? Surely you would do better to acknowledge the patient's fault. 7 The Protestants strive by this method to cover or hide their robberies and every kind of sacrilege, namely the plundering of temples, the murders of priests, and so on. Reply: The Papists are accustomed to impute such things to our teachers in the same way, if anything is committed anywhere by military licence. But it is impious to reproach in this way what soldiers or a mixed crowd do in the heat of war, as if religion, which the faithful churches or princes profess, were stabbed through their sides. Moreover, you will see in Paolo Giovio and others how shamefully and barbarously the Italian, Spanish and other armies have often behaved. Giovio plainly states that under Charles V he saw the Protestants to be much more humane than the Spaniards and Italians. "The German," he says, "from the first onset, by which he had destroyed the armed, refrained from the sword, so far was his fierceness of spirit relaxed that he would readily give liberty to captives for a small price, and rejoiced only in the spoils at hand and in drinking bouts; and at last he turned his fury against the temples and the statues of ancient work, defacing and wrecking everything, because most of them, mocking the laws of the pontiffs, followed Lutheran doctrines." The Spaniards, however, sharper in their cunning and implacable cruelty, broke into the hidden and secret places of the household and raged with torments and punishments against most noble bodies, with such greed for gold that they did not hesitate to dig up the corpse of Pope Julius, eaten away by much decay, and to strip it of its ring.

units.la: Sed ejus etiam gentis facinora Itali Brutiique praesertim, decerptis vi-tiis, nec ullis omnino admissis virtutibus, facile adaequabant. vide Jovium in vita Pompeii. Columna Cardina-lis. Similia leguntur de Latinis, apud Antonium histor. part. 3. tit. 19. cap. 2. §. 3. & alios; quàm flagitiosè sese gesserint, capta Constantinopoli; sub Innocetio III. Non sufficiebat, inquit, eis, imperiales ex haurire di-vitias, ac majorum diripere spolia pariter & minorum, nisi ad ecclesiarum thesauros extenderent manus, tabulas argenteas de altaribus depo-nentes, & violatis sacrariis, cruces, iconas, & reliqua ecclesiarum ornamenta rapiebant. 8 Impium esse ab ecclesia catholica deficere? R. esp. Pium vero & necessarium secedere a synagoga pontificia Romana: & quid;o-vibus nelitem intendes, si a lupis se segregent? consule Matt. 7. & similia scripturae loca. 9 Illos merito cen-seri haereticos, vel schismaticos, apostatas; adeoq; paenis ecclesiasticis ac politicis omni jure subjectos esse. R. esp. Ita quidem decerdecernere placet curiæ Romanæ; at longè aliter judicat Christus & scriptura sacra: neutiquam enim defecimus à Christo ad antichristum, quales describuntur 1. Cor. 11.19 Tit. 3.10.11. 1.Tim. 4.1. & alibi. sed discessimus à societate pontificum, qui solo ecclesiæ titulo gaudent atque infirmioribus imponūt; discessimus inquam, justis & necessariis de causis, idque ad Dei gloriam & nostram aliorúmque hominum salutem æternam. 10 Protestantium cœtus ex Christi auctoritate à Romano pontifice excommunicari. resp. Neutiquam ex auctoritate Christi; sed pro libitu pōtificis & cleri Romani. An nō? Tolet. de instruct. sacerd. lib. 1. cap. 10. Nullam injustam excommunicationis sententiam, nec quo ad Deum, nec quo ad ecclesiam ligare. Itē Rubrica can. 24. quæst. 3. capitulo Coperimus. Qui illicitè alium excommunicat, sē ipsum, non alium condemnat.
units.tr: But the Italians and especially the Bruttians, having plucked away the vices and admitting no virtues at all, could easily match the crimes of that nation. See Giovio in the life of Pompey; the Column of the Cardinal. Similar things are read about the Latins in Antonio, Historia, part 3, title 19, chapter 2, §3, and elsewhere: how shamefully they behaved when Constantinople was taken, under Innocent III. "It was not enough for them," he says, "to draw off the imperial riches and to plunder the spoils of the greater and lesser alike, unless they also extended their hands to the treasuries of the churches, taking down silver tablets from the altars, and, the sanctuaries having been violated, they seized crosses, icons and the remaining ornaments of the churches." 8 Is it impious to fall away from the Catholic Church? Reply: Rather it is pious and necessary to secede from the Roman papal synagogue. And what harm is there in sheep keeping away from wolves? Consult Matt. 7 and similar passages of Scripture. 9 Those are rightly judged heretics, or schismatics, or apostates, and therefore subject to ecclesiastical and civil penalties by every right. Reply: It may please the Roman court so to decree; but Christ and holy Scripture judge quite differently. For we have not fallen away from Christ to Antichrist, such as are described in 1 Cor. 11.19, Titus 3.10–11, 1 Tim. 4.1, and elsewhere. Rather we have departed from the fellowship of the pontiffs, who enjoy only the title of the church and impose upon the weaker; we have departed, I say, for just and necessary causes, and that for the glory of God and for our own and other men's eternal salvation. 10 The assemblies of the Protestants are excommunicated by the Roman pontiff by the authority of Christ. Reply: By no means by the authority of Christ, but at the pleasure of the pontiff and the Roman clergy. Is this not so? See Toletus, De instructione sacerdotum, book 1, chapter 10: "No unjust sentence of excommunication binds, either before God or before the Church." Likewise the rubric of canon 24, question 3, chapter Coperimus: "He who unlawfully excommunicates another condemns himself, not the other."

units.la: 11 Schismaticum atq; impium esse, se-parari à Romano pontifice. resp. Impium est separari à Christo capite: nos discessimus autem à pontifice, ut communicemus cum Christo.
units.tr: 11 It is schismatic and impious to separate from the Roman pontiff. Reply: It is impious to be separated from Christ the head. We have indeed departed from the pontiff so that we may communicate with Christ.

units.la: Neminem Christo subesse, qui non subest pontifici Romano. Resp. Ita, si sufficeret assertio Iesuitica: at contrarium demonstravimus in loco de pontifice & ecclesia Romana.
units.tr: No one is subject to Christ who is not subject to the Roman pontiff. Reply: Yes, if the Jesuit assertion were enough. But we have shown the contrary in the place on the pontiff and the Roman Church.

units.la: Extra ecclesiam Romanam nullam esse salutem. Resp. Certè extra eam servati sunt & servabuntur innumeri: deinde Romana illa, de qua quæritur, non est Christi ecclesia.
units.tr: Outside the Roman Church there is no salvation. Reply: Certainly innumerable people have been saved outside it, and will be saved. Further, that Roman Church under discussion is not the Church of Christ.

units.la: Languere quidem eam leviculâ infirmitate; at neutiquam propterea licere piis ab eâ deficere. Resp. Ostendimus antea, eam laborare pestiferarum hæresiū gangrænâ, & factam esse antichristi sedem.
units.tr: It is true that she is weakened by a slight infirmity, but by no means is it therefore lawful for the godly to fall away from her. Reply: We have shown earlier that she labours under the gangrene of pestilential heresies, and has become the seat of Antichrist.

units.la: Nihil aliud studere Romanenses, quàm ut omnes & singuli ad Christi agnitionem rite deducantur. Resp. Imò verò, ut inter Christum & sua merita salutis laudem dividant: quâ de re vide plura suis locis, interea respondeat jurecôsultus ille, si dividas, perdes.
units.tr: The Romanists strive for nothing else than that all and each be duly led to the knowledge of Christ. Reply: Rather, they aim to share the praise of salvation between Christ and their own merits. On this matter see more in the proper places. Meanwhile let that lawyer answer for himself: if you divide, you will lose.

units.la: Non licere illico ob vitia, si qua sint, discedere, sed legitimè cogitandum esse de rep de reformatione vel generali vel particulari. R. At pōtifices neq; capitis neq; membrorum reformatione ferre volūt. hincille synodū Basiliensem ex verbis revocavit, & armis dissipavit. vide appendicem concilii Basiliensis, ejus literas revocatorias, item Platinam de vitis pontificum in Eugenio 4. & similes. neque sanè hodie quemquam latere potest, quàm illegitimè & præposterè concilia à pontificum factione hisce posterio-ribus seculis indicta & habita sint; quantoquè studio Romani in hoc unum incumbunt, ut concilii efficto nomine suam idololatriam, dominationem, & tyrannidem stabiliant.
units.tr: It is not lawful to depart at once on account of faults, if there are any, but one must think lawfully about reformation, either general or particular. Reply: But the pontiffs will bear reformation neither of the head nor of the members. Hence that pontiff revoked the Council of Basel in words, and scattered it by arms. See the appendix to the Council of Basel, its letters of revocation, likewise Platina on the lives of the popes under Eugenius IV, and similar works. Indeed, no one today can be unaware how illegitimately and preposterously councils have been summoned and held in these latter centuries by the faction of the pontiffs, and with how much zeal the Romanists labour at this one thing: that under the false name of a council they may establish their idolatry, domination and tyranny.

units.la: 17 In concilio Tridetino generali omnibus piis hac in parte abunde satisfactum esse, & generalem ecclesiæ reformationem instituta. R. esp. Quid de concilio Tridentino sit statuendum, quodque illud Tridentinum, cæteraq; pontificum Romanorum auctoritate indicta concilia nullo, nec divino, nec humano iure piis comprobata sint, multis apertis & firmissimis rationibus doctores orthodoxi, ipsiq́ue adeò principes christiani abūde de-monstrarunt. Sed esto, quòd cōplu-ra ibi decreta sint de reformatione: audi Hervedum papistam lib. de re-parandá ecclesiastica disciplina, quí tres malorum labes perstringit, quas antiquas renovent corruptelas: prima est, quòd quae rectè fuerint decreta, nequaquam servantur; altera quòd tametsi serventur, non sint ejusmodi, quae restituant priscos mores in integrum: tertia quòd etiam parum prosint; quia pontifex Romanus & solvitur ipse legibus & quoslibet solvit; videlicet hac clausula omnibus decretis annexâ; salvâ semper auctoritate sedis apostolicæ: vides ergo Romanæ ecclesiæ valc-tudinem non tantùm afflictam, sed prorsus deploratam esse: plura de-concilio Tridentino videbis infra.
units.tr: 17 In the general Council of Trent, all the godly have been abundantly satisfied on this point, and a general reformation of the Church has been instituted. Reply: What is to be decided about the Council of Trent, and that the Tridentine council, and the other councils summoned by the authority of the Roman pontiffs, have been approved by the godly as valid by no right, divine or human, the orthodox teachers and the Christian princes themselves have abundantly demonstrated by many open and most firm arguments. But granting that many decrees on reformation were made there, hear the papist Hervedus in his book on restoring ecclesiastical discipline. He lists three blemishes of evils which renew the old corruptions: first, that what has been rightly decreed is in no way observed; second, that even if it is observed, such decrees are not of the kind that restore the earlier morals to their integrity; third, that they also do little good, because the Roman pontiff both releases himself from the laws and releases whomever he likes, namely by this clause attached to all decrees: "the authority of the apostolic see always saved." You see, therefore, that the health of the Roman Church is not merely afflicted but utterly despaired of. You will see more about the Council of Trent below.

units.la: 18 Protestantes imitari Donatistas & similes, eorumq; perfido cum ecclesia catholica dissido communicare. Resp. Quàm rectè hoc nobis imputetur, judicet lex Dei: interea certi sumus, quòd ducti oraculis Spiritus s. jugum' pa-pæ tanquam alterius Pharaonis ex-cusserimus. 19 Complures etiam magnâ cum injuriâ magistratus ab ecclesiâ Romana decedere, testibus Galliâ, Bataviâ, & quibusdam locis Germaniæ. Resp. Si id alicubi contingat, obtemperandum est Deo potiùs, quàm hominibus: ad exemplum apostolorum act. s. 29. Plura vide suo loco, de jure ecclesiarum clandestinarum. 20 Non decere pios, præsertim homines plebejos, sibi vendicare auctoritatem judicandi doctrinâ; sed rectiùs sese antistitum ordinariorum judicio subjicere. Resp. Hoc nihil aliud est, quàm velle promiscuè dominari in gregem Domini, & hominibus oculos eruere. 21 Merito omnes simpliciter acquiescere ecclesiæ judicio: quia ex divinis scripturis constet, eam neque falli neque fallere posse. Resp. Suo loco autem demonstravimus omnes & singulas visibiles ecclesias errare posse; idque ex s. literis, omniùmque temporum historiâ, & crebrâ experientiâ constat; ac proinde non ex ecclesiâ veritas, sed ex veritate ecclesia dignosci de-bet. 22 Nulli ex protestantibus certò con-stare posse, professionem suam esse funda-mentum in s. literis. Resp. Examinetur ea ad canonem scripturæ propheticæ & apostolicæ; & abunde constabit, penes quos sit veritas. 23 Ecclesiam Romanam eandem fidem constanter reti-nere, idem dicere, et ne in minimo quidem religionis negocio discrepare. Resp. Ita, si sufficit gloriari: quàm verò alienum id sit à vero, complures ex orthodoxis auctoribus demonstrarunt: nobis sufficiant pauca exempla, quæ neque ipse Bellarminus rejicit. Ita consilium Basiliense, Parisiensium Sorbona, & complures ex pontificiis doctoribus statuunt, concilium esse supra papam: contradicunt. alii vide Bellarm. lib. 2. cap. 11. & 14.
