Similiter quidam statuunt concilia generalia non posse errare; papam verò posse, atque etiam sæpius errasse: contrarium docent alii. vide Bellarm. ibid. Similes contradictiones exstant de peccato concupiscentiæ; teste Bellarmino de amissione gratiæ lib. 5. cap. 15. de libero arbi-trio, apud eundem lib. 3. cap. 7. de justificatione; teste eodem libr. 2. cap. 1. & similibus doctrinæ capitibus. 24 Antecessores & patres nostros non ita decessisse ab ecclesia Romana, sed eam tanquam communem matrem coluisse. Resp. Quæstio est de jure: deinde licet olim plurimi inebriati fuerint poculo meretricis Romanæ, tamen excitavit Deus subinde, qui idolatriæ pontificiæ contradixerunt: sicut testatur historia martyrum, & similes.
units.tr: 18 That Protestants imitate the Donatists and the like, and, by their faithless dissent, communicate with the Catholic Church. Reply: Let the law of God judge how rightly this is imputed to us. Meanwhile we are certain that, led by the oracles of the Holy Spirit, we have shaken off the yoke of the pope, as of another Pharaoh. 19 Many also, with great injury to the magistrates, depart from the Roman Church, as witnessed by France, Batavia and certain places in Germany. Reply: If this happens anywhere, one must obey God rather than men, after the example of the apostles, Acts 5:29. See more in its place, on the right of the secret churches. 20 It is not fitting for the godly, especially common people, to claim for themselves the authority of judging doctrine, but they should rather submit themselves to the judgment of the ordinary bishops. Reply: This is nothing other than wishing to lord it indiscriminately over the flock of the Lord and to gouge out men's eyes. 21 All should rightly simply acquiesce in the judgment of the Church, because it is established from the divine Scriptures that she can neither err nor deceive. Reply: In its place we have shown that all and each visible church can err. This is established from the holy writings, from the history of all times, and from constant experience. Therefore truth should be recognised not from the Church, but the Church from the truth. 22 It cannot be certainly established for any of the Protestants that their profession is founded on the holy writings. Reply: Let it be examined by the canon of prophetic and apostolic Scripture, and it will abundantly be clear with whom the truth lies. 23 The Roman Church constantly retains the same faith, says the same thing, and does not differ even in the smallest matter of religion. Reply: Yes, if boasting is enough. But how far that is from the truth, several orthodox authors have demonstrated. A few examples will suffice, which not even Bellarmine himself rejects. Thus the Council of Basel, the Sorbonne of Paris, and several papist teachers hold that a council is above the pope; others contradict them. See Bellarmine, book 2, chapters 11 and 14. Similarly, some hold that general councils cannot err but the pope can, and indeed has often erred; others teach the contrary. See Bellarmine, ibid. Similar contradictions exist concerning the sin of concupiscence, as Bellarmine witnesses in his book on the loss of grace, book 5, chapter 15; on free will, in book 3, chapter 7 of the same work, on justification; and, as the same author witnesses, in book 2, chapter 1, and in similar heads of doctrine. 24 Our forefathers and fathers did not so depart from the Roman Church, but cherished her as a common mother. Reply: The question concerns right. Further, although in former times very many were made drunk with the cup of the Roman harlot, yet God from time to time raised up men who spoke against papal idolatry, as the history of the martyrs testifies, and the like.

units.la: 25 Non decere pios ita discedere a moribus parentum, & antecessorum suorum. Resp. Equidem licet etiam perstringere & deplorare illorum peccata atque errores, ad exemplum Josuæ cap. 24. 14. Davidis Psal. 78. 19. & alibi. Daniel. cap. 9. atque adeo Christi ipsius & reliquorum sanctorum Dei servorum Matth. 23. 23. act. 7. 39. 1. Cor. 10. 5. deinde non dubitamus, Deum semper complures servasse in medio papatu, qui, vel etiam in extremo vitæ discrimine, rejecta traditionum pontificiarum fiducia, ad fosolius Christi meritum confugerut.
units.tr: 25 It is not fitting for the godly to depart thus from the customs of their parents and forefathers. Reply: Indeed, it is also permitted to expose and lament their sins and errors, after the example of Joshua cap. 24. 14, of David, Psalm 78. 19, and elsewhere; Daniel cap. 9; and indeed of Christ himself and the other holy servants of God, Matth. 23. 23; Acts 7. 39; 1 Cor. 10. 5. Further, we do not doubt that God has always preserved many in the midst of papacy who, even at the extreme peril of life, rejecting confidence in the pontifical traditions, have fled to the sole merit of Christ.

units.la: 26 Revera protestantes in majores suos esse summe injurios. Resp. Neutiquam sunt: sed eos qui Dei beneficio ab idololatria Romana fuerunt immunes, justa laude ornamus: reliquorum vero lapsus deceter agnoscimus ac deploramus: eorum etiam qui fundamentu mediocriter retinuerunt, salutem speramus: etenim in papatu, perditis doctoribus, discipuli sæpe sunt dubio procul servati, cum simplici integritate Deo servientes.
units.tr: 26 Indeed, Protestants are highly injurious to their elders. Reply: By no means. We commend with just praise those who by God's benefit were free from Roman idolatry. The lapses of the others we rightly acknowledge and lament. For those who have kept the foundation, though imperfectly, we hope for salvation; for in the papacy, with the teachers lost, disciples have doubtless often been preserved, serving God with simple integrity.

units.la: 27 Manifestò impios esse qui discedunt ab ecclesia Christi. Resp. Non vero qui discedunt ab ecclesia Romana pontificia.
units.tr: 27 Clearly those are impious who depart from the Church of Christ. Reply: But not those who depart from the Roman pontifical church.

units.la: 28 Romanam illam esse ecclesiam Christi. Resp: Quòd verae ecclesiae Christi nomen haud mereatur, dictum est antea, & prolixè demonstravimus suo loco. Gloriantur quidem Romanenses ecclesiae titulo, sed non sufficit gloriari, nam non est infrequens haereticis & apertis ecclesiae hostibus, quòd ecclesiae filios & alumnos se dici & habere voluerint. Ita Cyprianus de Novatiano scribit epist. 73. Novatianum simia-rum more, quæ quum homines nō sint, homines tamen imitatur, velle ecclesiæ catholicæ auctoritatem sibi & veritatem vendicare, quum tamen ipse in ecclesia non fuerit, imò adhuc insuper contra ecclesiam rebellis & hostis exstiterit. & Tertullianus lib. 4. contra Marcionem dicit, Marcionitas facere fa-vos, & vespas; facere item ecclesias. Ergo non sufficit Romanensium gloriatio, sed necessum est, rationes atq; argumenta eorū expendamus.
units.tr: 28 That Roman Church is the Church of Christ. Reply: That it does not deserve the name of the true Church of Christ has been said before, and we have demonstrated it at length in its place. The Romanists indeed glory in the title of Church, but boasting is not enough. It is not uncommon for heretics and open enemies of the Church to wish to be called, and to be held as, sons and nurslings of the Church. Thus Cyprian writes of Novatian in letter 73: Novatian, like apes, which though not men nevertheless imitate men, wished to claim for himself the authority and truth of the Catholic Church, though he himself had never been in the Church, and indeed had further stood as a rebel and enemy against the Church. And Tertullian, in book 4 against Marcion, says that the Marcionites make honeycombs and wasps, and likewise make churches. Therefore the Romanists' boasting is not enough; it is necessary that we weigh their reasons and arguments.

units.la: 29 Protestantes revera fraternam chari-tatem abrupisse [?]. Resp. Quia Romanenses fidem abnegaverint, non possumus neque debemus cum illis fraternam colere charitatem, quātum ad communionem ecclesiasticam: quia charitas ex fide pendet. interea autem non subducimus illis dilectionem christianam, & precamur illis meliorem mentem.
units.tr: 29 The Protestants have in truth broken fraternal charity [?]. Answer: Because the Romanists have renounced the faith, we cannot and must not cultivate fraternal charity with them so far as ecclesiastical communion is concerned, since charity depends on faith. Meanwhile, we do not withdraw Christian love from them, and we pray that they may have a better mind.

units.la: 30 Protestantes discessisse non publicâ, sed privatâ auctoritate [?]. Resp. Omnes & singuli tenetur ex mandato Dei, ut propriam salutem curent, licet alii nolint veritati assentiri: deinde neque deest auctoritas publica ec-clesiis nostris, quando in eis etiam magistratus & principes versantur.
units.tr: 30 The Protestants separated not by public but by private authority [?]. Answer: Every single person is bound by God's command to look after his own salvation, even if others refuse to assent to the truth. Moreover, our churches do not lack public authority, since magistrates and princes are also present in them.

units.la: 31 Non esse unius aut alterius reipub. neque unius aut alterius principis, hoc facere: sed prius exspectandum esse communem totius orbis consensum. R csp. Deus & cuique magistratui, & cuique principi mandavit, ut sint summo studio soliciti de illorum salute, quos vident suae fidei esse commissos: & quid; an diutius exspectandum censes? equidem omnes sana mente praediti vident, quod satis diu passi sint principes & populus christianus sibi obtrudi vi & fraude varias consuetudines & novationes à Romano pontifice & ejus juratis, cardinalibus, episcopis, & reliquis sacrificulis: ea itaq; nunc tandem aliquando sine deliberatione sunt ejiciendae. etenim deliberatio non habet locum in rebus simpliciter & certo mandatis à Deo, neque in turpibus.
units.tr: 31 It is not for one commonwealth or another, nor for one prince or another, to do this; rather, the common consent of the whole world must first be awaited. Answer: God has commanded every magistrate and every prince, and indeed everyone, to take the greatest care for the salvation of those whom they see have been committed to their faith. And what? Do you think we should wait any longer? Indeed, all people of sound mind see that princes and the Christian people have suffered long enough the various customs and innovations forced upon them by violence and fraud by the Roman pontiff and his sworn men: cardinals, bishops, and the other sacrificing priests. Therefore these things must now at last be cast out without deliberation, for deliberation has no place in matters that are plainly and certainly commanded by God, nor in shameful ones.

units.la: DE JURE ECCLESIARUM clandestinarum, sub cruce; & tyrannide pontificis Romani.
units.tr: On the right of clandestine churches under the cross and under the tyranny of the Roman pontiff.

units.la: Quæritur an pii, qui sub magistratu pontificio latent, cœtus clandestinos, exercendæ veræ religionis nomine, contra illius edictum, bona conscientia, & citra rebellionis suspicionem instituere ac fovere queant? Resp. Pontificii Romani negant: Orthodoxi protestantes affirmant.
units.tr: The question is whether the godly who lie hidden under the papal magistracy may, in conscience and without suspicion of rebellion, set up and foster secret assemblies in the name of exercising the true religion, contrary to his edict? Answer: The Roman Papists deny; the orthodox Protestants affirm.

units.la: Ecclesiarum clandestinarum nomine intelligimus hoc loco cœtus hominum, voce verbi Dei ex reliquâ turbâ collectos, veram religionem observantes, sed latetes in medio luporum.
units.tr: By the name of clandestine churches we here mean assemblies of people, gathered out of the rest of the crowd by the voice of God's Word, who observe the true religion but lie hidden in the midst of wolves.

units.la: De earum veritate, antiquitate, sanctitate, & privilegiis nō est quòd quisquam jure dubitet.
units.tr: No one may rightly doubt their truth, antiquity, holiness, and privileges.

units.la: Nam auctorem habent communem cum omnibus ecclesiis publi-cis: Deum Patrem, Filium,& Spiritum sanctum, fontem bonorum omnium; eoque nomine verè in scripturis comparatur Deus modo gallinæ pullos suos foventi, modo pastori, oves suas amanti, & ubique locorum quærenti, modo patri, qui filiorum miserias doleat. Quod autè Deum auctorem & approbatorem habet, quis jure improbet aut damnet?
units.tr: For they have the same author as all public churches: God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the fountain of all good things. On this account Scripture truly compares God sometimes to a hen fostering her chicks, sometimes to a shepherd who loves his sheep and seeks them in every place, and sometimes to a father who grieves over the miseries of his children. Since they have God as their author and approver, who may rightly disapprove or condemn them?

units.la: Deinde quid quæso à verâ ecclesiâ Jesu Christi requires, quòd in hisce minùs offendas? Vis veras ecclesiarum notas? iis non minùs, quàm publicæ sunt conspicuæ; videlicet, sincerâ verbi divini prædicatione, legitimâ sacramentorum administratione, & accuratâ ecclesiasticæ censuræ, juxta Dei verbum, observatione.
units.tr: Next, what, I ask, do you require of the true Church of Jesus Christ that you take offence at these less? Do you want the true marks of churches? They are no less conspicuous in these than in public churches, namely, the sincere preaching of the divine Word, the lawful administration of the sacraments, and the careful observance of ecclesiastical discipline according to the Word of God.

units.la: Cives habent homines liberatos à servitute Babylonicâ, qui esuriunt & sitiunt Christum: licet inter eos etiâ multi hypocritæ & falsi fratres latitent. Pri-
units.tr: They have as citizens people freed from Babylonian slavery, who hunger and thirst for Christ, although many hypocrites and false brethren also lurk among them. The first

units.la: Privilegiis gaudent, quæ omnibꝰ sanctis sunt communia ; videlicet, liberatione à peccato, morte, maledictione & Satanâ: ut cętera omittā.
units.tr: They enjoy privileges that are common to all the saints: namely, deliverance from sin, death, the curse, and Satan, to omit the rest.

units.la: Præterea illarum ortum si inquiras ; reperies eas verè à Christi apostolis esse fundatas, atq; in hunc usque diem singulari Dei ꝓvidentiâ conservatas: consule annales, historias Græcas & Latinas : inspice veterū monumenta, ritus, cærimonias, quicquid demum aliquid antiquitatis refert: invenies, inde à passione Christi eas quovis tempore per oēs ætatum gradus exstitisse ; ut veteris populi conditionem omittam.
units.tr: Moreover, if you inquire into their origin, you will find that they were truly founded by the apostles of Christ and have been preserved to this day by the singular providence of God. Consult the annals and the Greek and Latin histories; inspect the ancient monuments, rites, and ceremonies, and whatever else refers to antiquity. You will find that from the passion of Christ onward they have existed at every time, through all the ages, not to mention the condition of the ancient people.

units.la: Si progressum: Illæ sub uno capite Jesu Christo, præter quod aliud excogitari nec potest nec debet, unam eandemque fidem constanter retinuerunt, & per Græciam, Italiâ, Germaniam, Galliam, Angliam, Hispaniam, imò per totum terrarum orbem, sunt diffusæ, ut ut tumultuetur Satan cum suis : ac proinde summo jure de ecclesiæ catholicæ nomine, æquè ac publicæ, gloriari possunt.
units.tr: If you proceed further: under the one head, Jesus Christ, besides whom no other can or should be devised, they have constantly retained one and the same faith. They have been spread through Greece, Italy, Germany, Gaul, England, Spain, and indeed through the whole world, however Satan may rage with his own. Therefore they may with the greatest right glory in the name of the catholic Church, just as the public churches do.

units.la: Hæc omnib. seculis verâ fide, martyriis, & sanctitate non simulatâ floruerunt: de hisce verè asserimus, quòd non inferendo regibus bella, nec invadêdo principum civitates, non occupando per vim alienas terras, non mortem minitâdo, non tormenta inferendo ecclesiam propagarunt: sed quòd obediendo, patiendo, supplicia, martyria mortem tolerando, sanguinem suum fundendo, sancta & stabilia ecclesiæ Christi initia, atque incrementa dederunt: neq; enim dubium est, quod ipsum quoq; experientia satis superq; testatur, quin plurimi in istis ecclesiis latètes alios à fide alienos cōverterint & convertât, partim piis colloquiis & concionib., partim cōfessione & martyrio, dum ad necem euangelii gratiâ correpti veritatem perspicuè & intrepidè confitentur, eandemq; sanguine suo constanter obsignant.
units.tr: These have flourished in every age by true faith, by martyrdoms, and by unfeigned holiness. Concerning them we truly assert that they did not spread the Church by waging war on kings, by invading the cities of princes, by seizing other lands by force, by threatening death, or by inflicting torments. Rather, by obeying, by suffering, by enduring punishments and martyrdoms and death, and by shedding their own blood, they gave the holy and steadfast beginnings and growth to the Church of Christ. For there is no doubt, as experience itself abundantly and more than sufficiently attests, that very many people in these churches, lying hidden, have converted and still convert others who were alien to the faith, partly by godly conversations and sermons, partly by confession and martyrdom, while, seized for the slaughter for the sake of the gospel, they confess the truth clearly and fearlessly and constantly seal it with their blood.

units.la: Hic meridianâ luce clariûs omni-bus bus conspicua fiūt[?] invictissima Dei contra hostium suorum furore tro-phæa; patiendo, videlicet hostes nostros affligi, moriendo prosterni, iacendo nos de omnibus triuphare.
units.tr: Here, more clearly than the midday light, there appear to all, conspicuous, the most unconquered trophies of God against the fury of his enemies. By suffering, namely, our enemies are afflicted; by dying, they are laid low; by lying low, we triumph over all things.

units.la: Hæc meritò, ut vivaria & seminaria ecclesiarum publicarum, venerabimur: veteres omittam, in hisce sunt educati nostro seculo eximii Dei servi & lumina Theologorum, Martyr, Beza, Tosfanus, Junius, Taffinus, Trelcatius, & alii complures.
units.tr: These, rightly, we shall revere as the nurseries and seminaries of the public churches. To omit the ancient ones: in our own age there have been educated in these churches outstanding servants of God and lights of the theologians, such as Martyr, Beza, Tossanus, Junius, Taffin, Trelcatius, and many others.

units.la: Miror itaq; ullum reperiri, qui de illorum sanctissimorum cætuū promotione vel tantillum dubitet, quasi verò in his hodie Dei ecclesiæ minùs liceret, quod apostolicæ, primitivæ, & omnium ætatum ac seculorum ecclesiis licuit.
units.tr: I therefore wonder that anyone should be found who doubts even a little the advancement of those most holy assemblies, as if in these days the Church of God were allowed less than what was permitted to the apostolic, primitive churches and the churches of all ages and centuries.

units.la: At reperiuntur tamen nonnulli, qui bonorum animis scrupulum in-jicere nō verentur, an cœtus illi clā-destini bonâ cōscientiâ foveri pos-sint? Sed quid? nónne ubi est cada-ver, illic congregabuntur aquilæ? nónne ubicunque fuerint fideles, quæcūq; sit ecclesiæ externa facies, cum Christo capite cohærent? adhærentes nimirū unico ejus verbo, sive dogmata sive vitam spectes: nū eorū cōmunionem contemnemus?
units.tr: Yet there are nonetheless some who do not hesitate to cast a scruple into the minds of good people, asking whether those secret assemblies can be fostered with a good conscience. But what? Where the carcass is, there the eagles will gather, will they not? Wherever the faithful are, whatever the outward appearance of the Church, do they not cling to Christ their head? Clinging, of course, to his one Word, whether you look at doctrine or at life, shall we despise their fellowship?

units.la: Absit ergo, ut de illis temere quippiam pronunciemus: de illis, inquā, qui reapse demonstrant, sibi Deum esse non ventrem, neque culinam religionem.
units.tr: Far be it, then, that we should rashly pronounce anything about them: about those, I say, who in very deed show that God is not their belly, nor their kitchen their religion.

units.la: Equidem non damnamus eos, qui tempore persequutionum, (dum legitima fugiēdi via & facultas datur) eo animo fugiunt, ut Deo vivant, utqúe Deum tentare, periculo nō necessario se exponendo, caveant, per fidem certiores facti, viam ad effugium sibi demōstrari à Domino; prati tamen veritatis hostibus resistere, quādo vocatio & hora defendendæ atque etiam per passionem obsignandæ veritatis aderit. gratulamur etiam ex animo illis ecclesiis, quæ publica verbi divini institutione fruuntur.
units.tr: Indeed we do not condemn those who, in a time of persecution, while a lawful way and opportunity of flight is given, flee with the intention of living to God, and who, being made more certain by faith, take care not to expose themselves needlessly to danger and not to tempt God, having been shown by the Lord a way of escape. Nevertheless, they will resist the enemies of the truth when the call and the hour of defending the truth, even to sealing it by suffering, is at hand. We also heartily congratulate those churches that enjoy the public institution of the divine Word.

units.la: Sed hoc vicissim petimus, ne quis temere illos fratres, qui sub cruce ingemiscunt, vel negligat vel condemnet sūt & in hisce ecclesiis(absit verbo invidia)viri repleti cœlesti doctrinâ & sapientiâ,qui nõ solùm se ipsos de via Domini erudiunt,sed alios quoq; monere & docere possunt: certè,qui aliquo studio pietatis ac divini cultus tanguntur, sanctos eorum conatus,quos in propagandâ Christi religione demõstrât, non solùm plurimi facient, sed in maximâ quoque voluptate & summis deliciis habebunt.
units.tr: But in turn we ask this: that no one rashly neglect or condemn those brethren who groan under the cross. For in these churches (let there be no envy in the word) there are men filled with heavenly doctrine and wisdom, who can not only instruct themselves in the way of the Lord but also admonish and teach others. Certainly those who are moved by some zeal for godliness and the worship of God will not only hold in high esteem the holy endeavours which these people display in propagating the religion of Christ, but will also take the greatest pleasure and delight in them.

units.la: Pergite itaque fratres & sorores, qui illic ingemiscitis, pgite[?], inquâ, ut cœpistis, & Christo feliciter vivite: Cogitate,quòd pro iustitiâ persecutionem patiamini,quodq; ita vos Deus peculiari mi'itiæ suæ notâ insignire velit : gaudete, apostolorum exemplo, quoties Deus vos reputabit dignos, qui pro suo nomine contumeliam patiamini. Cogitate ita oportere per multas afflictiones pios ingredi in regnum Dei: scitote vos Christi passionibus communicare: & fiet, ut quemadmodum ille ab omnium malorum labyrintho in gloriam cœlestem est ingressus, ita in eandem per varias tribulationes & vos deducamini. Esto, exuamini facultatibus, & ad inopiam apud homines redigamini; veræ vobis apud Deum in cœlis divitiæ accrescunt; extrudamini vestris sedibus, eo interius recipiemini in Dei familiam: contemnamini, eo firmiores agetis in Christo radices: notemini ignominiâ, eo ampliore loco eritis in regno Dei: trucidemini, ita vobis ingressus fit ad æternam salutem.
units.tr: Go on, therefore, brothers and sisters who groan there, go on, I say, as you have begun, and live happily to Christ. Think that you suffer persecution for righteousness' sake, and that God wishes to mark you with a special sign of his favour. Rejoice, after the example of the apostles, whenever God counts you worthy to suffer dishonour for his name. Remember that it is necessary for the godly to enter the kingdom of God through many afflictions. Know that you share in the sufferings of Christ, and it will come about that, just as he entered from the labyrinth of all evils into heavenly glory, so you too will be led into the same glory through various tribulations. Be it so: you are stripped of your possessions and reduced to poverty before men; true riches in heaven increase for you. You are thrust from your seats; you will be received more deeply into the family of God. You are despised; you will stand the firmer in Christ's roots. You are marked with disgrace; you will be in a more honourable place in the kingdom of God. You are slaughtered; thus an entrance into eternal salvation is made for you.

units.la: Assentiuntur patres : Augustinus tom. 8. in enarratione psal. 39. Noli, in-quit, numerare turbas hominum, incedentes per latas vias, implétes crastinum circum, civitatis natalé clamando celebrantes, civitatem ipsam male vivendo turbantes. Noli ergo illos attendere, multi sunt, & quis numeret, pauci autem per viam angustam; profer, inquam, stateram, appende: vide contra pau- ca grana, quantam paleam leves. Gregorius Nazianzenus, orat. prima de pa- ce: Melius est vitiosâ concordiâ dis- fidium veritatis causâ ortum. Gregorius Magnus comment. in lib. Reg. Ec- clesia est hæres crucis. Hilarius lib. con- tra Auxentium sub finem: Unum mo- neo, cavete antichristum: male e- nim vos parietum amor cepit, ma- lè ecclesiam Dei in tectis ædificiis- que veneramini, male sub his pacis nomen ingeritis. anne ambiguum est in his antichristum esse fesu- rum? motes mihi, & silvæ, & lacus, & carceres, & voragines sunt tutio- res. in his enim prophetæ, aut ma- nentes aut demersi, Dei spiritu pro- phetabant.
units.tr: The Fathers agree. Augustine, vol. 8, on Psalm 39 in his exposition: "Do not count the crowds of men walking along the broad roads, filling the circus tomorrow, celebrating the city's birthday with shouts, and disturbing the city itself by living badly. Do not pay attention to them. They are many, and who could count them? But the few walk the narrow way. Bring the balance, I say, and weigh: see how much chaff the few grains outweigh." Gregory of Nazianzus, first oration on peace: "It is better that discord arise for the sake of the truth than that there be a sinful concord." Gregory the Great, commentary on the Book of Kings: "The Church is the heir of the cross." Hilary, book against Auxentius, near the end: "I warn you of one thing: beware of Antichrist. For the love of walls has taken hold of you, and you wrongly revere the Church of God in roofed buildings, and you wrongly invoke the name of peace under them. Is there any doubt that Antichrist will be found in such places? Mountains, woods, lakes, prisons, and chasms are safer for me. For in these the prophets, whether remaining or sunk down, prophesied by the Spirit of God."

units.la: Subscribunt doctores pontificii. Acosta Jesuita de tempore novissimo lib. 1. c. 14. Bella quævis, ex quo homines esse cœperunt, nulla non ætas vidit; ta- men post tempora christiana maxi- me ormè orbem terrarum infestarunt, ut coactus sit Augustinus calumniis re-spondere eorum, qui istas calamita-tes legi Christianæ tribuebat, & re-vera regnorum conturbationes hæ-ἱρέσεων[?] furori successerunt, quum ta-men nihil accidit, quod non erat prædictum. En ergo interim nihil fieri, quod non modo sit prævisum, sed etiam, in genere saltem, prædictum. Ita de hæresibus oriturus & ecclesiam turbaturis imprimis in Pauli epistolis & in apocalypsi multa habentur. Bellarminus, de ecclesia lib. 4. c. 6. Ut aquæ diluvii arcam Nohæ attollebant, ita persecutiones ecclesiam illustrant: est enim persecutio ecclesiæ, inquit Iustinus, quod vineæ putatio, ut uberiores lætioresq; fruges reddat, &c, ut eleganter Tertullianus, sanguis martyrum est semen ecclesiæ. Pererius, comment. in Exod. disp. 5. Rubus ardens est figura ecclesiæ, inquit Hieronymus, quæ flammis persecutionum vexata, non consumitur, sed viret magis & splendescit.
units.tr: The Papist doctors subscribe to this. Acosta the Jesuit, On the Last Times, book 1, chapter 14: "Every age since men began to exist has seen wars of every kind, yet they have harassed the whole world most of all after the Christian times, so that Augustine was compelled to answer the slanders of those who attributed these calamities to the Christian law. And indeed these upheavals of kingdoms have followed upon the fury of heresies, although nothing has happened that was not foretold. Therefore, meanwhile, nothing happens that is not only foreseen but also, at least in general, foretold. Thus many things are found, especially in the Epistles of Paul and in the Apocalypse, about heresies that were going to arise and disturb the Church." Bellarmine, On the Church, book 4, chapter 6: "As the waters of the flood lifted up Noah's ark, so persecutions illustrate the Church. For the persecution of the Church, as Justin says, is like the pruning of a vine, which makes it yield richer and more abundant fruit, etc.; and as Tertullian elegantly puts it, the blood of the martyrs is the seed of the Church." Pererius, commentary on Exodus, disputation 5: "The burning bush is a figure of the Church," says Jerome, "which, troubled by the flames of persecution, is not consumed but flourishes all the more and shines."

units.la: Denique haud opus esse existimo, com-memorare exempla veterum piorum, qui sæpius in privatis ædibus sacros suos cœtus habuerunt. Ita 1.Reg.18.13. profitetur Hobadja, quòd, quùm occidisset Jezebel prophetas Domini, occultarit è prophetis Domini centum viros &c. Similiter Joh. 20. 19. & 26. dicuntur discipuli congregati fuisse, quum fores essent clausæ, propter metum Judæorum. videl. in privatis ædibus. Item act. 1. 13. 14. dicuntur ascendisse in cænaculum, posteaquam reversi essent Hierosolymam à monte Oliveti: atq; illic perdurasse concorditer in precibus & supplicationibus cum uxoribus, & Mariâ matre Jesu, & cum ipsius fratribus. act. 12. 12. legitur Petrus venisse domum Mariæ matris Johannis, ubi erant multi congregati & orantes. act. 15. docetur, quòd, quum Paulus & Barnabas, & reliqui eorum socii pervenissent Hierosolymam, congregati sint apostoli & presbyteri (equidem nō in templo, vel æde [?] publica, sed intra privatos parietes) similiter act.16.40. legitur, quod Paulus & Silas, postea quam e-gressi essent e carcere, introierint ad Lydiam, &, visis fratribus, consolati sint eos &c. Qui plura desideraverit, consulat locum de cruce, atq; afflictionibus ecclesiæ, & piorum.
units.tr: Indeed, I think there is no need to recall the examples of the godly of old, who very often held their sacred assemblies in private houses. Thus in 1 Kings 18:13, Obadiah testifies that when Jezebel had slain the prophets of the Lord, he hid a hundred men of the Lord's prophets, and so on. Similarly, in John 20:19 and 26, the disciples are said to have been gathered together, with the doors shut, for fear of the Jews; namely, in a private house. Likewise, Acts 1:13–14 says that they went up into the upper room after returning from the Mount of Olives to Jerusalem, and there they persevered together in prayers and supplications, with the women, and with Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren. Acts 12:12 reads that Peter came to the house of Mary, mother of John, where many were gathered and praying. Acts 15 teaches that when Paul and Barnabas and their other companions arrived at Jerusalem, the apostles and elders gathered together (certainly not in the temple or a public building, but within private walls). Similarly, Acts 16:40 reads that after Paul and Silas came out of prison, they went into Lydia's house, and, having seen the brethren, they comforted them, etc. Whoever desires more let him consult the passages concerning the cross and the afflictions of the Church and of the godly.

units.la: REFUTATIO OBJECTIONUM
units.tr: REFUTATION OF THE OBJECTIONS

units.la: Objiciunt pontificii: 1. Ejusmodi ecclesias destitui vera ecclesiarum forma. Resp. Destituuntur quidem publica & verbi prædicatione, & sacramentorum administratione, quæ in publicis & apertis locis fit, sed tamen non prorsus sine publico, hoc est communi coetu. at an putabis ecclesiam, nulla apparente forma, quam pontificii stultè admirantur, constare non posse? apage illas næuias: quam namque existimas resplenduisse formam, quum Helias se solum relictum deploraret? quamdiu ab adventu Christi defornis latuit? quoties ab eo tempore bellis, seditionibus, hæresibus sic oppressa jacuit, ut nulla parte ful-geret? Permittamus ergo hoc Domino, ut, quando ipse solus novit, qui sint sui, interdum etiam eccle-siæ suæ exteriorem notitiam ab ho-minum aspectu auferat.² Nullam il-lic cerni ecclesiæ faciem. Resp. Est qui-dem deploranda ista ecclesiæ facies & horribilis Dei vindicta super ter-ram; sed si ita meretur hominum im-pietas, cur iustè Dei ultioni obsiste-re nitimur? interim tamē novit ser-vare suos in medio Babylonis, & flammâ fornacis ardentis.³ Clande-stinos illos cætus magnas turbas secum tra-here. Resp. Invidiosè fateor com-memorant adversarii, quantas tur-bas isti clandestini cætus secū traxe-rint; sed indignè horum malorum culpa in doctrinâ & pios cætus derivatur, quæ Satanæ malitiæ tribuenda est. Novum tamen non est reipub. tur-batione ascribi veræ doctrinæ & e-jus interpretib. Interrogabat Elias, an nonis esset, qui turbabat Israelem? Christus erat judeis seditiosus: apostolis impingebatur crime comotionis popularis. nihil aliud agunt, qui hodie omnes turbas, quae in pios ebulliunt, Dei cofessoribus imputant. respondeamus autem cum Elia, nos non esse, qui vel errores spargimus, vel tumultus commovemus; sed eos ipsos qui Dei virtuti obluctatur: Succurrat nobis in hujusmodi angustiis, Christum esse lapidem offensionis, positum in ruinam & resurrectionem multorum; eaq; fiducia armati per omnia tumultuum & offensionum discrimina intrepidi progrediamur: si vero etiam in hos caetus subrepserint quidam homines impii, qui tumultuentur, et Dei nostri gratia transferant ad lasciviam, de quibus Iud. ep.v.4 & seq: sunt leges & legum paenae, quibus pro meritis graviter coerceantur; ne autem pii ob scelestorum nequitiam male audiant.{+}
units.tr: The Papists object: (1) Such churches lack the true form of a church. Answer: They indeed lack the public preaching of the Word and the administration of the sacraments, which take place in public and open places; yet they are not entirely without a public, that is, a common, assembly. But do you think the Church cannot subsist without some visible form, which the Papists foolishly admire? Away with those trifles! What form, pray, shone forth when Elijah lamented that he alone was left? How long did it lie hidden from the coming of Christ? How often since that time has it lain so crushed by wars, seditions, and heresies that it shone in no part? Let us therefore leave this to the Lord, who alone knows who are his, and who sometimes withdraws even the outward recognition of his Church from the sight of men. There is no sign of the Church to be seen there. Answer: That face of the Church is indeed to be lamented, and it is a dreadful vengeance of God upon the earth; but if human impiety so deserves, why do we strive to resist the justice of God's vengeance? Meanwhile, nevertheless, he knows how to preserve his own in the midst of Babylon and in the flame of the burning furnace. (3) Those secret assemblies draw great crowds after them. Answer: I admit that the adversaries invidiously recount how great crowds these secret assemblies have drawn with them; but unworthily, the blame for these evils is transferred to the doctrine and the godly assemblies, when it should be ascribed to the malice of Satan. Yet it is nothing new for the disturbance of the commonwealth to be imputed to true doctrine and its interpreters. Elijah was asked whether he was the one who troubled Israel. Christ was called a seditious man by the Jews; the apostles were charged with the crime of popular tumult. Those who today impute to the confessors of God all the disturbances that break out among the godly do nothing else. But let us answer with Elijah that it is not we who spread errors or stir up tumults, but those who struggle against the power of God. In such straits let it come to our mind that Christ is the stone of stumbling, set for the fall and rising again of many; and armed with this confidence, let us advance fearlessly through all the perils of tumults and offences. But if certain wicked men have crept even into these assemblies, who stir up tumults and turn the grace of our God into lasciviousness (of whom see Jude, verse 4 and following), there are laws and legal penalties by which they are severely restrained according to their deserts, lest the godly suffer ill repute on account of the wickedness of the criminals. {+}

units.la: {+} Cætus illos foveri in contemtum magistratus politici. policiti. Resp Neutiquâ . sed exstitit nostro seculo novû hominû genus, qui politici videri volunt, & interea vitâ & moribus sese atheos probant. Hi magistratus, regum, ac principû edicta proferunt, quibus omni ex parte satisfaciendû judicât. Verûm ne interea oblivisçamur edictorum summi magistratus, Dei & Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Scimus,nostrum officium esse,honorificentissimè de magistratu sentire,tanquam de Dei ministris ac legatis,quantum ipsûm ordinem attinet ; fatemur, illorum mandatis esse parendum : Imò etiam malos principes ac tyrannicè dominantes eadem ratione reverebimur , quâ optimum regem, quantum ad publicam,obedientiam attinet.Parebimus ergo illis ex animo, sed usq; ad aras, ut ajunt,neâ Dei obedientiâ nos abducant. iniquum enim est, ut hominibus satisfacias, in ejus offensionem incurrere, propter quem hominib. ipsis obedias. Adversus Deum ergo si quid imperent, nullo sit loco, nul-lo numero. Ita Daniel negat, se peccasse in rege, ubi impio eius edicto non paruit. Taceo quantopere isti adulatores in magistratus suos sint injurii, dum ne tantillum periculi experiri velint, ut eos lucrifaciant Domino Deo suo: nam, quod recte confitetur Costerus in Enchiridio suo, licet multus sit in commê-dando splendore suæ curiæ Romanæ, non prius imperatores & principes fidem susceperunt, quàm populus, ne Christi gloria humanæ potetiæ tribueretur; sed primò mündus fere universus Christum agnovit, qui deinde humili obedientiâ, malorum tolerantiâ, suppliciorum perpessione, innumeris mortibus, in una fidei consensione, sicut ad Christum accesserat, ita principes, reges, & imperatores ad idem Christi ovile adduxit. Resp. Neutiquam minuitur terrena potestas, dum suo auctori subjicitur, coram quo etiam cœlestes principatus supplices ex-pavescunt.Summa hæc sit. Quæ im-perat magistratus, ut magistratus & custos divinæ legis ac justitiæ,ea ser-vare debemus ; si quæ verò mandet, ut servus pontificis Romani,eis non tenemur. ac proinde quicunque ex Dei voluntate sub cruce degunt,hac consolatione sese erigere possunt, tunc illam præstari,quam Deus exi-git obedientiam, dum quidvis per-petimur potius, quàm à pietate de-flectamus.
units.tr: {+} These assemblies are fostered in contempt of the political magistrate. Answer: By no means. But in our age there has arisen a new kind of men who wish to seem political, and meanwhile show themselves atheists by their life and morals. They bring forward the edicts of magistrates, kings, and princes, by which they judge that everything must be satisfied in every respect. But let us not in the meantime forget the edicts of the supreme Magistrate, God and our Lord Jesus Christ. We know it is our duty to think most honourably of the magistracy, as of the ministers and ambassadors of God, so far as the office itself is concerned; we confess that their commands are to be obeyed. Indeed, even evil princes and those who rule tyrannically we will revere on the same ground on which we revere the best king, so far as public obedience is concerned. We will therefore obey them from the heart, but only up to the altars, as they say, unless they draw us away from the obedience of God. For it is unjust that, in order to satisfy men, you incur the offence of him on whose account you obey men themselves. Therefore, if they command anything against God, it has no place and no weight. Thus Daniel denies that he had sinned against the king when he did not obey his impious edict. I say nothing of how greatly these flatterers wrong their magistrates, while they are unwilling to undergo the slightest danger in order to win them for the Lord their God. For what Costerus rightly confesses in his Enchiridion, though he is great in extolling the splendour of his Roman court, is this: the emperors and princes did not receive the faith before the people did, lest the glory of Christ be attributed to human power; but first almost the whole world acknowledged Christ, who then by humble obedience, endurance of evils, endurance of punishments, and countless deaths, in one consensus of faith, just as he had come to Christ, so led princes, kings, and emperors into the same fold of Christ. Answer: Earthly power is by no means diminished when it is subjected to its author, before whom even the heavenly principalities tremble in supplication. Here is the sum: what the magistrate commands as magistrate and guardian of the divine law and justice, that we ought to observe; but if he commands anything as the servant of the Roman pontiff, we are not bound to it. And therefore, whoever lives under the cross by the will of God can raise himself with this consolation: that he then renders the obedience that God requires, when he endures anything rather than turn aside from piety.

units.la: Alii porrò ajunt. {6}Eos qui prote-statibus vel aliis accenseri volunt, confer-re se posse, in illa loca, ubi publicis exerci-tiis frui queant. Resp. Gratulor certè illis, quibus datum est in publicis ecclesiis altâ pace frui ; sed uniuscu-jusque res non ferunt, ut discedat. deinde nónne animadvertis,Deum ita regnare in medio hostium suo-rum?ut omittam uberrimum & fœ-licissimum clandestinorum cœtuũ fructum in Galliâ, Angliâ, Belgio, ne quid de veteribus dicam: nondũ clādestinas ecclesias femina publi-carum agnoscēs ? 7 Per clandestinos istos cœtº ansam dari adversariis calumnia-di, comprimis si de nocturnis sermo instituatur. Resp. Equidem scio quàm a-trocibus delationibus Pontificii au-res suorum impleant, ut causam no-stram ipsis quàm odiosissimam red-dant, sed nulla neq; in dictis neq; in factis innocentia erit, si accusasse suf-ficiat. Et an miraris Satanam instare etiam nunc, quâ solet insaniâ & fe-rocitate, in parietem jam multis in locis inclinatum? Sed an putas fore, ut sic desinant doctrinam nostram, quibus possunt nominibus, infama-re? nūquid & publicæ ecclesiæ sunt prorsus immunes ab adversariorum telis? nonne quotidie doctrina no-stra traducitur? quòd non aliorsum spectet, nisi ut regibus sua sceptra è manibus extorqueat, tribunalia & judicia omnia præcipitet, leges ab-roget, omnia deniq; sursum & deor-sum volvat. Sed frustratur illi ingenio suo, modò Dominum exercituum san[illegible, ~6 letters] sanctificare exstant dei apologiæ, [illegible, ~5 letters] in quos [illegible, ~8 letters] delcunt [illegible, ~10 letters] tum nostror[illegible, ~3 letters] ut oves mac[illegible, ~3 letters] tremaquæq[illegible, ~3 letters] fortis Dei [illegible, ~6 letters] spectantur[illegible, ~3 letters] tescunq[illegible, ~3 letters] tum fuit, [illegible, ~4 letters] tionecœruen[illegible, ~3 letters] tes vindicande cutitæ exsult[illegible, ~3 letters] REFVTATIO [illegible, ~12 letters] [illegible, ~10 letters] Alunt por[illegible, ~5 letters] Ac[illegible, ~4 letters] ecc[illegible, ~3 letters] Et cœlhe [illegible, ~4 letters] dem gave[illegible, ~4 letters] sanctificaverimus, haud terrebimur. exstant deinde tot confessiones & apologiæ, ex quibus vel imperitissi-mi percipiunt, si velint, qualis sit doctrina nostra, quales sint nostri cœtus in quos tantâ rabie furiosi illi exardescunt.{s}[?] Eos, qui subsistunt in ejusmodi ecclesiis, sese exponere manifesto periculo. Resp. Equidem tempore parentum nostrorum multi viri boni, velut oves mactationi destinatæ, ad extrema quæq; sunt redacti; attamen fortis Dei manus, quâ patienter expectarunt, sese armata exseruit, quotiescunq; ita opus, & Domino ita visum fuit, tum ad pauperes ex affli-ctione eruendos, tum ad contemto-res vindicandos, qui nunc tanta se-curitate exsultant.
units.tr: Others, moreover, say: (6) "Those who wish to be counted among the Protestants or other groups should betake themselves to those places where they can enjoy public worship." Reply: I certainly congratulate those to whom it has been granted to enjoy deep peace in public churches. But the circumstances of each person do not allow them to leave. Furthermore, do you not notice that God reigns in this way in the midst of his enemies? To pass over the abundant and most happy fruit of the secret assemblies in France, England and the Netherlands, not to mention the old examples: do you not recognise churches that are hidden even from the eyes of women? (7) Through these secret assemblies an occasion is given to the adversaries for slander, especially if talk is made of night meetings. Reply: I indeed know with what savage accusations the Papists fill the ears of their own people, so as to make our cause as hateful as possible to them. But no innocence, either in word or deed, will be safe if it is enough to accuse it. And are you surprised that Satan is still pressing on, with the madness and ferocity he is accustomed to, against a wall that already leans over in many places? But do you think that they will cease to defame our doctrine by whatever names they can? Are the public churches entirely immune from the missiles of the adversaries? Does not our doctrine daily get distorted? And this aims at nothing else than to wrest sceptres from the hands of kings, to overthrow all tribunals and courts, to abolish laws, and in short to turn everything upside down. But they are thwarted in their cleverness. Only let the Lord of hosts be sanctified… there are defences of God… [illegible]. We shall not be terrified even if we have sanctified… Moreover, there remain so many confessions and apologies, from which even the most unskilled can perceive, if they wish, what our doctrine is and what sort of congregations ours are, against which those madmen blaze with such rage. Those who remain in churches of this kind expose themselves to manifest danger. Reply: Indeed, in the time of our parents many good men, like sheep destined for slaughter, were reduced to the utmost straits. Yet the strong hand of God, with which they waited patiently, has shown itself armed whenever there was need and it seemed good to the Lord, both to rescue the poor from affliction and to avenge those who despise him and now exult in such security.

units.la: REFVTATIO ALIORVM ARgumentorum, quibus Pontificii promiscuè impetunt ecclesias protestantium,tùm publicas tùm privatas.
units.tr: REFUTATION OF THE OTHER ARGUMENTS, BY WHICH THE PAPISTS INDISCRIMINATELY ASSAIL THE CHURCHES OF THE PROTESTANTS, BOTH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE.

units.la: AJunt porrò : Grave crimen esse ab ecclesiâ discedere. Resp. Est crambe millies recocta: equidem grave crimen est ab ecclesiâ D Christi discedere: at quum ecclesia dicitur, quæ non est, illinc nos abire nemo bonus improbabit: ætate apostolorum Judæi similiter iactabant, se esse ecclesiam Dei: attamen apostoli ab eis iure discesserunt, quòd solo titulo gauderent, atq; euangelium filii Dei repuerent.² Ipsos protestantes confiteri ecclesiam Christi fuisse, atque etiamnum esse in papatu: Ergo necessario colligi, quòd deseruerint veram Christi ecclesiam, discedendo à papatu. R. Responsum est antea: & neutiquam inde sequitur, quòd deseruimus ecclesiam Christi, quam Deus servavit etiam in papatu, quia à papatu discessimus: nam qui sunt in ecclesia illa, quam Deus conservavit in medio hostium suorum, communione & professione à papistis semper fuerunt disjuncti. ³ Non sufficere, si quis dicat se adjunctum ecclesiæ catholicæ latenti; sed et iam requiri ut, quicunq; salvari volunt, ad certam aliquam visibilem ecclesiam sese adjungant: nullam autem aliam, cui nos adjungamus, dari posse, præter Romana R esp. Re-
units.tr: Furthermore they say: It is a grave crime to depart from the Church. Reply: This is cabbage warmed up a thousand times. It is indeed a grave crime to depart from the Church of Christ; but when that is called a church which is not one, no good man will disapprove of our leaving it. In the age of the apostles the Jews likewise boasted that they were the Church of God; yet the apostles rightly departed from them, because they had only the title and drove away the gospel of the Son of God. The Protestants themselves confess that the Church of Christ existed, and still exists, in the papacy; therefore it follows necessarily that by departing from the papacy they have deserted the true Church of Christ. Reply: This has been answered before, and it by no means follows that we have deserted the Church of Christ, which God preserved even in the papacy, because we have departed from the papacy. For those who are in that Church, which God preserved in the midst of his enemies, have always been separated from the Papists in communion and in profession. (3) It is not enough, if someone says that he is joined to the hidden catholic Church; but it is also required that all who wish to be saved join themselves to some definite visible Church. And that no other Church can be given to which we might join ourselves, except the Roman… Reply: Re-

units.la: [illegible, ~400 letters] Requiritur, ut adjungamus nos ad ecclesiam certam, videlicet, si nobis nota sit, nosq; ad illā adjungere possimus: sin minus, etiā salvi esse possunt, qui in nullā particulari ecclesiā vivunt, quæ videlicet fruatur publico ministerio verbi. exempli gratia, si quis vivat inter Turcas vel apud Barbaros, atq; illic solus degat, nihilominus tamen salvari potest, si veram fidem habeat, atq; ita sit ex numero illorum, qui sunt membra ecclesiæ catholicæ & Christi.
units.tr: [illegible] It is required that we join ourselves to a definite Church, namely, one that is known to us and to which we can join ourselves. But if not, those who live in no particular Church, which namely enjoys the public ministry of the Word, can nevertheless be saved. For example, if someone lives among the Turks or amongst the barbarians, and dwells there alone, he can nevertheless be saved, if he has the true faith, and so is among the number of those who are members of the catholic Church and of Christ.

units.la: 4 Athanasium, Augustinum, Basilium, Chrysostomum omnemq;[?] venerandam antiquitatem suas sententias ecclesiæ Romanæ placitis semperno foedere addixisse, Resp. Summum discrimen est inter ecclesiam Romanam, quæ fuit temporibus patrum & qualis postea facta est, atque etiam qualem nunc sese probat. Scotta, quæ sese publicè Romæ prostituunt & quotannis certum censum vel tributum pendunt cuidam ex ministris papæ, etiam fuerunt virgines, quum lac maternum sugerent. Idem statuitur merito de hodiernā ecclesiā Romanā, si conferatur cum illā veteri, veterem illam rectè prædicamus scholam apostolorum & metropolin pie-tatis ; recentiorem autem Romanam proh dolor jure vocamus scholam errorum & matrem abominationum terræ. 5. eAugustinum in lib. de util. credendi hunc in modum nos instituere. Dubitamus nos illius ecclesiæ conderegremio, quæ ab apostolicâ sede, per successiones episcoporum frustra circumlatrantibus hæreticis, culmen auctoritatis obtinuit ?
units.tr: 4 The claim that Athanasius, Augustine, Basil, Chrysostom and all venerable antiquity bound their opinions to the tenets of the Roman Church by an unbreakable covenant. Resp. There is the greatest difference between the Roman Church of the Fathers' times, and the Church as it was later made, and as it now shows itself. Harlots who openly sell themselves in Rome and pay a fixed annual levy or tribute to one of the pope's ministers were once virgins, while still sucking their mothers' milk. The same rightly applies to the Roman Church of today, if it is compared with the ancient one. We rightly call the ancient Church the school of the apostles and the metropolis of piety; but the more recent Rome, to our sorrow, we justly call the school of errors and the mother of abominations on earth. 5. Augustine, in his book On the Profit of Believing, teaches us in this way: Do we doubt the bosom of that Church which, from the apostolic see through a succession of bishops, while heretics bark around it in vain, has gained the height of authority?

units.la: ℟. Restitue illam ecclesiam, quæ fuit tempore Augustini, & lubētes[?] nos in illius gremio condemus. 6. Non minus illustre esse testimonium Hieronymi in dialogo contra Luciferianos sub finem, quum ait ; Brevem aper-tamq; animi mei sententiam proferam, in illa esse ecclesia permanendum, quæ ab apostolis fundata usque in diem hunc durat. ℟. Equidem permanendum est in illa ecclesia, quæ ab apostolis est fundata, & usque ad hunc diem duravit vel permansit in veritate apostolica ; at ecclesia Romana, licet ab apostolis sit fundata, à doctrina apostolorum defecit.
units.tr: Resp. Restore that Church which existed in Augustine's time, and let us gladly settle in its bosom. 6. The testimony of Jerome in his dialogue against the Luciferians near the end is no less distinguished, where he says: "I will set forth my brief and open opinion: one must remain in that Church which, founded by the apostles, endures down to this day." Resp. Indeed one must remain in that Church which was founded by the apostles and has lasted, or remained, to this day in apostolic truth. But the Roman Church, although it was founded by the apostles, has fallen away from the apostles' doctrine.

units.la: 7. Praeterea etiam aliorum veterum & virorum sanctorum exempla allegant, & dicunt, S. prophetas, Joannem baptistam, eMariam, Elisabetham, & complures pios neutiquam se-se ab ecclesia Jerofolymitana[?] Judaica subduxisse, licet non ignorarint sacerdotes & Levi-tas iltas illorum temporum admodum corruptos fuisse. Multò minus ergo licere christianis N.T. secedere ab ecclesiâ Romanâ, licet in eâ nonnulli reperiantur errores. ¶ Ex manda-to Dei singulari tenebâtur illi sacrificia offerre, atque in sacris sese exercere eo in loco, quem Deus designarat; nos verò ejusmodi præceptis non asstringimur. deinde servabant cerimonias & sacrificia in lege præscripta; falsis autem scribarum & pha-risæorum dogmatis non propterea communicarunt: at qui subscribunt placitis Romanensium, coguntur profiteri dogmata per-versa, neque eis licet sacramenta ex Christi instituto percipere, ac Dei nomen sincerè invocare. dispar itaque est utrinq; ratio.
units.tr: 7. Moreover, they also cite the examples of other ancient and holy men, and say that the holy prophets, John the Baptist, Mary, Elisabeth and many godly persons never withdrew from the Jewish Church of Jerusalem, although they were not unaware that the priests and Levites of those times were very corrupt. Much less, therefore, is it lawful for Christians of the New Testament to secede from the Roman Church, even though some errors are found in it. ¶ By a singular command of God they were bound to offer sacrifices and to exercise themselves in sacred rites in the place which God had designated; but we are not bound by such precepts. Next, they kept the ceremonies and sacrifices prescribed in the law, yet on that account they did not share in the false doctrines of the scribes and Pharisees. But those who subscribe to the tenets of the Romanists are compelled to profess perverse doctrines, nor are they permitted to receive the sacraments according to Christ's institution or to call upon the name of God sincerely. The case is therefore unlike on either side.

units.la: 8 Summos imperatores & reges Christianos maximis muneribus & officius suum erga ec-clesiam et pontifices Romanos animum summâ cum humilitate testatos esse. ¶ Et contra in pontificibus eorumque cōjuratis summam principes christiani deprehenderunt tan-dem ingratitudinem, summumque fastum; adeo ut neque tandem veritus fuerit pon-tifex pedem suum illis osculandum præbe-re, qua de re extat testimonium Christo-phori Marcelli episcopi Corcyrensis ad Leo-nem x. pontificem Romanum, & aliorum. Corcyrensis hac habet. Electus imperator, ut primùm pōtificem videt, detecto capite illum, genu terram tangens, veneratur: & iterum, quùm appropinquat ad gradus sedis, genu flectit; demum ad pontificis pedes pervenit, illos in reverentiam servatoris devotè osculatur. pontifex hilari vultu cæsarem aspiciens, ad osculum manus & oris recipit. tum cæsar iterum genu flectens auri massam ad pedes pontificis offert, habetque verba ad pontificem, gratias agens pro honore suscepto, pro ut ei videbatur. pontifex benignè ei respondens eum sublevat, & summa charitatis declaratione amplectitur. & stante ibi ad dextram pontificis cæsare, pontifex recipit imperatorem ad osculum pedis, & manus: regem verò, si quis adesset, ad osculum pedis, manus, & oris: alios autem prælatos, proceres, & nobiles cæsaris ad osculum pedis tantùm, Hæc Mar-cellus istè. En verò inauditam & intolerabilem Romanensium superbiam. His adde Alexandri III. papæ facinus, quod refert Jacobus Philippus Bergomensis monachus in supplemento chronicorum p.299. Inito fœdere inter imperatorem Fridericum & pontificem, Alexander summus pontifex confestim ad januas templi divi Marci euangelistæ accessit, & ibidem universo adstante populo, imperatori iussit, ut se humi pro-sterneret, lemeret, & ver[?] Quo facto Alex[?] ni collum pede[?] elt, super alpid[?] & conculcabis,[?] dericus, non ibi[?] cesfores, pateo[?] mihi & Petro, E[?] hibuerint Roma[?] ftianos & viros[?] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] sterneret, & veniam denuo expostularet. Quo facto Alexander pontifex imperatoris collum pede comprimens, ait: scriptum est, super aspidem & basiliscum ambulabis & conculcabis leonem & draconē. At Fredericus; non tibi, inquit, sed Petro, cui successores, pareo. Et summus pontifex ait, & mihi & Petro. Enitaq; quàm gratos sese exhibuerint Romanenses erga principes Christianos & viros bonos.
units.tr: (8) That the greatest emperors and Christian kings have, with the greatest gifts and services, testified with the utmost humility their devotion to the Church and to the Roman pontiffs. And on the contrary, Christian princes have at length found among the popes and their associates the greatest ingratitude and the highest pride; so much so that the pontiff did not hesitate to offer his foot for them to kiss. Concerning this there exists the testimony of Christopher Marcellus, bishop of Corfu, addressed to Pope Leo X, and of others. The Corfiote bishop has the following. As soon as the elected emperor sees the pontiff, with bared head he kneels and venerates him; and again, when he approaches the steps of the throne, he bends the knee once more; at last he comes to the pontiff's feet and devoutly kisses them in reverence for the Saviour. The pontiff, looking upon the emperor with a cheerful countenance, receives him to the kiss of the hand and of the mouth. Then the emperor, kneeling again, offers a mass of gold at the pontiff's feet, and speaks to the pontiff, giving thanks for the honour received, as seemed fitting to him. The pontiff, responding kindly, raises him up and embraces him with the greatest declaration of love. And with the emperor standing there at the pontiff's right hand, the pontiff receives the emperor to the kiss of the foot and of the hand; but a king, if one were present, to the kiss of the foot, hand and mouth; and the other prelates, nobles and magnates of the emperor only to the kiss of the foot. So writes Marcellus. Behold, indeed, the unheard-of and intolerable arrogance of the Romanists! Add to these the deed of Pope Alexander III, which Jacobus Philippus of Bergamo, a monk, relates in the Supplement of the Chronicles, p. 299. When a treaty had been concluded between the emperor Frederick and the pontiff, Pope Alexander at once came to the doors of the church of St Mark the Evangelist, and there, with the whole people standing by, ordered the emperor to prostrate himself on the ground, to kiss, and to ask pardon again. When this was done, Pope Alexander, pressing the emperor's neck with his foot, said: "It is written, you shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and trample the lion and the dragon." But Frederick said: "Not to you, but to Peter, whose successors I obey." And the supreme pontiff said: "To me and to Peter." Consider how little the Romanists have shown themselves grateful towards Christian princes and good men.

units.la: 9. Contra veteres haereticos & schismaticos consuevisse episcopos, atq; ecclesiam Romanam variis modis infestari. Dictum est saepius, nos neutiquam detrahere veteri ecclesiæ Romanæ, sed tantùm aversari hodiernam, quæ defecit a Christo & puritate doctrinæ euangelicæ. Deque episcopis Romanis ante multos annos conquesti sunt complures viri pii & docti. Franciscus Picus comes Mirandulanus haec scribit in epist. ad Leonem X. & concilium Lateranense de reformandis moribus; Quid aliud pater sanctissime: quidnam aliud nobis intelligi dedere? quas sacras aedes & templa lenonib. & catamitis: quàm nefariis lupis optimi pastoris ovilia demandata: quàm virginibus olim dicata plerisq; in urbibus septa, in meretricios fornices & obscaena latibula fuisse conversa!
units.tr: 9. That the Papists have often attacked both the ancient heretics and schismatics and the Roman Church in various ways. It has been said more than once that we by no means disparage the ancient Roman Church; we only object to the present one, which has fallen away from Christ and from the purity of evangelical doctrine. Many pious and learned men have also complained of the Roman bishops over many years. Franciscus Pico, Count of Mirandola, writes this in his letter to Leo X and the Lateran Council on reforming morals: "What else, most holy Father, have they allowed us to understand? What sacred buildings and temples have been handed over to pimps and catamites, what sheepfolds of the best Shepherd to savage wolves, and how many houses once dedicated to virgins in many cities have been turned into brothels and filthy hiding places!"

units.la: 10. Protestantes non tantùm aversari ecclejam Romanam, verum etiam universum fere terrarum orbem seditionibus, & bellis pertur-basse. ¶. Coacti sunt quidam ex principib° Christianis adversus crudelitatem Romanensium juste se tueri: quinam vero perrur-bent terrarum orbem, docent historiae Gallicanae, Belgicae, & similes.
units.tr: 10. That the Protestants not only dislike the Roman Church, but have also thrown almost the whole world into sedition and war. ¶. Some of the Christian princes were compelled to defend themselves justly against Roman cruelty. Who it really is that disturbs the world, the histories of France, the Netherlands, and similar countries show.

units.la: II. Revera praecipuam dissensionis causam esse merum odium hierarchiae ac disciplinae ecclesiasticae Romanae: & insatiabilem dominandi cupiditatem. ¶. Vera causa discessionis protestantium est; quia Romanenses pontifices à vero Dei cultu defecerunt, & homines innocentes ac pios ferro ac flammâ persequuntur. Sed audi Casandrum, qui longè aliter quàm hodierni Jesuitae, judicat, quum ait lib. consult. art. 7. Etiamsi protestantes seclusi ab ecclesiâ viderentur, & in aliquo per tempus errore versarentur, non putarem tamen ab internâ illâ, quam animo & voluntate colerent, alienos esse habendos. non negarem multos initio pio studio ad acriorem reprehensionem manifestorum abusuum impulsos fuisse, & praecipuam causam hujus calamitatis & distractionis ecclesiae illis assignandam, qui, inani quodam fastu ecclesiasticae potestatis inflati, rectè & modestè admonentes superbè & superstitiosè contemserunt, & repulerunt. quare
units.tr: II. In truth, the chief cause of the dissension is simply hatred of the Roman hierarchy and church discipline, and an insatiable lust for domination. ¶. The true cause of the Protestant secession is that the Roman pontiffs have fallen away from the true worship of God and persecute innocent and pious men with sword and fire. But listen to Cassander, who judges quite differently from today's Jesuits when he says in his Consultatio, article 7: "Even if the Protestants seem to be cut off from the Church and for some time to be in error, I would not think they should be regarded as alien from that inward Church which they cherish in mind and will. I would not deny that many were at first driven by pious zeal to a sharper rebuke of manifest abuses, and that the chief cause of this calamity and division of the Church must be assigned to those who, puffed up with a certain empty pride of ecclesiastical power, haughtily and superstitiously despised and repulsed those who admonished them rightly and modestly. Therefore..."

Item Neq; unquam , cre-do, controversia apud nos de unitate ex-terna exstitisset,nisi pōtifices Romani hac auctoritate ad dominationis quandā spe-ciem abusi fuissent, eámque extra fines à Christo & ecclesiâ veteri præscriptos ambi-tionis & cupiditatis causâ extulissent. hæc (Cassander. Idem fatentur alii. Quanti ve-rò æstiment præsules Romani ecclesiæ di-sciplinam,audi ex Francisco Pico, qui in-genuè & verè ad Leonem pōtificem; Apud plerosque,inquit,religionis nostræ primo-res, ad quorum exemplum componi atque formari plebs ignara debuisset, aut nullus, aut certè exiguus Dei cultus,nulla bene vi-vendi ratio atque institutio, nullus pudor, nulla modestia; justitia vel in odium vel in gratiam declinavit; pietas in superstitionę pene procubuit. Item. Nostra verò & in sacras ædes fit irruptio & ab illis etiam (pro pudor!)fœminæ abiguntur ad eorum libi-dines explendas,& meritorii pueri à parentibus commodantur & condonantur his, quiab omni etiam corporis concessâ voluptate sese immaculatos custodire debe-rent, hi postea ad sacerdotiorum gradus promoventur ætatis flore exoleto. non igitur miremur, si dejerent & falsò se nosse utrumque sacrarum literarum instrumentum ,p-fiteantur: quoniam nec quid ejus nomen significet pernovere. ac memini puerum quendam in episcopi locum accitum, qui, quoniam literas penitus ignorabat, per jocum dum interrogaretur,an magnos progressus fecisset in disciplinis? respondit ingenuè,non dum se didicisse exordium ejus orationis, quam de more sacerdotes prefari solent sacra facturi: novi & qui annuas sacerdotii pecunias, commendatas eorum fidei,spurcissimis voluptatibus & impendat, & impendisse glorientur. similia conquestus est orator ducis Bavariæ in concilio Tridentino; item alii, viri præstantissimi, unde etiam Adrianus vi. papa in epist. ad principes electores confitetur corruptione à curia Romana in omnes inferiores emanasse: vide fasciculum rerum pa. 173.
units.tr: Therefore I think no firm peace in the Church can be hoped for unless it begins with those who gave the cause of destruction, that is, unless those who preside over church government relax something of that excessive rigour, concede something to the peace of the Church, and, yielding to the prayers and admonitions of many pious people, correct the manifest abuses by the rule of the divine Scriptures and of the ancient Church, from which they have departed. Likewise I believe there would never have arisen among us any controversy about external unity, unless the Roman pontiffs had abused this authority to a certain semblance of domination, and for the sake of ambition and greed had extended it beyond the limits prescribed by Christ and the ancient Church. Thus far Cassander. Others also confess the same. How highly the Roman prelates value the discipline of the Church, hear from Franciscus Pico, who wrote frankly and truly to Pope Leo: "Among most of the leaders of our religion, after whose example the ignorant common people ought to have been formed and shaped, there is either no worship of God at all, or certainly a very small amount; no rule or training in good living; no shame, no modesty; justice has tended either to hatred or to favour; piety has almost collapsed into superstition." Likewise: "Indeed, our sacred buildings are invaded, and women (for shame!) are driven out there to satisfy their lusts; boys who are meant to deserve merit are lent and handed over by their parents to these men, who ought to keep themselves undefiled from every bodily pleasure; these men are then promoted to the grades of the priesthood when their youthful bloom has faded. We should not wonder, then, if they fail and profess falsely that they know both instruments of the sacred writings, since they do not even know what the name of each means. I remember a certain boy summoned to take a bishop's place who, since he was completely ignorant of letters, was asked in jest whether he had made great progress in his studies. He answered frankly that he had not yet learned the opening of that prayer which priests customarily recite when about to perform sacred rites. I also know men who spend and boast of having spent the yearly revenues of the priesthood, entrusted to their good faith, on the foulest pleasures." The orator of the Duke of Bavaria at the Council of Trent made similar complaints, as did other most distinguished men; hence also Adrian VI, in his letter to the electors, confesses that corruption has flowed from the Roman curia into all the lower ranks. See the Fasciculus rerum, p. 173.

units.la: {12} Protestantes præterea ejusmodi grave odium in sedem & ecclesiam Romanam habere, quia vident illa stante nova sua dogmata ruere oportere. ℞. Imo vero, quia vident ab ea, non absque insigni contumelia in Deum, & summo cum dispendio populi christiani, Domini nostri Jesu Christi & verbi divini auctoritatem ac veritatem indignissime conculcari. 13. Protestantes quidem videri velle singulares zelotas, & sectatores apostolorum; at revera probare, quam parum faciant mandata Domini; nullibi enim in S. literis permittit ejusmodi discedendi licentiam, sed potius juberi. 2 Thef. 3. 14. & alibi, ut non habeamus errantem velut inimicum, sed admoneamus ut fratrem. ℞. Quid exigant S. literae, liquet ex ante-dictis. In epist. ad Thef. jubetur praeterea, ut nullum commercium habeamus cum illo, qui non obedit sermoni evangelico. deinde apostolus intelligit illos, de quibus spes emendationis superest: at jurati pontificis Romani oppugnant aperte doctrinam Christi, & ab ea malitiose ac pertinaciter fideles abalienare student; tanquam ministri Satanae, & aperti hostes Christi & professionis evangelicae, de quibus apostolus ad Tit. cap. 3. vers. 10. Haereticum hominem post unam & alteram commonefactionem rejice. & Johannes 2. epist. v. 10. 11. Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc doctrinam (quam habemus in scripturis canocanonicis, prophetiicis & apostolicis) non adfert, ne recipite eum domum, nec Ave ei dicite: qui enim dicit ei Ave communicat operibus ejus malis.
units.tr: {12} Furthermore, the Protestants have such a grave hatred of the Roman see and Church because they see that their new doctrines must fall if it stands. ℞. On the contrary, they hate it because they see that through it, not without great insult to God and with the greatest loss to the Christian people, the authority and truth of our Lord Jesus Christ and of the divine Word are most shamefully trampled underfoot. 13. The Protestants indeed wish to appear to be singular zealots and followers of the apostles; but in fact they show how little they heed the Lord's commands. For nowhere in the holy writings is such a licence to depart granted; rather the opposite is commanded. 2 Thess. 3.14: "that we should not regard the erring one as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother." ℞. What the holy writings require is clear from what has been said above. In the Epistle to the Thessalonians it is further commanded that we have no fellowship with the one who does not obey the gospel word. Then the apostle means those in whom hope of amendment remains. But the sworn pontiff of Rome openly assails the doctrine of Christ and maliciously and obstinately seeks to estrange the faithful from it, like ministers of Satan and open enemies of Christ and of evangelical profession, of whom the apostle speaks in Titus 3.10: "Reject a heretical man after one or two admonitions." And 2 John 10–11: "If anyone comes to you and does not bring this doctrine (which we have in the canonical, prophetic and apostolic Scriptures), do not receive him into your house, nor say Hail to him; for he who says Hail to him shares in his evil works."

units.la: Postremo ad argumenta nostra quae an-notavimus supra pag. 2. & seq. quaest. de jure protestantium, ajunt.
units.tr: Finally, to our arguments, which we noted above on p. 2 and following, in the question about the right of Protestants, they say:

units.la: 14. Loca allegata ex Vet. Testamento agere, de populo Iudaico: longe aliam autem esse rationem populi Nov. Testam. & comprimis ecclesiae Romanae. ¶. Nullibi singularis aliqua praerogativa legitur data esse ecclesiae Romanae prae reliquis; sed quòd aliis, etiam isti evenire potest. & sicut reliquae sunt de-ferendae, si à Christo deficiant; similiter Ro-mana, quoties Christo adversatur: vide plu-ra in loco de ecclesia quaest. 2. pag. 361.
units.tr: 14. The passages cited from the Old Testament concern the Jewish people; the situation of the people of the New Testament, and especially of the Roman Church, is quite different. ¶. Nowhere is any singular prerogative read as given to the Roman Church above the rest; but what happens to others can happen to it as well. And just as the other churches are to be abandoned if they fall away from Christ, so the Roman Church is to be abandoned whenever it opposes Christ. See more on this in the place on the Church, question 2, p. 361.

units.la: 15. Locum apocal. non competere Romanae ecclesiae, sed intelligi debere de Roma, qualis fuit temporibus imperatorum ethnicorum: idque li-quere ex cap. 17. 9., ubi dicitur septicollis: hoc autem non competere Romae hodiernae. ¶. Longe aliter statuunt episcopi Belgici, in epistola ad Nicolaum primum, & diserte profite-tur, Romam esse, quae à S. vatibus Babylo-nia appellatur: apud Aventinum lib. 4. annal. Bojor. atq; idem confirmat Aventinus lib. 7. & ait: Romam esse Babylonem, & episcopos Romanos esse Flamines Babylonios. Similia leguntur tom. 2. conciliorum in epistola ecclesiæ Leodiensis contra Pa-schalem secundum. Sed sufficit, quòd urbs illa Roma aliquando fuerit dicta sepricollis[?], & quidem illa sola. Qui plura vult consulat Wittakerum de pontifice Romano quæst. 5. pag. 657. & seq. & videbit quàm perspicuè Roma ab apostolo Johanne notetur, & se-des antichristi statuatur: de quo prolixius dici potest in quæstione de Antichristo.
units.tr: 15. The passage of the Apocalypse does not apply to the Roman Church, but must be understood of Rome as it was in the time of the heathen emperors; this is clear from chapter 17, verse 9, where it is called seven-hilled, which does not fit Rome as it is today. ¶. The Belgian bishops take a very different view, in their letter to Nicholas I, and expressly declare that Rome is the city which the holy prophets call Babylon; see Aventinus, Annals of Bavaria, book 4. Aventinus also confirms the same in book 7, and says that Rome is Babylon and the Roman bishops are the Babylonian flamens. Similar things are read in volume 2 of the councils, in the letter of the Church of Liège against Paschal II. But it is enough that this city of Rome was once called seven-hilled, and indeed that city alone. Whoever wants more should consult Whitaker on the Roman pontiff, question 5, p. 657 and following, and he will see how clearly Rome is marked by the apostle John and set down as the seat of Antichrist. More may be said at length on this in the question about Antichrist.

units.la: 16 Neminem certò scire posse, cui tandem cœtui tutò atq; ex Christi mandato ad salutem suam adhærere possit, si cuivis liceat propter errores hos vel illos ecclesiam Romanam dere-linquere nullum enim dari posse, qui sit im-munis ab omni errore: Imò sapius accidere posse, ut errent viri optimi, etiam in illis, qua fundamentum concernunt. Idq; testari exem-plum primorum discipulorum Christi: eiq; convenire illud apostoli; 1.Cor.3.12. de stipulis &c. ℟. Magnum discrimen est inter ↄ er-rare, vel super fundamentum superstruere lignum, fœnum, stipulam; & rejicere vel evertere fundamentum. Similiter inter errare ex imbecillitate humanâ in concer-nentibus fundamentum, & pertinaciter perseverare in opinionibus fundamentum evertentibus. Equidem non est temerè discedendum ab ecclesiâ aliquâ ob errores quoslibet; neque etiam etsi laboretur in præpraecipuis doctrinae Christianae capitibus modo absit pertinacia. Verum, quod prolixe demonstravimus loco de ecclesia Romana, pontificii evertunt penitus fidei fundamentum: neq; ullas admonitiones fraternas admittunt. Locum ad Corinthios quod attinet, nihil inde colligi potest ad excusandum pontificios Romanenses:qua teste Bellarmino ipso lib. 1. de purgat. cap. 5. apostolus loquitur de illis, qui fundamentum licet obscurent, deforment, tamen illud non rejiciant, sed retineant; at Romanenses, nihil superaedificant, sed tantum destruunt & evertunt, haereticis & blasphemis suis traditionibus atque hominum commentis.
units.tr: 16 That no one can know with certainty to which assembly he may safely and, by Christ's command, adhere for his salvation, if anyone were free to abandon the Roman Church on account of these or those errors; for there is no one who is immune from every error. Indeed it can quite often happen that the best men err, even in those matters which concern the foundation. The example of Christ's first disciples bears witness to this, and the apostle's words in 1 Cor. 3.12 about wood, hay and stubble apply to it. Answer: There is a great difference between erring, or building wood, hay and stubble upon the foundation, and rejecting or overthrowing the foundation. Likewise there is a difference between erring through human weakness in matters concerning the foundation, and obstinately persisting in opinions that overthrow the foundation. Indeed one should not rashly depart from any church on account of any errors whatever, nor even if men labour under errors in the chief heads of Christian doctrine, provided obstinacy is absent. But, as we have demonstrated at length in the place concerning the Roman Church, the Papists utterly overthrow the foundation of faith, and they admit no fraternal admonitions. As for the passage to the Corinthians, nothing can be gathered from it to excuse the Roman Papists. For, as Bellarmine himself testifies (book 1 on purgatory, ch. 5), the apostle is speaking of those who, although they obscure and deform the foundation, nevertheless do not reject it but retain it; but the Romanists build nothing upon it, and only destroy and overthrow it with their heretical and blasphemous traditions and the inventions of men.

units.la: 49[?]. In tantâ dogmatizantium varietate, nemini certò constare posse, apud quos sit salva veritas & fides orthodoxa, si impunè liceat discedere à repraesentivâ Romanâ, quae tot seculis floruit. ¶[?].
