Reply: We do not say that it is right for the magistrate to make laws about religion against or beyond the Word of God at his own discretion; but that he ought to take care that the worship of God, just as it is prescribed by him in his Word, is set forth purely by the ministers of the gospel, understood and observed by the subjects, and that a controversy about doctrine that has arisen is decided from the Holy Scriptures; but blasphemers and obstinate disturbers of the Church are to be kept out of the city of God. 10. But princes are not always godly, nor do they always seek the rule of governing from the law of God. Reply: If they command impious things, and things contrary to Holy Scripture, the political magistrate is not to be heard; indeed it is fitting to admonish, rebuke and correct even princes, in imitation of the prophets and other faithful servants of God. For we must always obey God rather than men.

units.la: II. Impium esse, vel sanè rem plenam periculi, deferre magistratui tantam potentiam in ecclesiâ, quantam habet in politiâ. Resp. Neque hoc fit ab orthodoxis doctoribus: plus enim potest in politicis quàm in ecclesiasticis. In politiâ potest novas leges ferre, & subditos etiâ invitos ad illas observandas cogere: at in ecclesiâ non potest novos fidei articulos condere, neque potest subditos suos ad illorum observationem per vim adigere. 12 Ita actum esse de ecclesiâ, & aperiri ianuam tyrannicis ingeniis saeviendi in subditorum conscientias. Resp. Si magistratus non cedat locū sanis consiliis, & ad verbi divini praescriptum instituat in religionis negocio, non tenentenentur subditi novis fidei articu-lis à magistratu sancitis fidem adhi-bere; neque propterea ullus fideli-um vel spreti principis vel laesæ ma-jestatis jure postulari potest. Semper enim obtinet illud Christi, Da-te cæsari, quæ sunt cæsaris, & Deo quæ sunt Dei: omnes etiam & sin-guli tum superiores tum inferiores tenentur hac lege Deut. 4.1. & seq. at-tende ad statuta judiciaque illa, quæ ego doceo vos facere; ut vivatis &c. Item Ne addite ad verbum illud, quod ego præcipio vobis, neque detrahi-te de eo; ut servetis præcepta Jeho-væ Dei vestri, quæ ego præcipio vo-bis. & Josf. 1. 7. Tantummodo con-firmare & fortis esto valde, ut [cum] observantia facias prorsus secun-dum legem illam, quam præcepit tibi Moses servus meus, ne recedas ab eo dextrorsum aut sinistrorsum: ut secunderis quocunq; iveris &c.
units.tr: II. That it is impious, or at least a thing full of danger, to grant the magistrate as much power in the Church as he has in the state. Answer: Orthodox teachers do not hold this either. For the magistrate has more power in civil affairs than in ecclesiastical ones. In civil affairs he can enact new laws and compel subjects, even unwilling ones, to observe them. But in the Church he cannot frame new articles of faith, nor can he force his subjects by violence to observe them. 12 Thus the Church would be undone, and a door opened to tyrannical minds to rage against the consciences of subjects. Answer: If the magistrate does not yield to sound counsel, and does not order matters of religion according to the prescription of the divine Word, subjects are not bound to give faith to new articles of faith sanctioned by the magistrate. Nor can any of the faithful for this reason be charged with contempt of a prince or with treason. For that saying of Christ always holds: "Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's." All and each, both superiors and inferiors, are bound by this law of Deut. 4.1 and following: "Attend to the statutes and judgments which I teach you to do, that you may live," etc. Likewise: "Add nothing to the word which I command you, nor take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of the LORD your God which I command you." And Josh. 1. 7: "Only be strong and very courageous, that you may observe to do according to all the law which Moses my servant commanded you; turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may prosper wherever you go," etc.

units.la: 13 Sæpe numero & multis in locis non esse magistratum christianum, neque illum esse de essentia christiana ecclesia, & resp. Si nullus sit magistratus christianus, ipsa ecclesia habet jus cognoscen-di & dijudicandi controversias, & promovendi, quantum potest, ecclesiæ exædificatione: sicuti liquet ex historia apostolica & ecclesiæ primitivæ. Act. 1. 23. & 6. 2. & 14. 24. & 15. 2. 1. Tim. 4. 14. Tit. 1. 5. & similibus.
units.tr: 13 That often, and in many places, there is no Christian magistrate, and that the Church is not of the essence of the Christian Church, and the answer: If there is no Christian magistrate, the Church itself has the right to examine and judge controversies, and to promote, as far as it can, the building up of the Church. This is clear from apostolic history and the primitive Church: Acts 1. 23; 6. 2; 14. 24; 15. 2; 1 Tim. 4. 14; Titus 1. 5; and similar passages.

units.la: 14 Solenne esse hominibus haereticis, seditiosis, ambitiosis sese inplus quàm servilem adulationem projicere, & principibus viris quidlibet attribuere, non quòd tantopere cupiant magistratui; sed quia sperant hac ratione aliquam dominationis partem in se derivatam iri &c. resp. Qui sub pietatis & modestiæ prætextu quærunt superbire & dominari in ecclesiam & viros bonos, eos judicabit Dominus: Romanenses pontificii autem eorúm-que asseclæ omnis superioritatis impatientes non volunt principibus tribuere, quod ipsorum est.
units.tr: 14 It is customary for heretics, seditious and ambitious men to throw themselves into more than servile flattery, and to attribute anything whatever to princes, not because they desire so greatly to be magistrates, but because they hope by this means that some part of dominion will be derived to themselves, etc. Answer: Those who, under the pretext of piety and modesty, seek to domineer over the Church and good men, the Lord will judge. But the Roman Papists and their followers, impatient of all superiority, are unwilling to grant princes what is theirs by right.

units.la: 15 Ita demum futurum, ut politici nihil non ausint in rebus fidei. resp. Quantum possint in legibus forensibus condendis docetur alibi: in rebus fidei autem sunt alligati Dei verbo. Deut. 17. 18. Ios. 1. 8. ac proinde neque veteres fidei articulos abrogare, neque novos condere possunt: Si qui hac in re exorbitaverint, satius est vel vitam ꝑfundere, ad exemplum s. martyrum, quàm in hominis gratiam veritatem in Dei verbo revelatam abnegare.
units.tr: 15 In this way it will at last come about that politicians dare nothing in matters of faith. Answer: How far they may go in enacting civil laws is taught elsewhere; but in matters of faith they are bound to the Word of God. Deut. 17. 18; Josh. 1. 8. Accordingly they can neither abrogate the old articles of faith nor frame new ones. If any have gone astray in this matter, it is better to pour out one's life, after the example of the holy martyrs, than to deny for the sake of a man's favour the truth revealed in the Word of God.

units.la: 16. Confundi munia ecclesiastica et politica. Resp. Si ad s. scripturæ normæ & exemplū ecclesiæ veteris omnia instituantur, nulla confusio metuenda est. Nunc nobis sufficit demō- strase, pertinere ad officium magistratus politici etiam cognoscere & dijudicare religionis controversi- as. Ita Constantinus Magnus & patres vel doctores ecclesiæ Nicææ congregati, canones communi consensu promulgarunt : eodemque modo factitatum est in concilio Constantinopolitano, Ephesino, Chalcedonensi & aliis. 17 Imperatores christianos committisse iudicium rerum ecclesiasticarum[?] solis episcopis : neque etiam in conciliis assedisse priusquam episcopi annuissent. Resp. Ambitiosi episcopi autem postea Imperatorum modestiâ & pietate abusi sunt. Deinde rectè tribuitur episcopis auctoritas judicandi de capitibus fidei; sed nō eo sensu, ut aliorum ordinum homines omnino excludantur.
units.tr: 16. The ecclesiastical and political offices are confused. Answer: If everything is arranged according to the norm of Holy Scripture and the example of the ancient Church, no confusion need be feared. For now it is enough for us to show that it belongs to the office of the civil magistrate also to examine and judge controversies of religion. Thus Constantine the Great and the fathers or teachers of the Church gathered at Nicaea published canons by common consent; and the same was done at the councils of Constantinople, Ephesus, Chalcedon and others. 17 That Christian emperors committed the judgment of ecclesiastical matters to the bishops alone, and did not even sit in councils before the bishops gave their assent. Answer: Ambitious bishops afterwards abused the moderation and piety of the emperors. Then, rightly, authority to judge concerning the heads of faith is attributed to bishops; but not in such a sense that men of other orders are altogether excluded.

units.la: DE CRIMINE HÆRESIS Protestantibus imputato.
units.tr: ON THE CRIME OF HERESY IMPUTED TO THE PROTESTANTS

units.la: Quæritur
units.tr: The question is:

units.la: Utrum Protestantes sint hæretici vel schismatici: an verò Romani pontificii? Resp. Pontificii prius affirmant, posterius negant. Orthodoxi protestantes prius negant, posterius affirmant.
units.tr: Whether the Protestants are heretics or schismatics, or rather the Roman Papists? Answer: The Papists affirm the former and deny the latter. The orthodox Protestants deny the former and affirm the latter.

units.la: Orthodoxa thesis probatur. Nam communi omnium orthodoxè sententiarum consensu hæreticus neutiquâ dicetur is, qui relinquit perversam doctrinam; neque schismaticus, qui recedit ab ecclesia & doctorib. falsam doctrinam pertinaciter sectantibus: sed ille demum dicitur jure hæhæreticus, qui sectatur doctrinam scripturæ atque apostolicæ adversantem, eamque pertinaciter tuetur ac defendit; & scismaticus, qui secessionem facit ab ecclesia vera.
units.tr: The orthodox thesis is proved. For by the common consent of all orthodox writers, he is by no means called a heretic who abandons a perverse doctrine, nor a schismatic who withdraws from a Church and from teachers who obstinately cling to false doctrine. Rather, he is rightly called a heretic who follows a doctrine opposed to Scripture and the apostles, and stubbornly maintains and defends it; and a schismatic is one who makes a secession from the true Church.

units.la: At protestantes secessionem fecerunt ab ecclesia & doctoribus pontificiis, falsam doctrinam, traditiones humanas, & omnis generis superstitiones atq; idololatriam abominandam sectantibus: idque eo fine, ut bona conscientia Deo serviant, secundum præscriptū scripturæ propheticæ & apostolicæ. Contrà pontificii sectantur doctrinam scripturæ propheticæ atq; apostolicæ adversantem. Ergo.
units.tr: But the Protestants have seceded from the Church and from the Papist teachers, who cling to false doctrine, human traditions, and superstitions and idolatry of every kind, which are to be abhorred. They did this so that they might serve God with a good conscience, according to the prescription of the prophetic and apostolic Scripture. On the contrary, the Papists cling to a doctrine opposed to the prophetic and apostolic Scripture. Therefore, etc.

units.la: Veritatem assumtionis abundè probavimus in Medullâ papismi p. 183. & seq. ubi propositimus pandectas errorum ac traditionum pontificiarum. Similiter supra quæst. 1. de jure protestantium orthodoxorum contra pontificem Romanum atque ejus imperium pag. 5. & seq. demonstravimus, ecclesiam Romanam pontificiam pertinaciter ne-gligere puram dei cognitionem, purumque ejus cultum; & contra errores capitales contra fundamē-tum doctrinae christianae defendere.
units.tr: We have amply proved the truth of the assumption in the Medulla Papismi, p. 183 and following, where we set out the complete catalogue of Papist errors and traditions. Likewise, above in question 1, On the right of orthodox Protestants against the Roman Pontiff, p. 5 and following, we demonstrated that the Roman Papist Church stubbornly neglects the pure knowledge of God and his pure worship, and defends capital errors against the foundation of Christian doctrine.

units.la: Veritas propositionis probatur consensu orthodoxorum scriptorum. Augustinus contra Manich. Qui in ecclesia Christi morbidum aliquid pravúmq; sapiunt, si correpti, ut sanum rectúmq; sapiant, resistunt contumaciter, suaq; pestifera & mortifera dogmata emendare nolunt, sed defensare persistūt, haeretici fiunt. Basilius Magnus in oratione de fide. Ma-nifesta est elapsio à fide & superbiae crimen, aut reprobare quid ex his quae scripta sunt, aut superinducere quid ex nō scriptis: quum Dominus noster Jesus Christus dixerit, oves meae vocem meam audiunt. Irenaeus libr. 4. adv. haeres. Ab omnibus igitur talibus abstinere oportet, adhaerere vero his, qui & apostolorum, sicut prædixi-mus, doctrinam custo-diunt, & cum presbyterii ordine sermonem sanum, & conversatio- nem sine offensa præstant ad infor- mationem & correctione reliquo- rum.
units.tr: The truth of the proposition is proved by the agreement of orthodox writers. Augustine, against the Manichaeans: Those in the Church of Christ who have some diseased and perverse opinion, if, when corrected so that they may think soundly and rightly, they resist obstinately, and are unwilling to amend their pestilent and deadly dogmas, but persist in defending them, become heretics. Basil the Great, in his discourse on the faith: It is a plain falling away from the faith and a crime of pride either to reject anything of what has been written, or to introduce anything not written; since our Lord Jesus Christ has said, "My sheep hear my voice." Irenaeus, book 4, against heresies: Therefore one must abstain from all such persons, and cling rather to those who guard the doctrine of the apostles, as I have said, and who, together with the order of the presbytery, present sound speech and conduct without offence, for the instruction and correction of the rest.

units.la: Idem statuunt pontificii. In decretis Gratiani. causa 24. quæst.3.cap.Hæ- resis 27. Quicunque aliter scripturam intelligit, quàm sensus Spiritus san- Cti flagitat, quo scripta est, licet de ecclesia non recesserit, tamen hæ- reticus appellari potest. & de carnis operibus est eligens , quæ pejora sunt. Item ibid, cap. Hæreticus 28. Hæ- reticus est, qui aliquid temporalis commodi, & maximè gloriæ prin- cipatusq; sui gratia falsas ac novas opiniones vel gignit vel sequitur.
units.tr: The Papists themselves hold the same. In the Decretum of Gratian, cause 24, question 3, chapter "Heresy" 27: Whoever understands Scripture otherwise than the sense of the Holy Spirit requires, by which it was written, although he has not withdrawn from the Church, may nevertheless be called a heretic, and is among the works of the flesh, those choosing the worse things. Likewise, in the same place, chapter "Heretic" 28: A heretic is one who either begets or follows false and new opinions for the sake of some temporal advantage, and above all for the sake of glory and his own principate.

units.la: Quòd autem pontificii à fide defecerint, & scripturam sacram aliter intelligant, quàm sensus Spiri- tus s. flagitat, probavimus locis paulò ante citatis.
units.tr: That the Papists, moreover, have fallen from the faith and understand the sacred Scripture otherwise than the sense of the Holy Spirit requires, we have proved by the passages cited a little earlier.

units.la: REFUTATIO ARGUMENTATIONUM PONTIFICIARUM.
units.tr: Refutation of the Papists' Arguments.

units.la: PLerasque pontificiorum obje- ctiones attigimus, ubi egimus de ponpontifice & ecclesia Romana: de auctoritate conciliorum. & doctorum ecclesiæ. comprimis vero etiam quæstionibus proximè præce-dētibus, de jure orthodoxarum ecclesiarum adversus pontificem, & concilium Tridentinum, reliquásque Romanensium synodos.
units.tr: We have touched on many of the Papists' objections when we treated the pope and the Roman Church, and the authority of councils and of the teachers of the Church. But we have dealt with them most fully in the questions immediately preceding this one, on the right of the orthodox churches against the pope, the Council of Trent, and the other Roman synods.

units.la: Ajunt enim?{1} Omnes ac singulos fideles merito à pontificis Romani definitioni-bus dependere; & proinde vel hæresis vel schismatis crimen non effugere, qui ejus communionem deserunt. nam illum habere supremam, generalem & absolutam mandandi & vetandi de rebus fidei pote-statem: item esse summum & absolutum omnium controver-siarum judicem, atque arbitrum. Resp. Quàm verò inepta sit illa Romanensium assertio, vide in Medulla papismi pag.139. & seq. & pag.325. & seq. Item{2} Iure divino esse constitutum, ut soli Romani pontifices succedant Petro in tali primatu. &. At in Medulla papismi pag.285. & seq. si-militer[?] ostendimus, illud esse falsū & erroneum: imò verò etiam quæ-cunque cunque dictitant de primatu Petri f. literarum effatis è diametro adver-sari. de quo vide Ibid. p. 241. & seq.
units.tr: They say: All the faithful, each and every one, rightly depend on the definitions of the Roman pontiff; and therefore whoever deserts his communion cannot escape the guilt of heresy or schism. For he has supreme, general and absolute power to command and forbid in matters of faith; likewise he is the highest and absolute judge and arbiter of all controversies. Reply: How false that assertion of the Romanists is, see in the Medulla papismi, pp. 139 ff. and 325 ff. Again, it is established by divine right that only the Roman pontiffs succeed Peter in such a primacy. Reply: In the Medulla papismi, pp. 285 ff., we have likewise shown that this is false and erroneous; indeed, whatever they keep asserting about Peter's primacy runs directly counter to the words of the Scriptures. On this see the same work, p. 241 ff.

units.la: 3 Judicium Romani pontificis in decretis fidei & praeceptis morum, quae toti ecclesiae praescribuntur, esse immune ab omni errore. Resp. At contrarium demonstravimus Ibid. p. 296. & seq. 4 Ecclesiam Romanam, quae nunc est, esse veram sponsam & ecclesiam Christi. Ideoque nemini fidelium licere absque manifesta haeresEos & schismatis nota, ut ab ejus communione recedat. Resp. At contrarium evicimus Ibid. pag. 370. & seq. aliquot. Item quaest. 1. de jure ecclesiarum orthodoxarum pag. 2. & seq. 5 Schismaticum atque impium esse, separari a pontifice et ecclesia Romana quae nunc est, Resp. imo vero pium est & necessarium ad Dei gloriam & hominum salutem, sicuti constat & dictis locis. vide item responsa ad objecta 11. & 18. quaest. 1. & ob. 9 quaest. 2. & quid opus est hisce diutius immorari?
units.tr: 3. The judgment of the Roman pontiff in decrees of faith and precepts of morals, which are prescribed to the whole Church, is free from all error. Reply: But we have demonstrated the contrary in the same work, pp. 296 ff. 4. The Roman Church, as it now is, is the true spouse and church of Christ; and therefore it is not lawful for any of the faithful to withdraw from its communion without a clear mark of heresy and schism. Reply: But we have proved the contrary in the same work, pp. 370 ff. in several places; also in the first question on the right of the orthodox churches, p. 2 ff. 5. It is schismatic and impious to be separated from the pope and the Roman Church as it now is. Reply: On the contrary, it is pious and necessary for the glory of God and the salvation of men, as is clear from the passages cited. See also the replies to objections 11 and 18 of the first question, and objection 9 of the second question. And why need we linger longer over these things?

units.la: Addunt praeterea, & numero argumentomentorum certant. {6}Protestantes ab auctoribus suis nomina induere; atq; alios dici Lutheranos; alios Calvinianos; alios Zvinglianos : At Romanos pontificios nunquam ab uno aliquo certo homine esse vocatos; Illud autem esse proprium haereticorum et schismaticorum; idq; constare ex 1. Cor.3. resp. Equidem istiusmodi elogiis & titulis ornantur à pontificiis vel Jesuiticis doctoribus, eorumque asseclis; at non ex mente Lutheri, vel Calvini, vel Zvinglii, vel ullius sani. neque enim in ullius hominis, sed in Christi nomen baptizati sumus, neque etiam in ullius hominis, licet praestantissimi, doctissimi, verba juramus, sed ad amussim s. literarum omne fidei negocium institui atque examinari petimus, urgemus. Id quod ipse Bellarminus ipse profitetur de verbo Dei lib. 3. cap.3. Protestantes, inquit, tenent, Spiritum non esse alligatum ullis episcopis, aut ulli hominum generi: & Johannes Calvinus omnium hominum, atque adeo ipsorum cōciliorum definitiones ad amusim scripturarum examinari jubet: & Lutherus, non ulli homini, inquit, commissum est, ut concludat aut constituat, quid sit fides; & Brentius, non licet, inquit, cujusquā sententiæ ita inhærere, ut eam sine judicio nostro complectamur. Hæc Bellarminus. Si vis consule præterea nostrorum auctorum codices, etiam ipsius Lutheri, Calvini, & aliorum: & reperies quod schismatica illa nomina uno ore execrentur.
units.tr: They add besides, and vie with one another in the number of their arguments: The Protestants take their names from their authors, and some are called Lutherans, others Calvinists, others Zwinglians. But the Romanists have never been called by the name of any one certain man; and that is the mark of heretics and schismatics, as is proved from 1 Corinthians 3. Reply: Indeed, such titles and labels are bestowed on us by the Papist or Jesuit teachers and their followers, but not by the mind of Luther, or Calvin, or Zwingli, or of any sound person. For we were not baptized into the name of any man, but into the name of Christ; nor do we swear by the words of any man, however outstanding and learned he may be. Rather, we ask and insist that every matter of faith be established and examined by the rule of the holy letters. Bellarmine himself professes this very thing in De verbo Dei, book 3, chapter 3: The Protestants, he says, hold that the Spirit is not bound to any bishops or to any class of men. And John Calvin orders the decisions of all men, and indeed of the councils themselves, to be examined by the rule of the Scriptures; and Luther, it has not been committed, he says, to any man to conclude or determine what faith is; and Brenz, it is not allowed, he says, to cling to any opinion in such a way that we embrace it without our own judgment. So Bellarmine. If you wish, consult besides the books of our authors, even those of Luther, Calvin and the others, and you will find that they curse those schismatic names with one voice.

units.la: Conqueritur Lutherus pluribus in locis, quòd sint, qui se Lutheranos esse gaudeant: At non sic, inquit, ô fatue, non sic: oro, ut meum nomen taceatur, & nemo Lutheranus, sed christianus appelletur. vide tom. 7. Wittemb. Germ. sol. 304. 364. a. tom. 2. jen. Germ. sol. 385. a. 7 Romanenses semper dictos esse catholicos, ecclesiam Christi. Resp. Dicuntur etiam antichristi & ecclesia antichristi. idq; merito, sicuti probatur alibi. Deinde non sufficit titulus: sed videndum, quo jure, quamque merito id fiat. Etiam veteres haeretici voluerunt dici christiani, peculiū Dei &c. catholici, orthodoxi: imo magnificè sese vendicarunt: contrà praestatissimos viros Basilium, Nazianzenum, Ambrosium, Hieronymum, Augustinum, & alios dixerunt haereticos, homousionistas, Sabellianos, Basilianistas &c. adde ex act. 8. quod Simon Magus vulgò dictus fuerit magna Dei potentia. Item ex apoc. 3. quod angelo Sardiensium ecclesiae dictum sit, Novi opera tua, quod dicaris vivere, sed mortuus sic. Ergo inquiratur potius, quo jure tales vel tales esse dicamur. 8 Protestantes insuper finxisse novas opiniones, et discessisse à communi consensu antiquitatis. Resp. At non sufficit accusasse, & contrà saepius & abundè demonstratum est, Protestantes hoc uno nomine discessisse à Romanensibus, ut Deo inservire queant pacatâ conscientiâ juxta praescriptum verbi Divini, quod extat in scriptis propheprophetices & apostolicis: atque nihil aliud requirit S. patrum, vel totius antiquitatis orthodoxæ cõsensus. Sicut constat ex articulo de judice ac norma controversiarum, in loco de s. scriptura & similibus, 9 Ambrosium et alios patres mandare, quòd fides ecclesiæ imprimis quæreda sit. ʀ esp. Ita, quatenus consentit scripturæ propheticæ & apostolicæ. Ita Ambrosius comm. in Lucam lib. 6. ad cap. 9. Lucæ. Si qua est ecclesia, quæ fidem respuat, nec apostolicæ prædicationis fundamenta possideat: ne quam labem perfidiæ possit aspergere, deserenda est. Similia occurrunt passim apud veteres orthodoxos scriptores. 10 Veteres unanimi consensu pontifici Romano adhæsisse. A veteribus episcopis Romanis ad hodiernos non valet consecutio. Plura vide in Medulla papismi pag. 217. & seq. quid item de posterioribus & hodiernis pontificibus Romanis sit statuendum, quámq; graviter à veritate euangelicâ aberra-rint: tint. videibid. pag.300.301. & seq. Item quaest. de jure orthodoxorum adversus pontificem pag.17. & seq. & pag. 53. 55.
units.tr: Luther complains in many places that there are some who rejoice to be called Lutherans. But, he says, not so, you fool, not so; I beg you, let my name be passed over in silence, and let no one be called a Lutheran, but a Christian. See vol. 7 of the Wittenberg German edition, fol. 304 and 364a; vol. 2 of the Jena German edition, fol. 385a. The Romanists have always been called Catholics, the Church of Christ. Reply: They are also called antichrists and the church of antichrist, and rightly so, as is proved elsewhere. Furthermore, a title is not enough; we must see by what right, and how justly, it is claimed. The ancient heretics too wanted to be called Christians, the people of God, and so on, Catholics and Orthodox; indeed they boasted of it grandly. On the other hand, they called the most outstanding men, Basil, Gregory Nazianzen, Ambrose, Jerome, Augustine and others, heretics, Homoousians, Sabellians, Basilians and so on. Add from Acts 8 that Simon Magus was commonly called the great power of God; and from Revelation 3 that it was said to the angel of the church of the Sardians, I know your works, that you are said to live, but you are dead. Therefore let us rather inquire by what right we are called this or that. 8. The Protestants moreover have invented new opinions and departed from the common consensus of antiquity. Reply: It is not enough to make an accusation; on the contrary, it has been shown again and again and abundantly that the Protestants have departed from the Romanists on this one point, so that they may serve God with a quiet conscience according to the prescription of the divine Word, which stands in the writings of the prophets and apostles. And the consensus of the holy Fathers, or of all orthodox antiquity, requires nothing else, as is clear from the article on the judge and rule of controversies, in the place on holy Scripture, and similar passages. 9. Ambrose and other Fathers enjoin that the faith of the Church is above all to be sought. Reply: Yes, insofar as it agrees with the prophetic and apostolic Scripture. Thus Ambrose in his commentary on Luke, book 6, on Luke 9: If there is any church which rejects the faith and does not hold the foundations of apostolic preaching, it must be abandoned, lest it spread some stain of faithlessness. Similar statements occur everywhere among the orthodox writers of antiquity. 10. The ancients with unanimous consent adhered to the Roman pontiff. The inference from the ancient Roman bishops to the present day does not hold. See more in the Medulla papismi, p. 217 ff. What is likewise to be judged about the later and present Roman pontiffs, and how gravely they have strayed from the evangelical truth, see in the same work, pp. 300, 301 ff. Also in the question on the right of the orthodox against the pope, pp. 17 ff. and pp. 53, 55.

units.la: Denique {1}ex ipsorum Protestantiu[?] confessis eos jugulare conantur. conqueri enim Lutherum, Smidlinum, Bucerum et alios, auditores suos et mundum longe deteriorem exstitisse, quam fuerit in Papatu: ut totus mundus agnoscat, eos non esse papistas, neque bonis operibus confidere, neque ullum opus bonum exercere velle. Resp. Ab eo quod inest per se ad aliud quod per accidens accedit non valet consequetia; est trita in scholis logicorum regula. Deinde norunt Jesuitae prophetas & apostolos saepius reprehendere universum po-pulum, quasi nemo sit bonus, quum tamen permulti fuerunt boni. vide Esa. 1. & similia s. scripturae loca. Item Bellarm. lib. 3. de eccles. militante cap.16. {2}Omne illud malum inde esse, quia ecclesiae pastoribus ordinariis parere recusant. {3} Non recusant protestantes obedire veris & legitimis ecclesiae clesiæ Dei servis : at Romanenses non sunt veri ac fidi Dei servi, sed discesserunt à principali successione; sicuti edocti sumus antea. audi ergo Irenæum libr. 4. adversus hæreses cap. 43. Quapropter eis qui in ecclesiâ sunt presbyteris obaudire oportet, his qui successionem habent ab apostolis, sicut respondimus, qui cum successione episcopatus charisma veritatis certum secundùm placitum patris acceperunt: reliquos verò qui discedunt à principali successione, & quocunque loco colliguntur, suspectos habere, vel quasi hæreticos, & malæ sententiæ, vel quasi scindentes & elatos, & sibi placentes, aut rursus, ut hypocritas quæstus gratiâ & vanæ gloriæ hoc operantes.
units.tr: Finally, they try to strangle us with the confessions of the Protestants themselves. For they claim that Luther, Schmidlin, Bucer and others complained that their hearers and the world had become far worse than they were under the Papacy, so that the whole world may recognise that these men are not Papists, do not trust in good works, and do not want to perform any good work. Reply: The rule of the schools of logicians is a commonplace: a consequence does not follow from what belongs to a thing in itself to what comes to it only by accident. Furthermore, the Jesuits know that the prophets and apostles often rebuke the whole people, as though no one were good, although very many were good. See Isaiah 1 and similar passages of Holy Scripture. Also Bellarmine, On the Militant Church, book 3, chapter 16. (2) All that evil arises from this, that they refuse to obey the ordinary ministers of the Church. (3) The Protestants do not refuse to obey the true and lawful servants of God's Church; but the Romanists are not true and faithful servants of God, but have departed from the principal succession, as we were taught earlier. Hear then Irenaeus, Against Heresies, book 4, chapter 43: Wherefore it is necessary to obey those elders who are in the Church, who have their succession from the apostles, as we have shown; who with the succession of the episcopate have received the sure gift of truth according to the good pleasure of the Father; but the rest, who depart from the principal succession, and wherever they gather, are to be regarded with suspicion, either as heretics and men of evil opinion, or as schismatics, proud and self-pleasing, or again as hypocrites who do this for the sake of gain and empty glory.

units.la: [?] Adhærendum ecclesiæ. Resp. Ita ecclesiæ veræ in quâ Christus est habitator: hæreticorum autem synagoga est fugienda: de quo prolixiùs egimus suis locis.
units.tr: Adhere to the Church: that is, to the true Church, in which Christ dwells. The synagogue of heretics is to be shunned, as we have discussed at greater length in their proper place.

units.la: Adhærendum ecclesia ita, ut evidenter probari possit successio ordinaria: & comprimus celebre esse illud Tertulliani, præscript. 32. Cedant inquit, hæretici origines suarum ecclesiarum, evolvant ordine episcoporum, & per successionem ab initio decurrentem, an primus ille episcopus aliquam ab apostolicis viris habeat auctoritatem. Resp. Non sufficit successio personæ, sed comprimis attendendum est ad doctrinam. Audiatur itaque Tertullianus, qui ibidem, ipsa, inquit, doctrina hæreticorum cum apostolica comparata, de diversitate & contrarietate suâ pronunciabit. Item paulo post. Licet ecclesiæ nullum ab apostolis aut apostolicis viris auctorem suum proferant, tamen in eadem fide conspirantes non minus apostolicæ reputantur, propter consanguinitatem doctrinæ. Idem inculcat Irenæus libr.3. cap.3. Iis presbyteris obaudiendum est, qui cum episcopatus successione charisma veritatis certum acceperint. & libr.4. cap.43. Successio sedis est nomine tenus successio, nisi fidei habeat veritatem. Item Hieronymus in Psal.133, Ecclesia nō in parietibus consistit, sed in dogmatum veritate: parietes omnes ecclesiarum hæretici possidebant, ecclesia vero ibi erat, ubi fides vera erat. Etiam hoc notandum, Protestantium confessiones aperire januam hominibus, ad omnis gene-ris scelera. Resp. Si sufficiat simplex assertio Iesuitarum: longe aliud autem testabitur inspectio confessio-num nostrarum. 16. Imo ex dictamine religionis ipsius seu confessionum homines secure sceleribus indulgere. ꝟ?
units.tr: One must adhere to the Church in such a way that an unbroken succession can be clearly shown. Here we may note that famous saying of Tertullian in De praescriptione 32: "Let the heretics," he says, "unfold the origins of their churches, and run through the order of their bishops, so that the first of them can be shown by an unbroken succession from the beginning to have had as his predecessor some man from among the apostles or apostolic men." Reply: succession of persons is not enough; we must above all attend to doctrine. Let Tertullian be heard, who in the same place says: "The very teaching of the heretics, when set beside the apostolic, will declare by its diversity and contrariety that it is not apostolic." Again, a little later: "Although the churches cannot put forward any founder from among the apostles or apostolic men, yet churches agreeing in the same faith are regarded as no less apostolic, on account of the kinship of their doctrine." Irenaeus urges the same in Against Heresies 3.3: "One must obey those elders who have received the sure gift of truth together with the succession of the episcopate." And in 4.43: "The succession of a see is a succession in name only, unless it holds the truth of faith." Likewise Jerome, on Psalm 133: "The Church does not consist in walls, but in the truth of doctrine. Heretics possessed all the walls of the churches, but the Church was there where the true faith was." We must also note this: the confessions of the Protestants open the door to men for every kind of wickedness. Reply: if the bare assertion of the Jesuits were enough, the matter would stand so; but an inspection of our confessions will testify to something quite different. (16) Indeed, by the dictate of this very religion, or of its confessions, men indulge in sins without care.

units.la: Quod dixi, aliter iudicabunt, qui pie & sincerè confessiones ecclesi-arum nostrarum legerint, audive-rint, & in timore Domini eas exa-minaverint. aliud item fatentur i-psi doctores pontificii. Maldonatus Jesuita com. in Joh. 3. Dicunt sane Pro-testantes fidem iustificantē nō pos-se esse sine bonis operib. Idē testan-tur Stapleton lib.9. de iustif. c.7, Bellarm. li.1. de iustif. c.14. li.4. c.1. lib.2. c.6. et alii.
units.tr: What I have said, those will judge otherwise who have read, heard and examined the confessions of our churches piously and sincerely, and in the fear of the Lord. The Papist teachers themselves also confess otherwise. The Jesuit Maldonatus, in his commentary on John 3: "The Protestants indeed say that justifying faith cannot exist without good works." The same is attested by Stapleton, De iustificatione 9.7; Bellarmine, De iustificatione 1.14, 4.1, 2.6; and others.

units.la: Juxta praescriptum Pauli Eph. 6. 16. anima fidelis semper muniat se se nō solum scuto fidei, sed etiā gladio spiritus: hoc est Dei verbo prophetico atque apostolico.
units.tr: According to the precept of Paul in Ephesians 6:16, the faithful soul should always arm itself not only with the shield of faith but also with the sword of the Spirit, that is, the prophetic and apostolic word of God.

units.la: Itaque ad superandas Pontificiorum haereses, primo omnium urgeto S. scripturae authoritatem & demonstra.
units.tr: Therefore, to overcome the heresies of the Papists, first of all press and demonstrate the authority of Holy Scripture.

units.la: Illud verbum, quod prophetae & apostoli tradiderunt, & scripturae in codicibus comprehenditur solum habere authoritatem canonicam in ecclesia Christi.
units.tr: That word which the prophets and apostles delivered, and which is contained in the books of Scripture, alone has canonical authority in the Church of Christ.

units.la: In S. scripturae libris tradi-quaecunque sunt omnibus & singulis piis ad salutem scitu necessaria.
units.tr: In the books of Holy Scripture are delivered all things that are necessary for salvation to be known by every single pious person.

units.la: Proinde omnes omnino homines omnibus temporibus illis solis esse devinctos, & alligatos.
units.tr: Accordingly, all men without exception, at all times, are bound and tied to those books alone.

units.la: Illos scripturae libros esse unicā, totalē, certā & perfectissimā regulā ad cuncta seu credenda seu agenda, Neque licere ulli ecclesiæ, pontifici, concilio ullius hominis libros vel traditiones prædictis adæquare.
units.tr: Those books of Scripture are the one, complete, certain and most perfect rule for all things, whether to be believed or to be done; nor is it lawful for any church, pope, council or any man's writings or traditions to be made equal to them.

units.la: Similiter ostende prædictorum scripturæ librorum lectionem & meditationem esse æquè concessam, imò verò mandatam omnibus hominibus, tum laicis, tum clericis, qui dicuntur.
units.tr: Similarly, show that the reading and meditation of those books of Scripture is equally permitted, indeed commanded, to all men, both laity and so-called clergy.

units.la: Eâ linguâ quam, quisque novit, etiam vernaculâ.
units.tr: In the language that each knows, even the vernacular.

units.la: Præterea omnia ad salutem necessaria illic proponi sufficienter, & perspicuè satis.
units.tr: Moreover, show that all things necessary for salvation are set forth there sufficiently and plainly enough.

units.la: Deinde disputa contra auctoritatem & decreta vel traditiones sedis pontificiæ, ejusque conjuratorum, & doceto[?].
units.tr: Next, dispute against the authority and decrees or traditions of the papal see, and of its confederates, and teach [...].

units.la: Traditiones Romanensium, extra & præter scripturam propheticam & apostolicam nullam apud pios auctoritatem promereri.
units.tr: Show that the traditions of the Romanists, apart from and beside the prophetic and apostolic Scripture, deserve no authority among the godly.

units.la: Neque sufficere ad pacandu[?] conscientias, auctoritate antiquitatis, conciliorum, & ecclesiæ doctorum.
units.tr: Nor is antiquity, nor councils, nor the teachers of the Church, sufficient to quiet consciences by their authority.

units.la: a Omnium minimè autem pontificis Romani.
units.tr: Least of all the authority of the Roman pontiff.

units.la: Adhæc examinato præcipua doctrinæ Christianæ loca: & demonstra quàm indignè s. literarum auctoritatem suis decretis & traditionibus postponant, ac Dei legem ac euangelium violent.
units.tr: Moreover, examine the principal passages of Christian doctrine, and demonstrate how unworthily they set the authority of the Holy Scriptures beneath their own decrees and traditions, and violate the law of God and the gospel.

units.la: Exempli gratia: quòd {4}Traditiones & consensum conciliorum atque ecclesiæ Romanæ, vel decreta pontificum suorum scripturis proprie canonicis adæquant, ne dicam, præferunt.
units.tr: For example, that they make their traditions, the consensus of their councils and of the Roman Church, or the decrees of their popes, equal to the canonical Scriptures, not to say that they prefer them.

units.la: b Pontifex etiam sibi vendicat potestatem relaxandi leges Dei immutabiles, & conscientias hominum ab earum observatione pronunciandi liberas.
units.tr: (b) The pope also claims for himself the power to relax the unchangeable laws of God, and to declare men's consciences free from their observance.

units.la: c Similiter de iuramentis iustis & legitimis dispensant, & subditos sacramento solvunt.
units.tr: (c) Likewise, he grants dispensations from just and lawful oaths, and releases subjects from their sworn obligation.

units.la: d Præterea Papam à nemine mortalium judicari volunt, licet innumerabiles populos cervatim secum detrudat in gehennam. Adde reliqua quibus Christi personam, officia, beneficia, cultū, sponsam violat. quæ annotavimus in Medullâ papismi, loco de traditionibus; & datur alibi de illis prolixius disserendi locus.
units.tr: (d) Further, they will have it that the pope cannot be judged by any mortal, although he drives countless peoples before him, herd-like, down into hell. Add the rest, by which they violate the person, offices, benefits, worship and bride of Christ. These we have noted in the Marrow of Papism, under the heading of traditions, and elsewhere there is opportunity to discuss them at greater length.

units.la: Præterea ostende quàm inanibus gaudeant titulis, ut imperitiores fallant.
units.tr: Further, show how they delight in empty titles, so as to deceive the less learned.

units.la: Ad convicia & maledicta autem prorsus aures occludito.
units.tr: But to reproaches and abuse, shut your ears entirely.

units.la: Similiter inculcato quàm inanis sit larva ad falledos[?] rudiores, quòd jactitent communem omnium chri-stianorum consensum, & conciliorum auctoritatem.
units.tr: Similarly, insist how empty is the mask they use to deceive the ruder sort, in boasting of the common consent of all Christians and the authority of councils.

units.la: Contrà demonstrato, quàm securè quævis veterum conciliorum decreta pro suo libitu rejiciât; nec non à patribus dissentiant. Imo verò etiam inter se ipsos de plerisque fidei articulis dissideant.
units.tr: On the other hand, demonstrate how confidently they reject whatever decrees of the ancient councils they please, and how they dissent from the Fathers. Indeed, they even disagree among themselves about most articles of faith.

units.la: Assentiuntur nobis patres, quorum testimonia annotavimus alibi, & comprimis in loco de verbo Dei. Nunc sufficiat Hieronymi sententia in Esa.[?]cap. 13. quum ait, Filios hæreticorum & omnium qui decepti, interficiamus sagittis spiritualibus, id est testimoniis scripturarum.
units.tr: The Fathers agree with us, whose testimonies we have noted elsewhere, especially in the place concerning the Word of God. For now let the saying of Jerome suffice, in his commentary on Isaiah chapter 13, where he says: "We shall slay the sons of heretics and of all who are deceived with spiritual arrows, that is, with the testimonies of the Scriptures."

units.la: Quia vero multis imponunt se-cure calumniando, & detrahendo ecclesiarum orthodoxarum doc-toribus, audi Costerum Jesuitam in En-chirid. Ad extremum, inquit, convicia, maledicta, cognomina, quibus nomen nostrorum urgere solent, surda velut aure sunt praetervehenda: nam sicut qui malam causam coram judice tuetur, quum rationibus & aequitate deficitur, clamoribus instat; ita haereticus, quum veris ac solidis argumentis se vincere posse desperat, contumeliis certat, ut rem a legitima disputatione ad contentionem detorqueat. Tu vero dissimulatis omnibus verborum portentis, quasi cum homine phrenetico ac furioso negocii habeas, in solam miseri hominis salutem & conversionem animum intendas.
units.tr: But because they securely impose on many by calumny and by disparaging the teachers of the orthodox churches, hear the Jesuit Costerus in his Enchiridion: "Finally," he says, "reproaches, abuse and nicknames, with which they are wont to press our people, must be passed by as if with deaf ears. For just as a man who defends a bad cause before a judge, when he is failing in reasons and fairness, presses on with clamour, so the heretic, when he despairs of being able to win by true and solid arguments, contends with insults, so as to turn the matter from lawful disputation into strife. But you, dismissing all the monstrous words, as if you were dealing with a frenzied and raving man, should direct your mind solely to the salvation and conversion of the unhappy man."

units.la: Quinam possint judicare cōtroversias theologicas.
units.tr: Who may judge theological controversies.

units.la: Quaeritur: an viri pii, tum ecclesiastici tum politici; tum docti tum plebeji certi esse possint de veritate professionis suae: Item dijudicare, quibus tuto adhaerere possint in tanta dogmatum varietate, quantum cuiusvis ad salutem est necessarium? Romani pontificii negant. Orthodoxi protestantes affirmant.
units.tr: It is asked: whether pious men, both churchmen and civil men, both learned and common people, can be certain of the truth of their profession; and likewise, can they discern to which they may safely adhere amid such a variety of doctrines, as is necessary for each one's salvation? The Roman Papists deny it. The orthodox Protestants affirm it.

units.la: Orthodoxa sententia probatur. Nam Deus in illum finem omnibus proposuit s. scripturae meditationem, ut inde omnes & singuli addiscant rite timere Deum, & deducantur ad fruitionem vitae aeternae, sicut constat ex Deut. 6. 6. & seq. & cap. 31. 11. 12. Joh 5. & 7.17. 2.Cor.8.7. Eph.6.16 Coloss.1.9. & 3.16. & similibus scripturae locis.
units.tr: The orthodox view is proved. For God has set before all men the meditation of Holy Scripture to this end: that all and each may learn to fear God rightly and be led to the enjoyment of eternal life, as is clear from Deuteronomy 6:6ff. and chapter 31:11-12; John 5 and 7:17; 2 Corinthians 8:7; Ephesians 6:16; Colossians 1:9 and 3:16, and similar passages of Scripture.

units.la: Deinde omnium interest nosse mysteria regni coelestis: atque ita Dei gloriam & suam salutem promovere debent omnes & singuli; quisque pro ratione conditionis suae. Praeterea certus etiam debet esse quisque de sua fide & uti certo judicio, ut pacata conscientia Deo servire possit.
units.tr: Next, it concerns everyone to know the mysteries of the heavenly kingdom; and so all and each ought to advance the glory of God and their own salvation, each according to the measure of his station. Moreover, each person ought also to be certain of his own faith and to hold a sure judgment, so that he may serve God with a quiet conscience.

units.la: [illegible, ~10 letters] Idem docent Patres Orthodoxi, quorum testimonia annotavimus in Medullâ papismi pag. 57. & seq. Item pag. 116. & seq. & pag. 132. & seq.
units.tr: [illegible] The orthodox Fathers teach the same; their testimonies we have noted in the Marrow of Papism, pp. 57ff., likewise pp. 116ff. and pp. 132ff.

units.la: Indidem pete refutationem objectionum pontificiarum: Ne actū[?] agere videamur.
units.tr: Seek the refutation of the Papist objections from the same place, lest we seem to be doing what has already been done.

units.la: Unde confirmentur viri pii de religionis capitibus.
units.tr: Whence pious men may be confirmed concerning the heads of religion.

units.la: Quæritur, Utrum viri pii certi existant de Christiana religionis capitibus ex decretis & consensu pontificis, cleri, atque ecclesiæ Romanæ pontificiæ; an vero tantum ex scripturis propheticis & apostolicis de eâ confirmari debeant? Romani pontificii affirmant prius, negat posterius. Orthodoxi protestantes negant prius, affirmant posterius.
units.tr: The question is: do pious men have certainty concerning the heads of the Christian religion from the decrees and consensus of the pope, the clergy and the Roman Church of the Pope; or ought they rather to be confirmed in it only from the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures? The Roman Papists affirm the former and deny the latter. The orthodox Protestants deny the former and affirm the latter.

units.la: Orthodoxa sententia probatur. Quia Esa. 8. remittimur ad legem & testimonium, teste Domino Matt. 15. 9. frustra colitur Deus juxta observationem traditionum humanarum. Joh. 5. 39. excitamur ad scrutandū[?] scripturas. Idem probat perpetua praxis Christi, apostolorum, & re-liquorum piorum. act. ii. ii.[?] & alibi.
units.tr: The orthodox opinion is proved: because in Isaiah 8 we are referred to the law and the testimony, as the Lord witnesses in Matthew 15:9, that God is worshipped in vain by observing human traditions. In John 5:39 we are urged to search the Scriptures. The perpetual practice of Christ, of the apostles and of the other pious also proves this, Acts 2 and elsewhere.

units.la: Deinde extremè impium est, fidem nostram in ecclesiæ vel doctorum ecclesiasticorum vocem resolvi.
units.tr: Next, it is extremely impious to resolve our faith into the voice of the Church or of ecclesiastical teachers.

units.la: Detestandum verò etiam, depedere á definitionibus & decretis ecclesiæ Romanæ, qualis nunc est, queque cũ pontifice suo á veritate Christi quàm turpissimè defecit.
units.tr: Indeed it is also to be detested to depend upon the definitions and decrees of the Roman Church, such as it now is, which, together with its pope, has most shamefully fallen away from the truth of Christ.

units.la: Plura qui desiderat, consulat locum de scriptura f. pontifice Romano ? de ecclesiâ, comprimis verò Romanâ: De patribus & conciliis. Ex professo etiam hæc argumenta annotavimus in Medullâ nostra in loco de verbo Dei sect. 9. de lectione & usu script. quæst. 4. p. 58. 63. Item sect. 10. de script. auctoritate quæst. 2. p. 78. & seq. sect. 13. de regula controversiarum quæst. 3. p. 132. 136. & seq. Subiice quæ ibidem docuimus de traditionibus Romanensium. de auctoritate pontificis, & reliquis capitibus controversis.
units.tr: Whoever desires more let him consult the places on Scripture against the Roman pope, on the Church, especially the Roman Church, and on the Fathers and councils. We have also expressly noted these arguments in our Medulla, in the locus on the Word of God, section 9, on the reading and use of Scripture, question 4, pp. 58, 63; likewise section 10, on the authority of Scripture, question 2, pp. 78 ff.; section 13, on the rule of controversies, question 3, pp. 132, 136 ff. Add what we taught there concerning the traditions of the Romanists, the authority of the pope, and the remaining controverted heads.

units.la: Ad objectiones Romanensium similiter dictis locis est responsum. Itaque pluribus super sedemus.
units.tr: The objections of the Romanists have likewise been answered in the places cited. Therefore we dwell no longer on them at length.

units.la: De pastoribus & doctoribus ecclesi-arum reformatarum.
units.tr: Concerning the pastors and teachers of the reformed churches.

units.la: QUæritur. An pastores et doctores protestantium sint veris ac legitimis Dei servis annumerandi? Romani pō-tificii negant. Protestates orthodo-xi affirmant.
units.tr: THE QUESTION is: are the pastors and teachers of the Protestants to be numbered among the true and lawful servants of God? The Romanist Papists deny it; the orthodox Protestants affirm it.

units.la: Orthodoxorum sententia probatur. Nam Jer. 23. damnantur qui cur-runt, & non sunt à Deo missi. Matt. 9. Jubemur orare dominum mes-sis, ut ipse mittat operarios in mes-sem. & Paulus dicit Eph. 4. quòd Christus det, sicuti apostolos & e-vangelistas, ita etiam pastores & doctores.
units.tr: The orthodox opinion is proved: for in Jeremiah 23 those are condemned who run and were not sent by God. In Matthew 9 we are commanded to pray the Lord of the harvest that he would send workers into his harvest. And Paul says in Ephesians 4 that Christ gives, as apostles and evangelists, so also pastors and teachers.

units.la: Hinc liquet quòd jus & auctoritas vocandi & mittendi pastores & doctores sit penes Deum.
units.tr: Hence it is clear that the right and authority of calling and sending pastors and teachers rests with God.

units.la: Deinde quales esse debeant, qui ad ministerium vocandi sunt, diser-tè docetur act. 6. 1. Timoth. 3. & si-milibus locis.
units.tr: Next, what kind of men ought to be called to the ministry is plainly taught in Acts 6, 1 Timothy 3 and similar places.

units.la: Quia verò Deus vulgò per me-dia eligit, vocat & mittit operarios in messem suam, similiter docetur in scriptura s, quorum voce & suffragiis illa electio & vocario fieri debeat. Ita act 6.6. dicitur, diaconos esse electos & vocatos, convocatâ ab apostolis ecclesiâ; act.14.13. Paulus & Barnabas dicuntur constituisse presbyteros in singulis ecclesiis, non quòd sibi solis illius auctoritatem arrogaverint, sed χειροτονήσαντες [?]; quæ vox 2.Cor.8.19. usurpatur de electione, quæ fit ecclesiæ totius voce seu suffragiis, quæ porrectis manibus, ex consuetudine Græcorum, fieri solebant. Similiter 1.Tim.4. 14. legitur, quòd non tantùm apostoli; sed etiam presbyterorum cætus Timotheo manus imposuerit.
units.tr: But since God commonly chooses, calls and sends workers into his harvest through means, it is likewise taught in Scripture by whose voice and suffrages that election and calling ought to be made. Thus in Acts 6:6 the deacons are said to have been chosen and called, the Church having been convened by the apostles; in Acts 14:13 Paul and Barnabas are said to have appointed elders in each church, not because they arrogated that authority to themselves alone, but χειροτονήσαντες [having chosen by show of hands]; a word used in 2 Corinthians 8:19 of an election which is made by the voice or suffrages of the whole Church, which, by the custom of the Greeks, used to be made with hands stretched out. Similarly in 1 Timothy 4:14 we read that not only the apostles but also the assembly of elders laid hands upon Timothy.

units.la: Hinc apparet ad legitima ministrorum vocationum in ecclesia apostolica ecclesiæ ac totius presbyterii consensum & judicium requisitum fuisse, ita ut neq; ipsi & apostolici viri privato arbi-trio presbyteros in ecclesiâ con-stituerint ; sed tantùm salutari-bus consiliis populo præiverint, populus verò suum consensum ma-nuum porrectione vel aliis modis declararit: comprimis verò seni-ores, viri tum pietate tum dignitate in ecclesiâ præstantes suis suffragiis eligendos confirmarint.
units.tr: Hence it appears that for the lawful calling of ministers in the apostolic Church the consent and judgment of the Church and of the whole presbytery were required, so that neither the apostles themselves nor apostolic men appointed elders in the Church by private judgment; rather they only went before the people with salutary counsels, and the people declared its consent by stretching out hands or by other means; and especially the elders, men outstanding in the Church both for piety and for dignity, confirmed those to be elected by their suffrages.

units.la: Posteaquam verò Imperatores & principes amplexi sunt fidè chri-stianam, illorum etiam iudicium atque auctoritas ad electionem & vocationem pastorum ecclesiæ re-quiri cæpit. & merito, quia sunt eccle-siæ nutrici, & à prisciis seculis in-spectio ipsis mandata est, sicuti ex-empla piorum regum, Davidis, Sa-lomonis, Iosaphati, Iosiæ & similium demonstrant.
units.tr: But after the emperors and princes embraced the Christian faith, their judgment and authority also began to be required for the election and calling of the pastors of the Church; and rightly so, because they are nursing fathers of the Church, and oversight was entrusted to them from the earliest ages, as the examples of pious kings—David, Solomon, Jehoshaphat, Josiah and the like—demonstrate.

units.la: Eadem hæc sententia, quæ fuit ec-clesiæ primitivæ apostolicæ, san-ctè observatur in ecclesiis reforma-tis: earumq; pastores & doctores non ab uno quopiam homine proprio arbitratu, sed ab illius ecclesiæ, cui prospiciendum est, vel conjun-ctarum ecclesiarum presbyterio & magistratu fideli, atque assentiente populo sunt vocati, electi, & singuli certo cuidam gregi addicti. Idq; adhibito religioso timore, & præeunte accurato tum vitæ tum doctrinæ examine: ab illis, inquam, ecclesiis & cœtibus[?] electi & recepti; quos manifestis argumentis constat esse veras Christi ecclesias, quæq; eligendorum pastorum jus habent.
units.tr: This same opinion, which was that of the primitive apostolic Church, is holily observed in the reformed churches; and their pastors and teachers are called and elected not by any one man at his own pleasure, but by the presbytery and faithful magistrate of that church which is to be looked after, or of the joined churches, and with the assent of the people, and each is attached to a certain flock. And this is done with religious fear and with a careful examination preceding, both of life and of doctrine: elected and received, I say, by those churches and assemblies which by clear arguments are known to be true churches of Christ and which have the right of electing pastors.

units.la: Officium illorum est erudire populum & gregem fidei suæ commissū, vel simpliciter scripturas interpretando (quod est doctorum in scholis proprium) vel etiam insuper singulariter illas tum publicè tum privatim ecclesiæ usibus applicando. Præterea impendunt operam administrandis sacramentis simulq; cum presbyteris disciplinæ ecclesiasticæ & cavendis offendiculis, quantum possunt, invigilant.
units.tr: Their office is to instruct the people and the flock committed to their faith, either simply by interpreting the Scriptures (which is the proper task of teachers in the schools), or further by singularly applying them, both publicly and privately, to the uses of the Church. Moreover they devote their labour to administering the sacraments, and together with the elders they watch over church discipline and, as far as they can, over the avoiding of stumbling-blocks.

units.la: Proinde jure ac merito concludi-mus ecclesiarum reformatarum ministros, pastores & doctores secun-dum ordinem a Christo institutū, & in literis praescriptum esse vocatos, atque ita in numero verorum ac legitimorum Dei servorum habendos atque audiendos esse.
units.tr: Therefore we conclude justly and rightly that the ministers, pastors and teachers of the reformed churches are called according to the order instituted by Christ and prescribed in the writings, and thus are to be held and heard as among the number of the true and lawful servants of God.

units.la: Quod si vero quis praeterea urgere velit successionem ordinariam, atque ordinationem ab episcopis ordinariis factam; testantur historiæ, neque infitiari audent Jesuitæ, primos ecclesiarum reformatarum doctores legitimā ordinis successi-one non caruisse.
units.tr: But if anyone further wishes to press ordinary succession, and ordination made by ordinary bishops, the histories bear witness, and the Jesuits do not dare to deny, that the first teachers of the reformed churches did not lack lawful succession of office.

units.la: Illi etiam qui ordinis potestatem sunt nacti, ex jure divino, similiter ordinandi potestate praediti sunt.
units.tr: Those also who have obtained the power of orders are, by divine right, similarly endowed with the power of ordaining.

units.la: Atq; ita ordinariam successionem non minus in protestantium pastoribus doctoribus comperimus; sed abstersis postea ecclesiæ Romanæ sordibus.
units.tr: And so we find ordinary succession no less among the pastors and teachers of the Protestants, but cleansed afterwards of the filth of the Roman Church.

units.la: His assentitur veneranda antiquitas, Ambrosius lib.10. epist.82. Merito vir tantus evasit, quem omnis ele-git ecclesia, & merito creditum, quòd divino esset electus judicio, quæ omnes populi postulavissent.
units.tr: The venerable antiquity assents to these things, Ambrose, book 10, letter 82. Rightly did that great man become one whom the whole Church chose, and rightly was it believed that he was chosen by divine judgment, since all the people had demanded it.

units.la: Hieronymus ad Rusticum Monachum.
units.tr: Jerome to Rusticus the Monk.

units.la: Ita vive in monasterio, ut clericus esse mereariis[?], quum ad perfectam ætatem perveneris, & te vel populus vel pontifex civitatis in clericū elegerit, age, quæ clerici sunt. Cypri-anus formam electionis, quæ suo tempore viguit in ecclesia, ita describit lib. 1. Epist. 4. Propter quod, inquit, plebs obsequens præceptis dominicis & Deum metuës à peccatore præposito separare se debet, nec se ad sacrilegi sacerdotis sacrificia miscere[?], quum ipse maximè habeat potestatem vel eligendi dignos sacerdotes, vel indignos recusandi. Quod & ipsum videmus de divinâ auctoritate descendere, ut sacerdos plebe præsente sub omnium oculis deligatur, & dignus atque idoneus publico judicio ac testimonio comprobetur.
units.tr: Live in the monastery so that you may deserve to be a cleric. When you have reached full age, and either the people or the bishop of the city has chosen you as a cleric, then do what clerics do. Cyprian describes the form of election that prevailed in the Church in his time, in Letter 4 of Book 1: "Wherefore," he says, the people, obedient to the Lord's precepts and fearing God, ought to separate themselves from a sinful prelate, and not mingle themselves in the sacrifices of a sacrilegious priest, since they especially have the power both of choosing worthy priests and of rejecting unworthy ones. We see that this too descends from divine authority: that a priest be chosen in the presence of the people, under the eyes of all, and be approved as worthy and fit by public judgment and testimony.

units.la: Item ordinari nonnunquam videmus indignos, non secundum Dei voluntate; sed humana præsumtione, &c. Propter quod diligenter de traditi-one divina & apostolica observati-one servandum est, & tenendum, quod apud nos quoque & fere per provincias universas tenetur, ut ad ordinationes ritè celebrandas, ad eam plebem, cui præpositus ordi-natur, episcopi ejusdem provinciæ proximi quinque conveniant, & episcopus deligatur plebe præsente, qui singulorum vitam plenissimè novit, & unicuiusque actum de ejus conversatione perspexit. Augustinus Epist. 110 [?] quod Eradium cupe-ret successorem oratione suavissi-mâ proponit populo, & inquit: Quia scio, post abitus episcoporum, per ambitiosos aut contentiosos solere ecclesias perturbari, debeo, quantum ad me attinet, ne contin-gat huic prospicere civitati.
units.tr: Likewise we sometimes see unworthy men ordained, not according to God's will but by human presumption, etc. Therefore it must be diligently observed and held, from divine tradition and apostolic practice, that which is also kept among us and almost throughout all the provinces: for the due celebration of ordinations, five neighbouring bishops of the same province come together to the people over whom the one to be ordained is to be set, and a bishop is chosen with the people present, who knows fully the life of each and has observed the conduct of each. Augustine, Letter 110: when Eradius wished to name a successor, he set the matter before the people in a most gracious speech, and said: "Because I know that after the departure of bishops the churches are wont to be disturbed by ambitious or contentious men, I ought, so far as concerns me, to take care that this does not happen to this city."

units.la: Haud dissentiunt doctores pontificii. Toletus Jesuita in Instruct. sacerd. lib. 1. c.
units.tr: The Papist teachers do not dissent. Toletus the Jesuit, in Instruction of Priests, book 1, c.

units.la: 3. Ordinis potestas est in omni sa-cerdote, nec ab eo auferri potest. Idem fatetur Gregorius Valentianus tö.[?] 4 disp.5.q.2.punct.1. Clarius autem proponitur apostolica electionis & vocationis forma in jure Canonico Distinct. 23. citatur ex quarto concilio Carthaginensi, cap. Qui episcopus. Quum in his omnibus examinatus, inventus fuerit plene instructus, tunc cum omni consensu clericorum & laicorum, & conventu totius provinciae episcoporum, maximeque Metropolitani vel auctoritate, vel praesentia ordinetur episcopus. Distin. 24 c.2. extat canon tertii concilii Carthaginensis. Nullus ordinetur Clericus, nisi probatus vel examine episcoporum, vel populari testimonio. dist.62.c.1. Leo dicit, Nulla ratio sinit, ut inter episcopos habeantur, qui nec a clericis sunt electi, nec a plebibus sunt experti, nec a comprovincialibus, episcopis cum Metropolitani judicio consecrati. Distin.67.c.1. Reliqui sacer-dotes dotes a[?] proprio ordinentur epi-scopo, itaut cives & alii sacerdotes assensum praebeant. Item dist. 63. c. 11. Plebs, Presbyteros, diaconos & universam turbam vos (episcopos) oportet saepius convocare, quatenus non, prout cuilibet libuerit, sed concordantibus animis, vobis admonentibus, tale sibi quaerat persona, quam nulla contrarietas a constitutis possit revocare rescriptis. Item c. 13. episcopos per Æmiliam non con-secres, nisi post electionem vel consensum cleri & populi. cap. 19. Metropolitan. Omnium clericorum atque civium voluntate discussa, optimus ordinetur. cap. 20. sin plebibus. Archidiaconus cum clericis & populis ipsius plebis electionem faciat. c. 34. Sacrorum canonum. Carolus & Ludovicus Imperatores statuunt, ut episcopi per electionem cleri & populi secundum statuta canonum eligantur. Hunc ordinem etiam ponit Leo. Expectanda sunt vota civium, testimonia populorum, honqratorum[?] arbitrium, electio cle-ricorum. Et Romæ tantum valuit ol m[?] imperatoris auctoritas in epi-scopis ornandis, ut Gregorius di-cat epist. lib. 1. epist. 5. se ipsius iussu in ecclesiæ gubernaculis constitutum esse, quum tamen solenniter à po-pulo fuisse expetitus.
units.tr: 3. The power of order is in every priest, and it cannot be taken from him. The same is confessed by Gregory of Valencia, tom. 4, disp. 5, q. 2, punct. 1. More clearly, however, the form of apostolic election and calling is set out in canon law, Distinct. 23, cited from the Fourth Council of Carthage, chapter "Qui episcopus": When he has been examined in all these things and found fully instructed, then with the full consent of clergy and laity, and the gathering of all the bishops of the province, and especially the metropolitan, a bishop is to be ordained, by his authority or presence. Distinct. 24, c. 2, contains a canon of the Third Council of Carthage: No clergyman is to be ordained unless he has been approved either by the examination of bishops or by the testimony of the people. Distinct. 62, c. 1: Leo says, no reason allows those to be counted among bishops who were neither chosen by the clergy, nor tested by the people, nor consecrated by the neighbouring bishops of the province with the judgment of the metropolitan. Distinct. 67, c. 1: The remaining priests are to be ordained by their own bishop, so that the citizens and the other priests give their assent. Likewise, distinct. 63, c. 11: The people, presbyters, deacons and the whole crowd ought to be summoned by you (the bishops) quite often, so that they seek, not as each pleases, but with agreeing minds and with your admonition, such a person as no contrariness can revoke from the decrees established. Likewise c. 13: Do not consecrate bishops in Aemilia except after the election or consent of clergy and people. Cap. 19, Metropolitan: After discussion with the will of all clergy and citizens, the best man is to be ordained. Cap. 20, sin plebibus: The archdeacon, with the clergy and people of the same parish, is to make the election. c. 34, Sacrorum canonum: The emperors Charles and Louis decree that bishops are to be chosen by election of clergy and people according to the statutes of the canons. Leo also lays down this order: the votes of citizens, the testimonies of peoples, the judgment of the honourable, and the election of the clergy are to be awaited. And at Rome the authority of the emperor once had such weight in adorning bishops that Gregory says in his letter, Book 1, letter 5, that he had been placed at the helm of the Church by the emperor's command, though he had been solemnly sought by the people.

units.la: Refutatio objectionum pontifi-ciarum.
units.tr: Refutation of the Papist objections.

units.la: Objiciunt[?] pontificii 1. Jerem. 23. 21. rejicit illos doctores qui currunt non misi a Deo, & Rom 10. dici, quomodo prædicabunt, nisi mittantur? Itaque ne-minem debere, licet sit doctissimus, minis-terium in ecclesia usurpare, sine peculiari & legitima vocatione. Profitentium doctores autem destitui legitima vocationis testimonium. Resp. doctores protesta-tium non destitui, legitima vocati-one demonstravimus antea. 2 Non intelligi vocationem immediatam; sed Deum mittere servos suos per vocatione & electionem ecclesiæ: ac proinde minis-terium tantum penes illos esse, qui à Deo per ecclesiam sunt electi, atque hoc ipsum inculinculcari ab apostolo, quum jubet, ut in ecclesia omnia fiant ordine & decenter.
units.tr: The Papists object: 1. Jer. 23:21 rejects those teachers who run without being sent by God; and Rom. 10: "How shall they preach unless they are sent?" Therefore no one, however learned, may assume the ministry in the Church without a special and lawful calling; and the teachers of the Protestants lack the evidence of a lawful calling. Reply: we have already shown that the teachers of the Protestants do not lack a lawful calling. 2. The immediate calling is not meant; rather God sends his servants through the calling and election of the Church, and accordingly the ministry rests only with those who are chosen by God through the Church. And this very point is inculcated by the Apostle, when he commands that in the Church all things be done in order and decently.

units.la: Resp. Etiam pastores & doctores protestantium per vocationem & electionem ecclesiae gregem sibi commissum ex Dei verbo pascunt; licet non sint ab episcopo aliquo Romano uncti & rasi. ii Cor. 12. doceri, quòd non omnes sunt apostoli, non omnes doctores. atque inde liquere, quòd non promiscue cuivis ex plebe s. verbi ministerium sit prostituendum. Resp. Neque hoc faciunt protestantes, licet pontificium morem in ordinandis ecclesiae ministris probare neque-ant, imò verò auctoritatem pontifi-cis & conjuratorum ejus prorsus respuant: nam vocationis ecclesia-sticae non est ratio talis, sicuti quan-do ministeria politica & œconomi-ca constituuntur à patrefamilias vel ab illis, qui publico regimini praesunt, ut certi quidam sive plures sive pauciores suo arbitratu eccle-siastica ministeria constituere va-leant; sed necessum est ut in domo DomiDomini omnia juxta praescriptum verbi instituantur. * Act. 14. Paulum & Barnabam constituisse presbyteros in singulis ecclesiis, quibus evangelizaverant. Idem fecisse apostolos reliquos, item Timotheum & alios. Resp. Non autem sibi solis jus atque auctoritate eligendi ac vocandi sumserunt, sicuti ex locis paulo ante allegatis constat. 5 Heb. 5.4. 5.juberi, ut nemo usurpet sibi ipsi honorem, sed qui vocatur à Deo sicut Aaron. ergo non ferendos esse, qui se obtrudunt aut eligunt. Resp. Si assumas, Pastores protestatium[?] se ipsos obtrudunt vel obtruserunt; hoc indiget probatione. Sed perpetua & constans est illorum sententia, eū, qui nullam omnino habet vocationem in ecclesia, aut habet, sed non legitima, nihil muneris ecclesiastici in ea legitimè gerere posse. 6 Ex act. 20. Eph. 4.1. Timoth. 4. et similibus locis apparere, illam vocationem, quae voce ecclesiae fit, esse divinam: nam tempore apostolorum, pastores, doctores, episcopos, presbyteros, diaconos nō immediatè à Deo ipso, ipso, sed voce ecclesiæ ad ministerium vocatos esse. Indidem etiam constare, Deum per illorum ministerium efficacem esse, qui ecclesiæ voce vocati sunt. Resp. Nihil hinc concluditur a Iversus protestantes, quorum doctores voce ecclesiæ juxta præscriptum verbi vocatos esse demonstravimus.
units.tr: Reply: The pastors and teachers of the Protestants also feed the flock committed to them from the Word of God through the calling and election of the Church, although they have not been anointed and shaved by some Roman bishop. 2 Cor. 12. It is taught that not all are apostles, not all teachers; and from this it is clear that the ministry of the Word is not to be thrust promiscuously upon anyone from the people. Reply: The Protestants do not do this either. Although they cannot approve the Papist custom in ordaining ministers of the Church, they utterly reject the authority of the pontiff and his sworn associates. For the ecclesiastical calling is not of the kind by which political and household offices are established by the head of a family or by those who preside over public government, so that certain persons, more or fewer, may at their own discretion set up ecclesiastical ministries. Rather, all things in the house of the Lord must be arranged according to the prescription of the Word. * Acts 14: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders in each church to which they had preached; the other apostles did the same, likewise Timothy and others. Reply: Nor did they take to themselves alone the right and authority of choosing and calling, as is clear from the passages cited just above. 5. Heb. 5:4, 5: It is commanded that no one take the honour to himself, but he who is called by God, as Aaron was. Therefore those who thrust themselves forward or elect themselves are not to be tolerated. Reply: If you assume that the Protestant pastors thrust themselves forward, or have thrust themselves forward, this needs proof. But the settled and constant view of the Protestants is that one who has no calling at all in the Church, or has one that is not lawful, can lawfully perform no ecclesiastical office in it. 6. From Acts 20, Eph. 4:11, 1 Tim. 4, and similar passages it appears that the calling which is made by the voice of the Church is divine; for in apostolic times pastors, teachers, bishops, presbyters and deacons were called to the ministry not immediately by God himself but by the voice of the Church. From this it also follows that God works efficaciously through the ministry of those who are called by the voice of the Church. Reply: Nothing follows from this against the Protestants, whose teachers we have shown to have been called by the voice of the Church according to the prescription of the Word.

units.la: 7 Antesignanum protestantium doctorum, Lutherum deseruisse vocationem & stationem suam, & ex mero fastu ecclesiæ Romanæ contradixisse, adeo ut in disputatione Lipsiæ habita exclamaverit. Hæc causa nec propter Deum cœpta est, nec propter Deum finietur. Resp. Contrarium docent eius scripta & historiæ. Imo vero ipse Bellarminus fatetur lib. 4. de verbo Dei cap. 3. ex Lutheri sententia nullam aliam doctrinam in ecclesia tradi aut audiri debere, quam purum Dei verbum, hoc est, scripturam s. Quod autem affertur ex disputatione Lipsensi, est Jesuitica calumnia, & Cochlæi commē-tum.
units.tr: 7. Luther, the forerunner of the Protestant teachers, abandoned his calling and station and, from sheer arrogance, contradicted the Roman Church, so that in the disputation held at Leipzig he exclaimed: "This cause was begun neither on account of God, nor will it be ended on account of God." Reply: His writings and the histories teach the contrary. Indeed Bellarmine himself confesses, in book 4 of On the Word of God, chapter 3, that according to Luther's opinion no other doctrine ought to be handed down or heard in the Church than the pure Word of God, that is, holy Scripture. What is brought forward from the Leipzig disputation is a Jesuit calumny and a fabrication of Cochlaeus.

units.la: 8 Ex fructibus agnosci prophetas. Lutheri autem vitam fuisse incestam. Similiter toti orbi notum esse, quàm falsa fuerit Beza, qui publicatis poëmatibus la-sciviam suam profiteri non erubuit, alios præterea testari, quod Lutherus fuerit in-signis meritibulu[?]. Resp. Quid verò dicetur de vita & moribus plurimorum præsulum pontificiorum? Acosta aut lib. 6. de procur. ind. salut. cap 21. et 22. Et sanè magno Christianis nobis opprobrio est, Ingam[?] regem barbarum, & idolis dedi tũ, ab ebrietate[?] subditum sibi populū cohibuisse; nostros verò temulentiæ incrementa tanta fecisse. Quæ spes restat infelicium horum salutis, quum ab iis venena porriguntur, à quibus esset antidotus exspectand[?] Item c. p. 20. Coniugatorū quæque adultè ia[?] seuerius apud indos, quàm apud nos puniuntur. Deinde quibus quæso auctoribus illa dicitur de Luthero, Beza & aliis? Contrà audi Maldanatum Jesuitam epist. dedicat. in com. in quatuor Euangelistas, qui longè aliud testatur de Luthero, Beza, & aliis. Inter religiosos inquit excullatos Monachos præferimus Lutherum, Bucerum, Bezam &c. Item comm. in Matth. 7.15. Nihil in Calvinistis, nisi Pater noster, nisi Christus, nisi fides, iuramentum inauditum: nihil in eorum factis apparebit, nisi eleemosina, nisi temperantia, nisi modestia. Præterea audi Costerum Jesuitam part. 3. apolog. cap. 3 § Ego. In hac causa non loquimur de peccatoribus; Felices nos, si nemo catholicus transgressor esset legis divinæ: sed hic loquimur de peccatis, quæ vi & dictamine religionis committuntur. Hæc recte dicuntur. Proba[?]-taque vi & dictamine religionis Protestantium homines sceleribus indulgere. Secus de illis testari coguntur præstantiores ex Jesuiticis doctoribus. Quorum testimonia proposuimus supra quaest. de crimine hæresis protestantibus imputato.
units.tr: 8. Prophets are known by their fruits. But Luther's life was incestuous. Likewise it is known to the whole world how false Beza was, who, having published poems, did not blush to profess his lasciviousness; others moreover testify that Luther was remarkable for his merits. Reply: What then shall be said of the life and morals of very many Papist prelates? Acosta, in book 6 of On the Procuring of Indian Salvation, chapters 21 and 22. And truly it is a great reproach to us Christians that the barbarian king Inga, a worshipper of idols, restrained his subjects from drunkenness, while ours have increased drunkenness to such a degree. What hope of salvation remains for these unhappy people, when poisons are offered to them by those from whom an antidote ought to be expected? Likewise, ch. 20: adulteries among married people are punished more severely among the Indians than among us. Then, I ask, on whose authority is that said about Luther, Beza and others? On the contrary, hear Maldonatus the Jesuit, in the dedicatory epistle of his commentary on the four Evangelists, who testifies quite otherwise about Luther, Beza and others: "Among the religious," he says, "we place Luther, Bucer, Beza, etc., among the cultivated monks." Likewise, commentary on Matt. 7:15: "Nothing appears among the Calvinists except the Our Father, except Christ, except faith; an oath is never heard of; nothing appears in their deeds except alms, except temperance, except modesty." Besides, hear Costerus the Jesuit, part 3, Apology, ch. 3, § Ego: "In this cause we are not speaking of sinners. Happy would we be if no Catholic were a transgressor of the divine law; but here we speak of sins which are committed by the force and dictate of religion." "These things are rightly said; and it is proved that by the force and dictate of the Protestant religion men indulge in crimes." Otherwise the more eminent of the Jesuit doctors are compelled to bear witness about them. Their testimonies we have set out above, in the question concerning the crime of heresy imputed to the Protestants.
