units.la: Denique Bezam quòd attinet, notato diligenter, quãdo illa poema-ta conta conscripserit,ediderit; videlicet quum hæreret,in scholis Romanen-sium,postea autem longè alium se-se probavit: valeat itaq; illud 1.Cor. 6.11. Hæc quidem fuistis,sed jam san-ctificati estis. responsum plenum qui desiderat,legat notas Bezæ in N.Testam.Matth.1.de verbo μεταδαιμονιζων [?]. 9 Lutherum confiteri, quòd à diabolo esset edoctus, Missam priva-tam esse rem malam,ac protinus Diabolicatiónibus convictum abolevuse eam. Resp. Delrius Jesuita autem testatur lib.4.de Magia c.1. q 3.§.5.q Satan abbati comendaverit Missam,tanquam Deo charissimam. Apud Surium, inquit, liquet, Diabolum in specie angelica apparuisse & statum abbatem, ut Missam celebaret, hortabatur. Ergo quid de missa sit statuendum non quæratur ex satana, sed ex scripturæ seloquiis.
units.tr: Finally, as for Beza, note carefully when he wrote and published those poems: plainly while he was still among the Romanist schoolmen, and he later proved himself to be quite another man. Let that verse of 1 Cor. 6.11 stand as the answer: "Such were some of you, but now you are sanctified." Whoever wants a full reply should read Beza's notes on Matt. 1 on the word [μεταδαιμονιζων] (9). Luther is said to have confessed that he was taught by the devil, that private Mass is an evil thing, and that, convicted by diabolical apparitions, he at once abolished it. Answer: the Jesuit Delrio, however, testifies in book 4 of his work on magic, ch. 1, q. 3, §5, that Satan commended the Mass to the abbot as most dear to God. "It is clear from Surius," he says, "that the Devil appeared in angelic form and urged the abbot to celebrate Mass." So what is to be decided about the Mass is not to be sought from Satan, but from the sayings of Scripture.

units.la: 10 Protestantium doctores penitus oble-stare se & auditores suos meris calumniis, adeo ut si ex illorum libris su-stuleris calumnias & convitia, ex maxi-mis voluminibus vix exigui libelli effici possint. Resp. Inspiciantur utriusque partis doctorum codices, & lo-gè aliud deprehendes: quòdsi verò nonnulli exorbitent, inde nihil decedit veritatis, qua gaudemus, professioni. At non est quòd miremur hujusmodi dicteria Jesuitica. respondeat August. epist. 137. Hic mos est, inquit, hæreticorum. crimina objicere doctoribus, quum nō possunt reprehendere doctrinam.
units.tr: (10) The Protestant teachers, it is said, wholly defame themselves and their hearers with mere calumnies, so that if you removed the calumnies and insults from their books, scarcely a small pamphlet could be made from their largest volumes. Answer: let the books of the teachers on both sides be inspected, and you will find quite otherwise. If some do go too far, nothing is taken from the truth, in which we take pride in our profession. But there is no reason to wonder at such Jesuit insults. Let Augustine answer, Epistle 137: "It is the custom of heretics," he says, "to bring charges of crimes against teachers when they cannot find fault with their doctrine."

units.la: Antesignanos Protestantium studu-isse [?] fictis & falsis miraculis auditores suos seducere, at frustra. Ita Calvinum Brullum mortem simulantem excitare voluisse: Lutherum autem Dæmonem expellere. at summâ cum ignominiâ doctrinæ & personarum. Resp. Quibus auctoribus, quibus testibus? Belseco, Cochlæo, Staphylo, Bellarmino, Costero. At stultum est, ait Bellarminus lib.4. de eccles.milit.cap.14. § Sed respondemus, credere de rebus, auctoribus iis, qui non interfuerunt, potius, quàm qui interfuerunt. Absitque damnentur protestatium doctodoctores propter Jesuiticam maledicendi & calumniandi libidinem. Omitto quod confitetur Maldonatus Jesuita com.[?] in Job. 2. 18. Calvinianos docere, nullis miraculis se à Deo missos esse. {11} Protestantium ministros nullam habere ordinationem legitimam, neque successionem ab apostolis: nullum ex episcopis illorum ab episcopo legitimo esse ordinatum: atque ita omnes carere auctoritate ordinis & jurisdictionis. Resp. Quamdiu conspicuus manet ordo & status legitimus ecclesiæ, ordinaria vocatio comprimis vigetur: ubi vero ille ipse ordo & status fuerit collapsus & interruptus, Deus præter morem solitum illum instaurat, per eos quos vult. Deinde antea ostensum est validissimis argumentis, Protestantium doctores & pastores legitimè juxta verbi divini præscriptum, & ecclesiæ primitivæ morem esse electos et vocatos ad ministerium Christi: atque ita auctoritate ordinis & jurisdictionis neutiquam carere. {13} Illos à quià quibus Protestantium doctores pastores ordinantur defecisse ab ecclesia Christi; ac proinde amisisse authoritatem & dignitatem episcoporum. Resp. deseruerunt synagogam Romanam pontificiū, ut ex prescripto s. literarum Christo inservire possint bona conscientia. Quid vero quod legitur apud Asorium Jesuitam lib. 8. instit. c. 19. In episcopo haeretico, inquit, manet potestas conferendi ordines; quia facit nomine, institutione, & authoritate Christi. Ideoque ab haereticis episcopis ordinati, & ad ecclesiam redeuntes, non iterum ordinantur; & tenent aliqui haereticos episcopos potestatem quoque jurisdictionis non amittere.{14} Potestatem ordinandi tantum esse penes episcopos. Resp. De eo agitur commodius suo loco. Interea hoc nobis sufficit, quod tempore apostolorum idem fuerit presbyter qui & episcopus, quod liquet ex actis{?}. Phil. 1. Tit. 1. 1. Pet. 5. & similibus scripturae s. locis. Similiter subsequentibus temporibus iidem fuerunt presbyteri, qui & episcopi; paulatim vero ad unum omnis so-licitudo est delata, ut dissensionum plantaria evellerentur. Deinde si potestas ordinandi est penes epi-scopos, ergo non penes Romanen-ses; quia hi sunt veræ doctrinæ hos-tes & persecutores, & episcopale officium prorsus à se rejecerunt, ac facti sunt principes gentium; Imò verò illorū officia episcopalia sunt, alere equos & canes, si non etiam scorta, omniaque ad libitum instituere. 15 Quia novam attulerunt doctrinam, neque ordinarie sunt vocati, electi, et confirmati ab illis, penes quos est vocandi potestas: ergo decere ut eam miraculis confirment, sicuti etiam ipsam vocationem suam. Resp. Non novam aliquam protulerunt doctrinam, sed revocarunt Dei beneficio in lucem doctrinam propheticam & apostolicam, quæ fuit aliquandiu fermento & traditionibus Romanensiū depravata, atque etiam in multorum cordibus videbatur propemodum extinextincta. Ideo non opus est mira-culis, quia non ad ecclesiam nova exstruendam, sed ad veterem mise-rè collapsam erigendam & reformandam excitati sunt. Plura de mi-raculorum productione vide in loco de miraculis. Interea audiatur Acosta de procur. Ind. salute l.2.cap.9. Re-ligio Christiana, ubi humana præ-sidia prorsus aberant, divinis est fundata miraculis: at nostrorum temporum longè alia est ratio. Item Unum illud huic novo orbi poten-tissimum & ad fidem efficacissimū, & pene singulare miraculū necessarium est. Mores cum fide cōgruentes: hoc abundè sufficit in hoc ignorum argumento explicando. & paulo post. Non ergo fides, jam satis firmata, miraculis novis indiget confirmari, quin potius utilius esse asserit, signis nunc carere, quoniam majoris meriti sit sine illis credere.
units.tr: The leaders of the Protestants, it is said, have tried to seduce their hearers with fictitious and false miracles, but in vain: thus Calvin is said to have wished to raise Brullus when he feigned death, and Luther to have cast out a demon, but all to the great disgrace of their doctrine and persons. Answer: on what authorities and what witnesses? Belsec, Cochlaeus, Stapleton, Bellarmine, Costerus. But it is foolish, says Bellarmine (book 4 on the Church Militant, ch. 14, §"Sed respondemus"), to believe things on the word of those who were not present rather than of those who were. Far be it that the Protestant teachers should be condemned on account of the Jesuits' lust for slander and calumny. I pass over the fact that the Jesuit Maldonatus, in his commentary on Job 2.18, admits that the Calvinists teach that they were sent by God without any miracles. {11} The Protestant ministers, it is said, have no lawful ordination, nor succession from the apostles; none of their bishops has been ordained by a lawful bishop, and so they all lack the authority of order and jurisdiction. Answer: as long as the visible order and lawful state of the Church remain, ordinary calling is certainly in force; but where that very order and state have collapsed and been interrupted, God, beyond the usual manner, restores it through whom he wills. Moreover, it was shown earlier, by the strongest arguments, that the Protestant teachers and pastors were lawfully elected and called to the ministry of Christ, according to the prescription of the divine Word and the custom of the primitive Church, and so by no means lack the authority of order and jurisdiction. {13} They say that those from whom the Protestant teachers and pastors received ordination had fallen away from the Church of Christ, and therefore had lost the authority and dignity of bishops. Answer: they deserted the Roman papal synagogue so that they might serve Christ with a good conscience, as the holy Scriptures prescribe. But what is read in the Jesuit Azor, book 8 of his Institutes, ch. 19? "In a heretical bishop," he says, "the power of conferring orders remains, because he acts in the name, by the institution and by the authority of Christ. Therefore those ordained by heretical bishops, when they return to the Church, are not ordained again; and some hold that heretical bishops do not lose the power of jurisdiction either." {14} The power of ordaining, it is said, belongs only to bishops. Answer: this is treated more conveniently in its own place. Meanwhile it is enough for us that in the time of the apostles the presbyter and the bishop were the same, as is clear from Phil. 1, Tit. 1, 1 Pet. 5 and similar passages of Holy Scripture. Likewise in the following times the presbyters and bishops were the same; but gradually all care was transferred to one man, so that the seeds of dissension might be rooted out. Further, if the power of ordaining belongs to bishops, then it does not belong to the Romanists, since these are enemies and persecutors of true doctrine and have utterly cast off the episcopal office, and have become princes of the nations; indeed their episcopal duties are to feed horses and dogs, if not also prostitutes, and to ordain whatever they please. 15 They have brought in a new doctrine, and were not ordinarily called, chosen and confirmed by those who hold the power of calling; therefore it is fitting that they confirm it with miracles, just as they confirm their own calling. Answer: they did not bring forward any new doctrine, but by God's favour brought back into the light the prophetic and apostolic doctrine, which for some time had been corrupted by the leaven and traditions of the Romanists, and in the hearts of many seemed almost extinguished. Therefore there is no need for miracles, since they were not raised up to build a new Church, but to restore and reform the old one, wretchedly fallen. More on the production of miracles may be seen in the place on miracles. Meanwhile let Acosta be heard, On the Procuring of the Salvation of the Indians, book 2, ch. 9: "The Christian religion, where human aids were wholly lacking, was founded on divine miracles; but the situation of our own times is quite different." Likewise: "One thing alone is most powerful for this new world and most effective for faith, and is a nearly singular miracle that is needed: morals agreeing with the faith; this is more than enough for explaining the matter to the ignorant." And a little later: "Therefore faith, already sufficiently firm, does not need to be confirmed by new miracles; rather he asserts it is more useful to lack signs now, since it is of greater merit to believe without them."

units.la: 16 Absurdum esse, & impium, vel sanè rem plenam periculi, permittere vo-candi & eligendi auctoritatem cæca mul-titudititudinis aut populi libidini. Hoc autem fieri apud Protestantes. Resp. Neutiquam hoc fit apud Protestantes, sed primores, qui spiritu discretionis & prudentiae sunt à Deo ornati praeeunt populo sanis consiliis, & sunt electionis ac vocationis moderatores: accedit etiam gravissimum judicium, examen tum doctrinae tum vitae, & comprobatio presbyterii, pro conditione uniuscujusque loci.
units.tr: 16 It is absurd and impious, or at least fraught with danger, to hand over the authority of calling and choosing to the blind multitude or to the lust of the people. But this, they say, happens among the Protestants. Answer: this by no means happens among the Protestants. Rather, the leading men, whom God has adorned with a spirit of discernment and prudence, go before the people with sound counsel and are the moderators of election and calling. Added to this is a most weighty judgement: examination both of doctrine and of life, and the approval of the eldership, according to the circumstances of each place.

units.la: 17 Protestantes hujusmodi potestatem sibi arrogare: non posse autem rite demonstrare, unde et quam juste illam acceperint. Resp. Similem fere in modum Judaeorum praesules rogatunt Johannem baptistam Johan. 1. & Christum Matth. 21. Quis tibi dedit hanc potestatem? Unde autem acceperint hanc potestatem Protestantium ecclesiae, demonstrant s. literae, & veteris ecclesiae praxis.
units.tr: 17 The Protestants, they say, arrogate this power to themselves, but cannot properly demonstrate whence and how justly they received it. Answer: in much the same way the leaders of the Jews asked John the Baptist (John 1) and Christ (Matt. 21): "Who gave you this authority?" But whence the Protestant churches have received this power, the Holy Scriptures and the practice of the early Church demonstrate.

units.la: 18 Equidem aperiri ab illis ostium cuivis, qui se sapientem existimet, seu verbo seu falso corrupta doctrina impugnandæ prætextu, ad clandestinos conventus habendos, & ad turbandum publicum ecclesiæ ordinem ac pacem, Resp. Hoc fieret si cuivis christiano in S. L. versato concederetur suggestum conscendere, & ministrorum Dei partes sibi sumere; hoc autem apud Protestantes non licet.
units.tr: 18 Indeed, they say, a door is opened by them to anyone who thinks himself wise, whether by word or in writing, on the pretext of attacking corrupted doctrine, for holding secret assemblies and disturbing the public order and peace of the Church. Answer: this would happen if every Christian versed in Holy Scripture were permitted to mount the pulpit and take upon himself the part of the ministers of God; but this is not allowed among the Protestants.

units.la: Præterea clamitat 19 S. Patres semper exegisse successionem ordinariam, Protestantes autem ea carere. Resp. Ostensum est antea, neq; doctores nostros destitui successione ab initio decurrere. Deinde successio personæ, licet non sit aspernanda, quum adest, tamen non sufficit; comprimis[?] vero inquirendum est de doctrina. Vide plura supra pag. 161[?].
units.tr: Moreover, he cries out: 19 the Holy Fathers always required an ordinary succession, but the Protestants lack it. Answer: it has been shown before that our teachers are not lacking succession running down from the beginning. Next, succession of persons, although not to be despised where it is present, is nevertheless not sufficient; above all we must inquire into doctrine. See more above, p. 161.

units.la: 20 Lutherum ipsum agnoscere se primum dogmatis sui auctorem, & fateri se a nullo homine institutum esse. Resp. Rectius dices Lutherum profiteri quod a Christo sit institutus, in scriptură prophetica & apostolica no-bis loquente. Deinde non respuit Lutherus orthodoxos doctores: Imò verò etiam Hussi & Waldensiū fidem commendat, non raro etiam orthodoxos patres allegat.
units.tr: 20 Luther himself acknowledges that he is the first author of his dogma, and confesses that he was instituted by no man. Answer: you would speak more correctly if you said that Luther professes he was instituted by Christ, the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures speaking to us. Furthermore, Luther does not reject orthodox teachers; indeed he commends the faith of Hus and the Waldensians, and not infrequently also cites the orthodox Fathers.

units.la: Contra illud quod allegavimus ex praxi ecclesiæ veteris de auctoritate principum & populi in eligendis Deiseryis[?], porrò ajunt. At Com-plura exstare[?] exempla in historia veteris ecclesiæ, quibus contrarium facile probari queat: & Valentinianum Imperat. illam auctoritate detulisse clericis. Resp. Pontifices Romani autè modestiâ piorum principū postea admodū abusi sunt. Deinde clerus agnovit eligendi potestatem esse penes Imperatorem: vide c. 3. Valentinian. dist. 63. Similiter apud Sozom. l. 7. c. 7. Imperator in Synodo eligit Nazianzenum, & suffragantur ei omnes episcopi. Quòd autem quædam exempla veteris ecclesiæ ab illâ formâ, quam antea proposuimus, aliquantulum discesserunt, inde factum est, quia pulcherrima illa symphonia episcoporum, magistratus & populi sæpius fuit ab hominibus malè feriatis turbata.
units.tr: Against what we have cited from the practice of the early Church concerning the authority of princes and people in choosing God's servants, they go on to say: But there are many examples in the history of the early Church by which the contrary can easily be proved, and the Emperor Valentinian handed that authority over to the clergy. Reply: the Roman pontiffs later greatly abused the moderation of pious princes. Moreover, the clergy acknowledged that the power of election rested with the Emperor; see c. 3, Valentinian, dist. 63. Likewise in Sozomen, bk. 7, ch. 7, the Emperor chooses Nazianzen in a synod, and all the bishops give their votes for him. That some examples of the early Church departed somewhat from the form we proposed earlier came about because that most beautiful harmony of bishops, magistrates and people was often disturbed by men of bad character.

units.la: Quæritur, An præsules Romani sint habendi in numero verorum ac fidorum servorum Christi: Romani pontificii affirmant. Orthodoxi Protestantes negant.
units.tr: The question is: Are the Roman prelates to be counted among the true and faithful servants of Christ? The Roman Papists affirm it. The orthodox Protestants deny it.

units.la: Orthodoxa sententia probatur iisdem argumentis, quibus demonstravimus pastorum & doctorū, qui sunt in ecclesiis Protestantium, ministerium esse legitimum.
units.tr: The orthodox view is proved by the same arguments by which we demonstrated that the ministry of the pastors and teachers in the churches of the Protestants is lawful.

units.la: Et docuimus
units.tr: And we have taught:

units.la: a Veros ac legitimos verbi Divini ministros habere Deū & Christum vocationis suæ auctorem.
units.tr: a that the true and lawful ministers of the divine Word have God and Christ as the author of their calling;

units.la: b Et coram Deo esse conscios sibi juxta scripturæ s. effata, quòd neque ambitione, neque ulla aliâ ꝑversâ cupiditate: sed sincero Dei timore, atque ædificandæ ecclesiæ studio episcopale munus desideret.
units.tr: b and that, before God, they are conscious to themselves, according to the sayings of Holy Scripture, that they desire the episcopal office neither from ambition nor from any other perverse desire, but from a sincere fear of God and a zeal for building up the Church;

units.la: c Præterea de Dei vocatione illos erudiri ac confirmari per vocē ecclesiæ.
units.tr: c and that they are taught and confirmed concerning God's calling by the voice of the Church.

units.la: Requi- [continues on the next page]
units.tr: Requi- [continues on the next page]

units.la: Requiri autem, ut sint sanæ doctrinæ & inculpatæ vitæ, simulq; ad docendum idonei, qui norint ἐλέγχειν[?] sermonem veritatis. 1 Tim. 3. 2. & seq.
units.tr: It is required, moreover, that they be sound in doctrine and blameless in life, and at the same time fit to teach, able to refute [ἐλέγχειν] the word of truth. 1 Tim. 3. 2 and following.

units.la: Ordinariè vocatos ab ecclesia ad munus suum exercendum deligi, confirmari & ordinari adhibito religioso timore, positis privatis affectibus, & diligeti tum vitæ tum doctrinæ examine præcunte.
units.tr: That those who are ordinarily called by the Church to exercise their office be chosen, confirmed and ordained with religious fear, with private affections set aside, and with a prior diligent examination both of life and of doctrine.

units.la: Electionem instituì non ab uno quopiam, proprio arbitratu, sed ab ecclesia, ejusq; presbyterio, & magistratu, si christianus est, non excluso populi consensu.
units.tr: That the election be carried out not by any one person at his own discretion, but by the Church, with its elders and magistrate (if he is a Christian), and not excluding the consent of the people.

units.la: Officium illorum esse, {1} pascere seu erudire populum puro Dei verbo, quod exstat in scripturis propheticis & apostolicis. {2} Administrare sacramenta ad præscriptum Christi. {3} Cum presbyteris invigilare, quantum possunt, disciplinæ spirituali & offendiculis cavendis.
units.tr: Their office is: (1) to feed, that is, to instruct, the people with the pure Word of God, which is contained in the prophetic and apostolic Scriptures; (2) to administer the sacraments according to the prescription of Christ; (3) to watch over, with the elders as far as they are able, spiritual discipline and the avoiding of stumbling-blocks.

units.la: Hoc fine ut oves per totum orbem [illegible, ~8 letters]orbem Christi tandem Conf[?] decorab[?] manifiqu[?] [illegible, ~6 letters] primi mini Ordin[?] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] [illegible, ~6 letters] Atq[?] [illegible, ~4 letters] orbem dispersæ ad pastorem suum Christum Jesum congregentur, & tandem salvi fiant.
units.tr: To this end, that the sheep, scattered through the whole world [illegible] of the world of Christ at last [illegible] first minister [illegible] [illegible] [illegible] and [illegible] scattered throughout the world may be gathered to their shepherd Christ Jesus and at last be saved.

units.la: Contrà præsules Romani dependent ab auctoritate pontificis Romani, qui est manifestus Christi & s. literarum hostis, sicuti demonstravimus prolixè in Medullâ papismi de auctoritate pontificis Romani.
units.tr: Moreover, the Roman prelates depend on the authority of the Roman pontiff, who is the manifest enemy of Christ and of the holy Scriptures, as we have demonstrated at length in the Medulla of Papism concerning the authority of the Roman pontiff.

units.la: Ordinationes instituuntur ad li-bitum cleri & juratorum sedis Romanæ. & cogitent illi ipsi, qui intersunt, quàm secure negligantur, contemnantur, violentur leges ex divino jure in electionibus præscri-ptæ, nec non, qui in jure illorum exstant, canones puriores.
units.tr: Ordinations are instituted at the pleasure of the clergy and the sworn men of the Roman see. And let those very men who take part consider how carelessly the laws prescribed in elections by divine right are neglected, despised and violated, and likewise the purer canons that exist in their law.

units.la: Præcipuum pastorum officium, quod est prædicare verbum Dei & administrare sacramenta ex insti-tuto Christi, pleriq; contemnunt, vel sanè raro admodum illud exer-cent.
units.tr: Most of them despise the principal duty of ministers, which is to preach the Word of God and to administer the sacraments according to the institution of Christ, or certainly exercise it very rarely.

units.la: Atque hunc finem sibi proposi-tum habent, ut traditiones ac commenta Romanę sedis eadem reuerentiâ iu[?] scipiantur, atque ipsa scriptura s. & pontifex cum suis conjuratis securè dominetur in Christi gregem: omitto autè quàm secure indulgeant omnis generis cupiditatibus carnis, omnisq; solutioris vitæ licentiam quærant.
units.tr: And they have this aim before them: that the traditions and inventions of the Roman see be received with the same reverence as Holy Scripture, and that the pontiff with his sworn associates may rule securely over the flock of Christ. I pass over how securely they indulge every kind of bodily lust and seek the licence of a more dissolute life.

units.la: Sed audiamus potius testimonia ipsorum pontificiorum.
units.tr: But let us rather hear the testimonies of the Papists themselves.

units.la: Episcopus Espensæus com. in Titum & in Timoth. digress. l. 2. cap. 2. & alibi, Quotusquisque prælatorum ma-jorum minorumve populum su-um docere videtur? certè ex nostratibus episcopis nemo per se docet: ludimus in re seriâ, ac potius decretorum specie reformatione poscentibus illudimus? Novi ex istis, qui ad istam docendi servitutem (generosi scilicet) se teneri præfractè negant: res nobis est cum iis, quibus nulli magis concilia, patres, ecclesiæ clamitant, & tamen functionem suam maximè sibi propriam & necessariam doctrinam abjiciunt: hos possem quæstioni-bus, tanquam tormentis, vexare: sed obtundis, inquiunt, tametsi in-telligimus; neque obtinebis, ut e-piscopi, quas theologastris & fra-terculis libenter concesimus, ca-thedras rursus conscendamus, vi-cariâ diligentiâ, contenti erimus. Item in 1. Tim. 3. Non concionantur pontifices multi, ita torporis ocio à lectionis gratiâ secluduntur, ut quid doctrinæ subditis gregibus exhibeant, præcones non inveni-ant, & Dei verbi fame populum perire sinant. Johannes Ferus com. in Matt. 16. Olim portenti instar ha-bitum fuit, si pro episcopo habere-tur, qui non etiam re ipsa verum & proprium episcopi munus exhibu-isset, quod hodie plusquam mon-stri loco habetur, si quis exhibeat: quos cum templorum natura, scrip-tura, ecclesia, concilia, pontifices, patres, cæsares, superi, inferi accu-sent damnentque, quis est qui ab-solvet: & paulo post. Ingenuè fateor, si Petri successores eodem modo uti fuissent potestate suâ, quo Petrus, nemo Christianus eam impugnasset. Acosta Iesuita de salute indorum l. 4. c. 15. Praeclarè verò ageretur, si sacerdotum ea saltem modestia esset, ut non solutioris vitae licentiam quaereret. Item paulo post. Quid verò dealeatoribus? populare est in sacerdotum domo, ludendum: Insomnes nocte sacra peragunt, idque tam cursim, ut mirum sit, eos pictas chartulas pro sacris paginis non referre. Item collapsa est scholastica disciplina omnis, idem & sacerdotes & praesules & monachi actitarunt.
units.tr: Bishop Espensaeus, commentary on Titus and on Timothy, digression bk. 2, ch. 2, and elsewhere: How few of the greater or lesser prelates seem to teach their people? Certainly none of our bishops teaches in person. Do we play games in a serious matter, and do we mock the reform demanded by the decrees? I know some of them who stubbornly deny that they are bound to this servitude of teaching (the noble gentlemen, of course). We have to do with men to whom councils, Fathers and churches cry out that nothing is more their own and necessary than teaching, and yet they cast off the very function most proper to them. I could vex these men with questions as with torments; but, they say, "you pester us, although we understand; and you will not get it that we bishops, whose chairs we have gladly conceded to theologasters and little friars, should climb back into them; we shall be content with vicarious diligence." Likewise on 1 Tim. 3: Many bishops do not preach; they are so shut away from reading by the idleness of sloth that they find no heralds to offer any teaching to the flocks under them, and they allow the people to perish from famine of God's Word. Johannes Ferus, commentary on Matt. 16: Formerly it was thought a monstrous thing if someone was regarded as a bishop who had not in fact exhibited the true and proper office of a bishop; today it is thought more than monstrous if someone does exhibit it. Whom the nature of the temples, Scripture, the Church, councils, pontiffs, Fathers, emperors, the upper and lower worlds accuse and condemn, who is there who will absolve them? And a little later: I frankly confess that if the successors of Peter had used their power in the same way as Peter, no Christian would have assailed it. Acosta the Jesuit, On the Salvation of the Indians, bk. 4, ch. 15: It would indeed be a fine thing if at least the priests had such moderation that they did not seek the licence of a more dissolute life. Likewise a little later: What of the gamblers? It is commonplace to play games in the priests' house. They perform the sacred rites through the night, and so hastily that it is a wonder they do not bring painted cards instead of the holy pages. Likewise: all scholastic discipline has collapsed; priests, prelates and monks have all acted in the same way.

units.la: Ecchius hom. 2. de festo Stephani. Nostrates praelati ordinem invertunt apostolicum, dum spiritualia graviora, quàm quae subeant, rati; in pontificalibus suffraganeorum, in judiciali officialium, in absolvendis poenitentiariorum ope utuntur, in praedicatione Monachum, nescio quem praeferunt, in aliis spi-
units.tr: Eck, homily 2 on the feast of Stephen. Our prelates invert the apostolic order, since they think the spiritual duties heavier than those they undertake: in pontifical matters they use the help of suffragans, in judicial matters the help of officials, in absolving penitentiaries; in preaching they put forward some monk or other, and in other spiritual matters they have vicars for the ritual duties. But if the matter concerns census and temporal things, the matter is to be referred to our Lord Bishop.

units.la: [?] ritualib[?] in re de[?] rus, res[?] Episcop[?] Depar[?] hesits[?] [illegible, ~10 letters] pruff[?] quibl fue[?] vulgus ex[?] timatert[?] nium [?] dan tem [illegible, ~12 letters] Item Plu[?] dubdecet[?] pauline[?] nahmalu[?] debar, fe[?] pontif[?] Quo[?] evange[?] vimus[?] [illegible, ~8 letters] ritualibus vicarios habent: sin qua in re de censu & temporalibus agi-tur, res hæc ad Dominum nostrum Episcopum referenda est.
units.tr: [illegible] in ritual matters [illegible] [illegible]; they have vicars for ritual matters. But if in any matter it concerns revenue and temporal affairs, this matter is to be referred to our Lord the Bishop. [illegible]

units.la: De pontificibus Romanis, qui & quales sint, diximus alias. Nunc audiamus Bellarminum. Hic ait l.4. de Rom. pontif. cap.14. de Johanne xxiii., quòd fuerit adeò dissoluta vitæ, ut vulgus existimaret, eum negare vitam æternam, & de Johanne xii l.2, cap.29. quòd fuerit pontificum omnium ferè deterrimus. De eodem testatur Franciscus de Victoria Relect. 2. Prop.23. Johannes xii. erat venator, lubricus & incorrigibilis. Item Platina in ejus vita. Homo aba-dolescētia[?] omnibus probris & turpitudine contaminatus; uni Cardinali nasum, alteri manum abscin-debat, sceleratissimus, vel monstrū potiùs.
units.tr: As to the Roman pontiffs, what sort they are and who, we have said elsewhere. Now let us hear Bellarmine. He says, bk. 4 on the Roman Pontiff, ch. 14, of John XXIII, that he was of so dissolute a life that the common people thought he denied eternal life; and of John XII, bk. 2, ch. 29, that he was almost the worst of all the pontiffs. Francisco de Victoria bears witness to the same in Relectio 2, Prop. 23: John XII was a hunter, slippery and incorrigible. Likewise Platina in his life: a man stained from youth with every disgrace and baseness; he cut off the nose of one cardinal and the hand of another; most wicked, or rather a monster.

units.la: Quàm graviter etiam à veritate euangelica aberraverint, annota-vimus in Medulla papismi pag. 297 & seq. aliquot.
units.tr: We have noted some of the ways in which they strayed from the evangelical truth, more gravely, in the Marrow of Papism, pp. 297 and following.

units.la: Quanta autem inter illos fue-rint odia & dissidia, non minùs li-quet ex historiis. Bellarminus l. 4. de Rom. pontific. cap. 9. §. post biennium, confitetur Liberium pontificem ordinasse haereticos Arianos ministros.
units.tr: How great the hatreds and dissensions among them were is no less clear from histories. Bellarmine, bk. 4 on the Roman Pontiff, ch. 9, §. after two years, admits that the pontiff Liberius ordained Arian heretics as ministers.

units.la: Apud Platinam legitur, quòd Stephanus VI. pontifex tanto odio sa-vierit in corpus Formosi pontificis mortui, ut digitos ejus abscinderet. Stephano successit Romanus, atqui hic omnia acta Stephani abrogavit.
units.tr: We read in Platina that Pope Stephen VI raged with such hatred against the corpse of the dead Pope Formosus that he cut off its fingers. Stephen was succeeded by Romanus, and yet this man annulled all the acts of Stephen.

units.la: Post Romanum Sergius Pontifex creatus, causam Formosi restituit. Sergius Papa acta Formosi improbavit.
units.tr: After Romanus, Sergius was created pope and restored the cause of Formosus. Pope Sergius disapproved of the acts of Formosus.

units.la: De Monachis audi denuo Episcopum Ephesinum com. in Tim. digress. 13. c. 12. Erant olim coenobia & collegia & exercitationes, in quibus orationi lectio, lectioni succedebat oratio &c. Nunc vix vicesimum quodq; coenobium literatorium invenies: hodierno tempore malunt haec eversa penitus quam ad originem reversa, Item in fine capitis. Hos autem, qui ventri obedientes sunt, animalium loco numeremus, an hominum? Imo quosdam ne ani-malium quidem, sed mortuorum: vivit enim, qui multis usui est, qui vero latitant & torpent, sic in cellula sunt, quomodo in conditivo; ocium enim sine literis mors est, & vivi hominis sepultura. Cassander libr.consult.art.25. Quàm longè Mo-nachatus hodie à primâ suâ origine degenerauit[?], & quantis abusib. contaminatus & deformatus sit, satis per se manifestû est: nam paulatim religio vera & solida in super-stitionem & inanem speciem religionis conversa est, & accrescentibus opibus decrevit pietas, & in ejus locum larvæ cerimoniarum suc-cesserunt, in quibus verae pietatis operibus neglectis, summa totius religionis constituta sit. Item Manent adhuc vestigia communis ac canonicæ vitæ; sed in edificiis ac no-minibus tantum: alii absurdo monstroso nomine canonici secu-lares dicuntur, hoc est, regulares, irregulares dici coeperunt: quae haud injuriâ Albertus Cranzius ca-nonicum secularem vocat mon-strum sine exemplo; Regularem si-ne regulâ; canonicum sine canone: Deniq; audiatur Petrus de Aliaco Car-dinalis Cameracensis, de reformat. eccle-sia, cap. de reform. religion. Primò, in-quit, videtur, quòd tanta religiosō-rum numerositas & varietas nō ex-pediat: quae inducit ad varietatem morum & quandoq; ad contrarie-tatem & repugnantiam observatio-num, & lape [?] ad singularitatem & superbiam, & ad vanam extollen-tiam unius statûs super alium. Et maximè videtur necessarium, quòd diminuerentur religiones ordinū mendicantium: quia tot sunt, & in numero conventuum, & in numero suppositorum, ut eorum statûs sit onerosus hominibus, damnosus leprosoriis & hospitalibus, ac aliis verè pauperibus & miserabilibus indigentibus (quibus convenit[?]us & verus titulus mendicandi) ipsis quoq; curatis parochialibus : & si bene consideretur, etiam præjudi-cialis omnibus ecclesię statibus, & spiritualiter hujusmodi religiosis intolerabilis, & eorum professioni contrarius.
units.tr: Concerning the monks, hear again the Bishop of Ephesus, on 1 Timothy, digression 13, chapter 12: "There were once monasteries, colleges and exercises, in which prayer followed reading and reading followed prayer, and so on. Now you will scarcely find one monastery in twenty devoted to learning. In our day men prefer to see these things utterly overthrown rather than restored to their origin." Likewise, at the end of the chapter: "Should we count those who obey their bellies among the animals, or among men? Indeed some of them are not even animals but dead. For he lives who is of use to many; but those who lurk and grow numb sit in their cells as in a storeroom, for leisure without letters is death and the burial of a living man." Cassander, Consultation, article 25: "How far monasticism has today degenerated from its first origin, and how much it has been defiled and deformed by abuses, is plain enough in itself. For little by little true and solid religion was turned into superstition and an empty show of religion; as wealth increased, piety declined, and in its place the masks of ceremonies took over, while the works of true piety were neglected and the sum of the whole of religion was placed in them." Likewise: "Traces of common and canonical life still remain, but only in buildings and names. Others, by an absurd and monstrous name, are called secular canons, that is, regulars; the irregulars have begun to be so called." Albert Cranz rightly calls the secular canon a monster without precedent: a regular without a rule, a canon without a canon. Finally, let us hear Peter d'Ailly, Cardinal of Cambrai, On the Reform of the Church, chapter on the reform of religious orders: "First, it seems that so great a number and variety of religious is not expedient. It leads to variety of customs and sometimes to contrariety and conflict of observances, and sometimes to singularity and pride, and to the vain exaltation of one rank above another. And it seems especially necessary that the religious orders of the mendicant friars be reduced, for there are so many of them, both in the number of convents and in the number of members, that their condition is burdensome to men, damaging to lazar-houses and hospitals and to other truly poor and wretched needy people (to whom the true title of begging belongs), and even to the parish priests themselves. And if it is rightly considered, it is also prejudicial to all the estates of the Church, intolerable to such religious spiritually, and contrary to their profession."

units.la: Plura de vita & votis Monacho-rum ac sacrificulorum vide suis lo-cis. Equidem sunt ex traditione merè humanâ: vovent inconsi-derate & pugnantia cū voluntate Dei: puta ipsum Monachatum, & mul-tos impios cultus, aliaq; quæ in co-rum manu nō sunt ut præstent vid. virginitatem perpetuam ; inediam toto vitæ cursu, & similia.
units.tr: More about the life and vows of monks and priests, see in their places. Indeed these are purely of human tradition. They vow rashly and in conflict with the will of God: for example, monasticism itself, and many impious cults, and other things which are not in their power to perform, such as perpetual virginity, fasting throughout the whole course of life, and the like.

units.la: Postremum ad Jesuitas necessum est progrediamur, de quibus extat integri tractatus, &, si velis consule Sorbonam Parisiensium, & histo-rias Gallicanas. Reperies, quòd cu-ria Parisiensis & Parlamentū, quod vocant, illos accusarit insatiabilis ambitionis atq; avaritiæ, item eos conconjurationes plus quam Catilina-rias exercere, infames quoscunq; & scelleratos[?] ad societatem suâ ad-mittere ; Ordinariis obedientiam subtrahere, multas in utraq; politia rebelliones & schismata inducere, magis ad ecclesiæ destructionem quàm ædificationem facere, ideoq; tam à curiâ, quam à Sorbonâ esse e-jectos. Vide Benedicti Ariæ Montani (qui fuit non solùm Romanus catholicus, sed etiam Hispanus) ju-dicium & vaticinium de Jesuitis, q; exstat in Bibliis interlinearibus, editis Antwerpiæ ann. 1584. Item Arestum supremæ curiæ Parisiensis incisum aureis literis pyramidi ex ni-gro marmore exstructæ Lutetiæ, quam multa millia testium omni exceptione majorum suis oculis viderunt, palparunt, legerunt, licet tandem ad Jesuitarum preces sit lo-co remota. Plura etiam petito ex oratione ad regem Christianissimū perscriptâ, de restitutione Jesui-tarum in regno Galliæ.
units.tr: Last, we must proceed to the Jesuits, about whom there is a whole treatise; and, if you wish, consult the Sorbonne of Paris and the Gallican histories. You will find that the Parisian court and the so-called Parlement accused them of insatiable ambition and avarice; likewise that they carry on conspiracies more than Catilinarian, admit to their society any infamous and wicked persons, withdraw obedience from the ordinaries, stir up many rebellions and schisms in both polities, and do more to destroy the Church than to build it; and for this reason they were expelled both by the court and by the Sorbonne. See the judgment and prophecy of Benedictus Arias Montanus (who was not only a Roman Catholic but also a Spaniard) about the Jesuits, which is found in the Interlinear Bibles published at Antwerp in 1584. Likewise the Arrest of the Supreme Court of Paris, engraved in golden letters on a pyramid built of black marble at Paris, which many thousands of witnesses, beyond any exception, have seen with their own eyes, touched and read, although at last it was removed from that place at the Jesuits' request. More may also be sought from the oration addressed to the most Christian king, written concerning the restoration of the Jesuits in the kingdom of France.

units.la: Refutatio objectionum pontificiarum.
units.tr: Refutation of the papist objections.

units.la: PLerasque attigimus in Medulla papismi, ubi egimus de pontifice, ecclesia, & doctoribus, comprimis vero de ecclesia Romana. Similiter aliquot notavimus in quæstione proximè præcedenti de doctoribus protestantium. At ut quæ instituimus ordinem felicius prosequamur, quasdam præterea adversariorum objectiones annotabimus.
units.tr: We have touched on many points in the Marrow of Papism, where we treated of the pope, the Church and teachers, and especially of the Roman Church. Similarly, in the immediately preceding question, we noted several things about the teachers of the Protestants. But so that we may follow the order we have begun more happily, we shall further note some objections of our opponents.

units.la: Primo multis prædicant legitimam ad ministerium vocationem per successionem ordinariam, & publicam ejus declarationem atq; approbationem: Item, ajunt, Deum illos demum, qui legitimè sunt vocati, donis suis ornare, perq; ministerium illorum efficacem esse, ex 2.Cor.3. 2.Tim.1. & similibus locis. &c. At ex præcedentibus liquet, nihil hinc concludi adversus protestantes, neutiquam etiam inde confirmari sedē doctorum Romanensium: quia illi sunt legitimè ad munus suum obeundum vocati, & revera sese pro-bant Dei servos; hi vero dependent à solius pontificis auctoritate, & officium pastorum ecclesiæ pror-sus negligunt. {2} Præsules Romanenses gaudere successione [?] perpetua Resp. Quod dictum est antea, exigitur comprimis successio in doctrina. vide supr. pa.161. {3} Irenæum & alios Patres ex successione veros Dei servos demonstrari velle. Resp. Patrum auctoritate movemur, quatenus s. scripturæ conveniunt. Deinde re-sponsum est antea, nō suffiecere suc-cessionem personæ. Denique audi Bellarminum l. 4. de eccles. militant. c. 8. §. Dico secundo. quum ait, Hoc argu-mentum à legitimā successione du-ctum, non necessariò probare ibi esse ecclesiam, ubi est successio. Ita[?] teste Episcopo Espensæo com. in Tim. digress. libr. 2. pag. 290. Photius homo profanus substitutus est Ignatio legitimo patriarchæ per auctoritatem pseudosynodi. Quo modis autem successio dissoluta est apud Roma-nenses{1} nensis? per quàm multàs hæresès per pontificum irruptiones, per muneris ecclesiastici contemtum, & id genus alia? + Reliquas ecclesias patriarchales[?] habuisse quidem episcopos manifestè hæreticos, ac proinde interrup-ta apud illos esse veterum pastorum suc-cessionem. In Romana autem contrarium videri. Resp. Paulo ante docuimus, quid testentur ipsi Iesuitæ de pon-tificibus. Si vis, adde plura: Zephi-rinus pontifex montanizavit. Li-berius pontifex fuit hæreticus, neque legitur conversus ad fidem. Cœlestinus Papa fuit infectus hæ-resi Nestorii. Honorius similiter fuit Montanista, eumq; plures sy-nodi & tres Papæ hæresis damna-runt. Omitto quod Romanus Pon-tificatum vi adeptus fuerit: Boni-facius dolo ac fraude. Formosus si-moniâ. Nihil etiam dicam de no-bilissimo scorto Joanna foemina, quæ sedem Romanam similiter te-nuisse scribitur. testes si petas, pro-ducuntur Rhenanus in argumentTertull. adversus Praxeam, Platina, Melchior Canus loc. theol. l.6, c.8. Alphonsus de Castro li.1. de haeref.c.4.& alii. 5 Figmentum esse, quod dicitur de Ioanna & aliis. Resp. Aliter judicant praestantiores ex doctoribus pontificiis, quos con-sule.
units.tr: First, they proclaim in many places a lawful calling to the ministry through ordinary succession, and its public declaration and approval. Likewise, they say, God at last adorns with his gifts those who have been lawfully called, and through their ministry is effective, from 2 Cor. 3, 2 Tim. 1 and similar places, etc. But from what has gone before it is clear that nothing is concluded from this against the Protestants, and in no way is the seat of the Roman teachers thereby confirmed: because the former are lawfully called to discharge their office and in fact prove themselves servants of God, whereas the latter depend only on the authority of the pope and utterly neglect the duty of the pastors of the Church. {2} The Roman prelates rejoice in perpetual succession. Reply: What was said before requires succession above all in doctrine. See above, p. 161. {3} They wish to show by the authority of Irenaeus and other Fathers that they are true servants of God by succession. Reply: We are moved by the authority of the Fathers insofar as it agrees with Holy Scripture. Then it was answered before that succession of person does not suffice. Finally, hear Bellarmine, On the Church Militant, book 4, chapter 8, §"I say secondly", where he says that this argument drawn from lawful succession does not necessarily prove that the Church is where there is succession. Thus, according to Bishop Espencaeus, commentary on 1 Timothy, digression, book 2, p. 290, Photius, a profane man, was substituted for the lawful patriarch Ignatius by the authority of a pseudo-synod. But in what ways has succession been broken among the Romans, and through how many heresies, through the invasions of popes, through contempt of the ecclesiastical office, and things of that kind? + The other patriarchal churches indeed had bishops manifestly heretical, and therefore the succession of the old pastors was interrupted among them. In the Roman church, however, the contrary seems to be the case. Reply: A little before we showed what the Jesuits themselves bear witness about the popes. If you wish, add more: Zephyrinus the pope became a Montanist. Liberius the pope was a heretic, nor is it read that he was converted to the faith. Pope Celestine was infected with the heresy of Nestorius. Honorius likewise was a Montanist, and several synods and three popes condemned him for heresy. I pass over the fact that the Roman pontiff obtained the papacy by force, Boniface by guile and fraud, Formosus by simony. I will say nothing of the most noble harlot, the woman Joan, who is likewise written of as having held the Roman see. If you seek witnesses, there are produced Rhenanus in his argument against Tertullian's Against Praxeas, Platina, Melchior Cano, Loci theologici book 6, chapter 8, Alphonsus de Castro, book 1 On Heresies, chapter 4, and others. {5} It is a fiction, what is said about Joan and others. Reply: The more eminent of the papist teachers judge otherwise; consult them.

units.la: 6 Propter gloriam Dei, honorem ministerii, solamen ministrorum, & salutem populi, necessariam esse legitimam & ordinariam vocationem. Resp. Ita est: at si legitima requiritur, ergo non pontificia: sed quae convenit praescripto verbi divini, quamq; explicuimus antea. 7 Hac successionis nota, quod episcopi sine interruptione originem suam ad apostolos ducere queant semper usos fuisse nostros majores adversus haereticos. Resp. Est crambe toties recocta. Quamdiu viguit doctrinae successio, recte illud factum est, at apud Romanenses est doctrina vitiata. 8 Auctoritatem praesulum Romanorum non raro confirmari multis & vere divinis miraculis. Resp. De his docetur commodiùs suo loco paulo post, rectius autem facturi essent præsules Romani, si doctrinâ & vitâ probarent se fidos Dei servos. ¶[?] E-tiam doctrinâ & vitæ sanctimoniâ eos excellere. Resp. Non sufficit autem laus propria. Sed audiatur Franciscus de Victoria, Relect. 5. prop. § 1 [?] Non satis, inquit, mihi liquet, an barbaris Indis fides christiana itaâ nobis propositâ fuerit & annunciata, ut teneantur credere, nam miracula & signa nulla audio, nec exempla vitæ adeo religiosa; Imò contrà multa scandala, & multas impietates. Plura de pietate præsulum Romanorum annotavimus paulò ante. Et sanè quæ illorum pietas? etiam quæ propriè spectât munus servorum Dei, secure negligunt, puta ministerium verbi, & sacramentorum administrationē, quod similiter annotavimus antea.
units.tr: 6 Because of the glory of God, the honour of the ministry, the comfort of ministers and the salvation of the people, a lawful and ordinary calling is necessary. Reply: So it is; but if a lawful calling is required, then it is not a papal one, but one that agrees with the prescription of the divine Word, which we explained before. 7 This mark of succession, that bishops can trace their origin without interruption to the apostles, shows that our forebears always used it against heretics. Reply: This is cabbage reheated so often. As long as the succession of doctrine flourished, that was rightly done; but among the Romanists the doctrine is corrupted. 8 The authority of the Roman prelates is not seldom confirmed by many truly divine miracles. Reply: These things are taught more fitly in their own place shortly after; but the Roman prelates would act more rightly if they proved by doctrine and life that they are faithful servants of God. ¶ That they excel also in doctrine and holiness of life. Reply: Their own praise is not enough. But let us hear Francisco de Victoria, Relectio 5, prop. §1: "It is not sufficiently clear to me," he says, "whether the Christian faith has been so set before and announced to the barbarian Indians that they are bound to believe; for I hear of no miracles or signs, nor of examples of so religious a life; rather, on the contrary, many scandals and many impieties." We noted more about the piety of the Roman prelates a little before. And indeed, what piety is theirs? Even what properly belongs to the office of the servants of God they securely neglect, namely the ministry of the Word and the administration of the sacraments, which we likewise noted before.

units.la: 10 Non opus esse, ut ipsi doceant populū, &c. sed satis esse, si curent illa ab aliis præstari. Item; licèt non concionentur pontifices & alii ex praesulibus Romanis, tamen eos exercere multos alios actus pastorales; ligando, solvendo, controversias diiudicando: praeterea facere per alios, quod per se concionando facere nequeunt. Resp. Hujusmodi potestatem vel potius licentiam non permittunt literae. Audi etiam Maldonatum Jesuitam in summul. qu. 10. artic. 3. 5. 6. Notarunt, inquit, Hieronymus & Augustinus, propterea Paulum nō distinxisse pastores & doctores, quia omnis potestas debet docere, & nomen pastoris significat actionem personalem, sicut nomen medici. Itaq; sicut nemo potest per alium curare, ita nemo potest suas oves per alium pascere. nec quic-quam valet responsio communis, satis esse per vicarium laborare, quia secundum eandem regulam satis esset manducare per vicariū: quia scriptum est. Qui non laborat, non manducet. Quibus assentitur Episcopus Espensaeus com. in Tit. 1. & 1. ad Tim. digress. l. 2. c. 23. Adjecit, inquit apostolus, quod est episcopo pro-prium, aptum esse ad docendum: & Hieronymus, si quis, inquit, plebe sibi sub ectam non instruit, nec a-postolus, nec propheta, nec epi-scopus, nec pastor est appellandus. Similia leguntur apud alios.
units.tr: 10 That it is not necessary for them to teach the people themselves, and that it is enough if they see that these things are provided by others. Likewise: although the popes and other Roman prelates do not preach, they still perform many other pastoral acts, by binding, absolving and deciding controversies; moreover they cause others to do what they cannot do by preaching themselves. Reply: the letters of Scripture do not grant this power, or rather licence. Hear also Maldonatus the Jesuit, in Summula, question 10, articles 3, 5 and 6. He observes, says he, that Jerome and Augustine noted that Paul therefore did not distinguish pastors and teachers, because every pastor ought to teach, and the name pastor signifies a personal action, just as the name physician does. So just as no one can take care of a patient through another, so no one can feed his sheep through another. Nor does the common answer avail, that it is enough to labour through a deputy, for by the same rule it would be enough to eat through a deputy, since it is written: He who does not work shall not eat. Bishop Espencaeus agrees with these, in his commentary on Titus 1 and 1 Timothy, digression, book 2, chapter 23. The apostle, he says, added what is proper to a bishop, namely to be apt for teaching; and Jerome: if anyone, he says, does not instruct the people committed to him, he is to be called neither apostle, nor prophet, nor bishop, nor pastor. Similar things are read in others.

units.la: De miraculis pontificiorum.
units.tr: On the miracles of the Papists

units.la: QUÆritur: An miracula, quæ proferuntur à Romanensibus, demonstrent, illorum ecclesia esse veram sponsam Christi, eorumq; prae-sules veros ac legitimos Dei servos: ac proinde audiendos? Romani pontif. affirmant, Orthodoxi Protestantes negant.
units.tr: The question is: Do the miracles that are put forward by the Romanists prove that their Church is the true bride of Christ, and that their prelates are true and lawful servants of God, and therefore that they are to be heard? The Roman pontiffs affirm it; the orthodox Protestants deny it.

units.la: Orthodoxa thesis probatur. Nam Exod.7.14.25. & 8.8. legitur Ægyp-tios magos suis incantationibus edidisse miracula. Matth.7.22.23. Testatur Christus, multos sibi dicturos in die illo, Domine, nonne per nomen tuum prophetavimus, & per nomen tuum daemonia eje-cimus, & per nomen tuum multas virtutes edidimus? Dominum autem professurum eis, Nunquam novi vos, discedite à me, qui operamini iniquitatem. 2 Thess. 2. 9. 10. & seq. de antichristo dicitur: Cujus adventus est in efficacia Satanæ cū omni potentiâ & signis ac prodigiis mendacibus, & cum omni fraude injustitiæ; in iis, qui pereunt, pro eo quòd nomen veritatis non receperunt, ut salvi fierent. Matth. 24.24. 25. disertis verbis Dominus præmunivit omnes, ne de veritate doctrinæ aut ecclesiæ ex miraculis judicaremus, quum ait, pseudoprophetæ edent signa magna & miracula, ita ut seducant, si fieri possit, etiam electos. ecce prædixi vobis. apoc.13.13.14. similiter dicitur de bestiâ. Et facit signa magna, adeo ut etiam ignem faciat de cœlo descendere in terram in conspectu hominum: & seducit incolas terræ propter signa, quæ datum est ei ut faciat. Illustris etiam est locus Deut.13 1. & seq. unde liquet Deum interdum pro suâ justitiâ ita laxare Satanæ enæ ejusque mancipiis habenas.
units.tr: The orthodox thesis is proved. For in Exodus 7:14, 25 and 8:8 we read that the Egyptian magicians produced miracles by their incantations. In Matthew 7:22–23 Christ testifies that many will say to him in that day, Lord, have we not prophesied in your name, and cast out devils in your name, and done many mighty works in your name? And that the Lord will profess to them: I never knew you; depart from me, you who work iniquity. In 2 Thessalonians 2:9–10 and following it is said of Antichrist: whose coming is after the working of Satan, with all power and signs and lying wonders, and with all deceit of unrighteousness, among those who perish, because they did not receive the love of the truth, that they might be saved. In Matthew 24:24–25 the Lord warned everyone in plain words not to judge the truth of doctrine or of the Church from miracles, when he says: false prophets will show great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if possible, even the elect. Behold, I have told you beforehand. Revelation 13:13–14 says the same of the beast: it does great signs, so that it even makes fire come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men, and it deceives the inhabitants of the earth by the signs that it has been given power to do. The passage in Deuteronomy 13:1 and following is also clear, from which it is plain that God sometimes, in his justice, gives free rein to Satan and his servants.

units.la: Hinc itaq; manifestum est quòd etiam instrumenta Satanæ, pseudoprophetæ, pseudochristi, & pseudodoctores interdum edant vera miracula. Itaq; non necessariò demonstrant veram ecclesiam & veros Christi servos.
units.tr: Hence it is therefore manifest that even the instruments of Satan, false prophets, false Christs and false teachers, sometimes perform true miracles. Therefore miracles do not necessarily demonstrate the true Church and the true servants of Christ.

units.la: Deinde sæpius deprehensum est, miracula Romanensium esse meras præstigias: si quæ autem videantur illorum esse miracula, speciem seu apparentiam tantùm habent, at vel formâ seu differentia miraculorum verâ destituuntur. Ea autem est modus omnem vim creatam excedens,& finis quoq;, qui divinis & proprie dictis miraculis est propositus, ab illis operibus abest, non enim fiunt virtute supernaturali, sed aut sunt dæmoniorũ fallacię, aut opera naturalib. causis pdu-cta[?], at pierisq; occulta eorum producendorum ratio: & ad mendacé doctrinam stabiliendam referuntur.
units.tr: Further, it has been found very often that the miracles of the Romanists are mere trickery; and if any of them seem to be miracles, they have only the semblance or appearance, and they lack the true form or character of genuine miracles. Moreover, the manner of them surpasses all created power, and the end too, which is proposed for true and properly so-called miracles, is absent from those works. For they are not done by supernatural power, but are either the deceptions of demons, or works produced by natural causes; and for most of them the method of producing them is hidden. And they are referred to establishing a lying doctrine.

units.la: Deniq; miracula ex doctrinâ iudicanda sunt, non contrà Joh 5.39.
units.tr: Finally, miracles are to be judged from doctrine, not the reverse; see John 5:39.

units.la: Quod si vero placet inquirere, quæ & qualia Romanenses proferant miracula, constabit ex inspectione Legendarum aliorumq; scriptorum pontificiorum, omnia fa-bulis, superstitione atq; extrema im-pietate redundare. Legatur liber conformitatum vitæ beati ac Seraphici patris Francisci. Exempli gratia, quod l.2. conformit. exstat. Clara multis & magnis claret si-gnis cujus corpus est integrum & capilli capitis & ungues ita cre-scunt sibi ac si viveret: Dicent Medici, illud naturâ contingere posse. Similiter arte humanâ eve-nit, quòd Franciscus ovem ita instruxit, ut ecclesiam vel templum ingrediens sine alicujus sermone flecteret genua, atq; ante altare vir-ginis voce balatus emitteret, quasi eam salutare gestiret. Ita etiam pi-ætæ[?] imagines invocantibus distillarunt guttas roris & unguentorum, quibus morbi sanati; atq; imagines læsæ ultæ sunt contemtores suos.
units.tr: But if indeed we wish to inquire what and what sort of miracles the Romanists put forward, it will be clear from inspecting the Legends and other Popish writings that everything overflows with fables, superstition and extreme impiety. Let the Book of Conformities of the life of the blessed and Seraphic father Francis be read. For example, what is found in book 2 of the Conformities: a body famous for many great signs is whole, and the hair of the head and the nails grow as if it were alive. The doctors will say that this can happen by nature. In the same way it happens by human art that Francis trained a sheep so that, entering a church or temple, it bent its knees without anyone's word, and before the altar of the Virgin it uttered a bleat, as if it were eager to greet her. So too painted images dripped drops of dew and ointments on those who invoked them, by which the sick were healed; and images that were injured took vengeance on their despisers.

units.la: Ex quibus dilucidè apparet, quę sint Romanensium studia; quodq; nihil aliud quaerāt productione miraculorum, quàm ut crassas suas superstitiones[?][?], imaginum cultus & adorationes, purgatorium, Missas, indulgentias & id genus alia homi-nibus persuadeant, atq; etiam contradicentibus obtrudant.
units.tr: From these things it is clearly apparent what the aims of the Romanists are; and that they seek nothing else by the production of miracles than to persuade men of their gross superstitions, the worship and adoration of images, purgatory, Masses, indulgences and other things of that kind, and even to force them upon those who contradict them.

units.la: Progrediamur ad patres. Miracula necessaria erant, ut crederet mundus, sed, qui nunc quaerit miraculum, postquam mundus credidit, magnum est ipse prodigium. Observandum est, quòd operari virtutes dicantur illi, qui nō tenent euangelii veritatem &c. hoc dico adversum hæreticos, qui probationem esse fidei suæ ex eo, si signum aliquod fecerint, arbitrantur.
units.tr: Let us proceed to the Fathers. Miracles were necessary so that the world might believe; but he who now seeks a miracle, after the world has believed, is himself a great portent. It must be observed that those are said to work virtues who do not hold the truth of the gospel, etc. I say this against the heretics, who think that the proof of their faith is that they have performed some sign.

units.la: Miraculorum operatio magis apud eos invenitur, qui sunt falsi chri-stiani. stiani. Tertullianus præscript. cap. 44. Quasi hoc non sit scriptum, ventu-ros esse qui maximas virtutes edent ad corrumpendam veritatem.
units.tr: The working of miracles is found more among those who are false Christians. Tertullian, Prescription, chapter 44. As if it were not written that there would come those who would work the greatest virtues to corrupt the truth.

units.la: Denig, adjiciamus testimonia pontifi-ciorum. Maldonatus Jesuita com. in Matt. 7, Chrysostom{9}, Hieronym{9}, & alii probant exemplis, etiam per alios quàm catholicos vera miracula fieri: & hoc ipso loco facile colligitur, falsos illos prophetas, de quibus Christus loquitur, vera miracula fecisse, verè prophetasse, verè dæmonia ejecisse: nec enim respondet Christus mentiri eos; sed se eos, quamvis ista fecerint, non nosse: nec magnum est, si moneret nos, ut falsa miracula facientibus non crederemus, sed magnum & admirabile est, omnino quod monet, ne falsis prophetis credamus vera etiam miracula facientibus.
units.tr: Finally, let us add the testimonies of the Papists. The Jesuit Maldonatus, in his commentary on Matthew 7, Chrysostom{9}, Jerome{9} and others prove by examples that true miracles are also done through persons other than Catholics; and from this very passage it is easily gathered that those false prophets, of whom Christ speaks, performed true miracles, truly prophesied, and truly cast out devils. For Christ does not answer that they lied, but that he did not know them, although they did these things. Nor would it be a great thing if he warned us not to believe those who perform false miracles; but it is great and admirable that he warns us altogether not to believe false prophets who perform even true miracles.

units.la: Pererius Jesuita com. in Exod. 7. disp. 11. Admonemur, ne turbemur prodigiis impiorum, quasi illa essent miracula, & divinæ virtutis testimonia: nia: quia propriū Diaboli est trans-figurare se in angelum lucis ad cir-cumveniendos mortales. Episcopus Roffensis de cap. Babil. adversus Luthe-rum c.10.part.4. Promisit Christus, ut discipuli dæmonia eijcerent,quà promissionem nullum his diebus effectum sortiri dilucidè cernimus: nemo enim est, qui nunc corpora-liter dæmonia ejicit,aut morbos sa-nat, & tamen minimè ambigimus, quin plurimi sint, qui fidem eandè & æquè magnam cum priscis fide-libus habeant,nec tamen inanis illa promissio fuit, quam noluit effica-ciam habere perpetuam, sed pro tempore nascentis & adolescentis ecclesiæ, vide etiā Acostæ testimo-nium supra in loco de doctoribus Protestantium. objeƈt.15.
units.tr: The Jesuit Pererius, in his commentary on Exodus 7, disputation 11. We are warned not to be disturbed by the portents of the impious, as if they were miracles and testimonies of divine power; for it is peculiar to the Devil to transform himself into an angel of light to circumvent mortals. The Bishop of Rochester, on the chapter of Babylon against Luther, chapter 10, part 4. Christ promised that the disciples would cast out devils; we clearly see that this promise has no effect in these days, for no one now casts out devils bodily or heals diseases. Yet we do not doubt in the least that there are very many who have the same faith, and an equally great faith, with the earlier believers; nor was that promise empty, but it was not willing to have a perpetual efficacy, rather it was for the time of the nascent and growing Church. See also the testimony of Acosta above, in the place about the teachers of the Protestants.

units.la: Refutatio argumentorum pon-tificiorum.
units.tr: Refutation of the Papists' arguments.

units.la: Aiunt: Ex Marc.16.20. & simi-libus locis constare [?], quòd miracula & revelationes divinæ veritatem confir-ment. Resp. At verò ad lydium s. literarum lapidem sunt exploranda, an fe, sint vera miracula, & san-ctæ revelationes, & notabitur illud apostoli Gal. 1. 8. Si nos vel angelus e cœlo euangelizet vobis praeter id, quod vobis euangelizavimus, ana-thema esto. Itaq; licet revelationes & miracula possint dici notæ sectu-dariæ doctorum: tamen primaria & certior est doctrinæ sanctitas, quæ consistit in consensu cum Literis.
units.tr: They say: From Mark 16:20 and similar passages it is clear that miracles and divine revelations confirm the truth. Reply: Indeed, miracles and holy revelations must be tested by the touchstone of Holy Scripture, to see whether they are true, and the apostle's words in Gal. 1:8 must be noted: "If we, or an angel from heaven, preach to you anything other than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed." So although revelations and miracles may be called secondary marks of teachers, the primary and more certain mark is the holiness of the doctrine, which consists in agreement with the Scriptures.

units.la: ² A prophetis & viris sanctis miracula edita esse in testimonium sanctitatis, tum doctrinæ, tum vitæ. Item ad muneris et prophetiæ suæ veritatem ab adversariorum ludibrio et injuriis vindicanda. Ita celebre esse illud Eliæ 2. Reg. 1. 10. Si homo Dei ego sum, descendat ignis de cœlo, et devoret te et quinquaginta tuos. Resp. Probandum vero est tantum à prophetis veris edi miracula, nam Literæ atq; experientia testantur etiam à pseudoprophetis sæpius illud fieri.
units.tr: 2 Miracles were wrought by the prophets and holy men as a testimony to their holiness, both of doctrine and of life; likewise to vindicate the truth of their office and prophecy against the mockery and insults of their opponents. Thus the famous passage of Elijah is 2 Kings 1:10: "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and devour you and your fifty." Reply: It must be proved that miracles were wrought only by true prophets, for Scripture and experience testify that false prophets also do this quite often.

units.la: ³ Tit. 1. 1. Deum esse mentiri nescium, ac proinde nunquam perhibere testimonium mendacio. & Antea demonstravimus, quod Deus etiam Satanam nam & ejus ministros aliquando si-nat falsa miracula & signa edere, vel ad suos probandos, vel ad verbi contemtores puniendos. 4 Pharisa-eos similiter damnasse miracula Christi et apostolorum. 5 Impie sane: quia omnia miracula Christi atq; apostolorum fuerunt, vere miracula divina, & ad literarum doctrinā confirmandam edita; at quae Romanenses vendicant, commendantur ad patrocinium erroris & doctrinam verbo Dei repugnantem, complura sunt vel vi daemonis vel arte humana effecta, multa etiam conficta ad fallendum simpliciores. Legantur aurea Legenda, Antonini episcopi historia de Dominico, Francisco, & similibus: Legenda Bonaventurae cardinalis, & similes Monachorum libelli.
units.tr: 3 Titus 1:2 says that God cannot lie, and therefore never bears witness to a falsehood. And we have shown above that God sometimes allows Satan, and his ministers too, to perform false miracles and signs, either to test his own people or to punish those who despise the Word. 4 The Pharisees likewise condemned the miracles of Christ and the apostles. 5 Surely this is impious: for all the miracles of Christ and the apostles were truly divine miracles, wrought to confirm the doctrine of the Scriptures. But those which the Romanists claim are put forward in defence of error and of a doctrine opposed to the Word of God. Many of them were done either by the power of the devil or by human art, and many were invented to deceive the simpler folk. Let people read the Golden Legend, the history of Antoninus, bishop, concerning Dominic, Francis and similar figures, the Legend of Bonaventure the cardinal, and similar little books of the monks.

units.la: 5 Teste omnium temporum historia atq; experientia, omnes ad unum haereticos quasi conjurasse contra miracula, quae per sanctos in ecclesia fiunt: Idq; propterea quia nulla illi vera miracula ad sua dogmata slabistabilienda ; patrare possint. Resp. Veris miraculis, quæ deducunt homines ad doctrinam s. literarum pie amplectendam, nihil derogamus. At quæstio est, an miracula necessario demonstrent veram ecclesiam & veros Christi servos? atq; hoc negamus. Deinde quod a Romanensium miraculis abhorreamus, illud non contingit ulla insania vel malitia, sed justo gloriæ divinæ amore, atq; idololatriæ odio; quia sunt detestanda idololatriæ instrumenta, sicuti abunde satis ostendimus antea.6. Catholicos inde a prisco seculis sanctorum miracula admirari & venerari tanquam sanctitatis et orthodoxæ doctrinæ illorum argumenta. Resp. Sanctorum miracula merito veneramur: at maximum discrimen est inter miracula sanctorum & Romanensium, quod ex ante dictis apparet.7. Lutherum et Calvinum non raro doctrinam suam miraculis confirmare studuisse, at frustra. ac proinde postea adversus miracula sanctorum conspirasse. Resp. Nunquam quam illud confirmari poterit idoneis & dignis testibus. imo falsum hoc est de Luthero & Calvino testimonium. deinde illi immediatam vocationem, qualis erat apostolorum, nunquam sibi arrogarunt. praeterea cur miraculis doctrinam suam non confirmarent, causam dixerunt, quod non ex revelatione extraordinaria nova doctrinam afferret, sed ex scriptis propheticis & apostolicis: denique ex literis contra eos disseruerunt, qui hoc tempore sibi miracula arrogat. plura vide supr. quaest. de doctoribus protestantium objecit. ii.
units.tr: 5 The history and experience of all ages testify that all heretics, to a man, have as it were conspired against the miracles which are wrought through the saints in the Church, and this because they could perform no true miracles to establish their dogmas. Reply: We detract nothing from true miracles, which lead men to embrace the doctrine of holy Scripture devoutly. But the question is whether miracles necessarily demonstrate the true Church and the true servants of Christ, and this we deny. Further, that we abhor the miracles of the Romanists is not due to any madness or malice, but to a just love of the glory of God and a hatred of idolatry; for they are detestable instruments of idolatry, as we have shown abundantly above. 6 The Catholics have from early ages admired and venerated the miracles of the saints as proofs of their holiness and of their orthodox doctrine. Reply: We rightly venerate the miracles of the saints; but there is the greatest difference between the miracles of the saints and those of the Romanists, as appears from what has been said before. 7 Luther and Calvin often strove to confirm their doctrine by miracles, but in vain; and therefore afterwards they conspired against the miracles of the saints. Reply: This could never be confirmed by fit and worthy witnesses; indeed this testimony about Luther and Calvin is false. Moreover, they never claimed for themselves an immediate calling such as the apostles had. Besides, as to why they did not confirm their doctrine by miracles, they gave the reason: that they did not bring a new doctrine by extraordinary revelation, but from the prophetic and apostolic writings. Finally, they argued against those who in this age claim miracles for themselves. See more above, in the question on the objections of the Protestant teachers, ii.

units.la: De tutissima via promovendi pacem et concordiam ecclesiarum.
units.tr: On the safest way of promoting peace and concord among the churches.

units.la: EXstant de hoc argumento integri tractatus virorum praestantissimorum. Insigne etiam de hoc argumento scriptum, etsi pacis hostibus invisum, Irenicum, sive de unione & synodo evangelicorum conciliandâ[?] liber Davidis Paraei, Doctoris, Theologi Heidelbergensis.
units.tr: Complete treatises on this subject exist by the most distinguished men. There is also a notable work on this subject, though hateful to the enemies of peace: the Irenicum, or book on uniting the evangelicals in union and synod, by David Paraeus, Doctor and Theologian of Heidelberg.

units.la: Nos pro ratione nostri instituti pauca subiiciemus, & dicimus
units.tr: For our part, in keeping with our purpose, we shall set down a few points, and we say:

units.la: Omnes & singuli: principes & subditi, literati & illiterati; personae ecclesiasticae & politicae, hoc unum sibi propositum habeant sancte, ut rixae & contentiones sopiantur, atque omnes coagmentati in fide unum idemque loquamur, sentiamus.
units.tr: All and each, princes and subjects, learned and unlearned, ecclesiastical and civil persons, should hold this one aim sincerely before them: that quarrels and contentions may be quieted, and that all, joined together in the faith, may speak and think one and the same thing.

units.la: 2 Præmissa seriâ Dei invocatio-ne, attendant, in quibus articulis ecclesiæ consentiant; de quibus vero dissentiant.
units.tr: 2 With earnest invocation of God first made, let them consider in which articles the Churches agree, and in which they disagree.

units.la: 3 Nullus jurato in ullius ecclesiæ vel doctoris confessionem aut verba, nullus etiam moveatur ullius hominis promissis, minis, gratiâ, atque auctoritate.
units.tr: 3 Let no one be bound by oath to the confession or words of any Church or teacher; nor let anyone be moved by the promises, threats, favour or authority of any man.

units.la: 4 Sed quisquis solas scripturas s. agnoscat pro unico fidei fundamen-to & norma.
units.tr: 4 Rather, let whoever acknowledges the holy Scriptures alone as the sole foundation and rule of faith.

units.la: 5[?] Controversias ordine, modestè ac pacificè sine præjudiciis, factionibus, acerbitate, scommatibus, contumeliis attendat, legat, & singula capita distinctè perpendat. Sicuti ostendimus supr. quaest. Qua-ratione viri pii certi esse possint de veritate professionis suae pag. 131. et seq.
units.tr: 5 Let him consider the controversies in order, modestly and peaceably, without prejudice, factions, bitterness, scoffing or insults; let him read, and weigh each head distinctly. As we have shown above, in the question "By what method may godly men be certain of the truth of their profession," p. 131 and following.

units.la: 6 Quaestiones singulas c[?]cipiat breviter & propriis ac perspicuis verbis.
units.tr: 6 Let him take up the individual questions briefly, in proper and clear words.

units.la: 7 Inquirat etiā accuratè de sententiis dissidentium, ne cui fiat in-juria.
units.tr: 7 Let him also enquire carefully into the opinions of those who disagree, so that no one is wronged.

units.la: 8 Adhibeat in consilium docto-res, & exercitatiores; comprimis autem, qui sunt viri pii, candidi, moderati, pacis & veritatis studiosi.
units.tr: 8 Let him take counsel from teachers, and the more experienced; above all from those who are godly, sincere, moderate, and lovers of peace and truth.

units.la: 9 Contrà fugiat contentiosos, superbos, clamosos, præcipites, suâ gloriam nō veritatem & pacem sectantes: fugiat item avaros & flagitiosos.
units.tr: 9 On the other hand, let him avoid the contentious, the proud, the clamorous, the rash, those who seek their own glory rather than truth and peace; let him likewise avoid the greedy and the disgraceful.

units.la: 10 Nemo etiam moveatur clamoribus & loquacitate eorum, qui plausibilius de causa sua disserere videntur.
units.tr: 10 Let no one be moved by the clamour and glib talk of those who seem to argue their cause more plausibly.

units.la: 11 Sed contrà ad exemplum Beroënsium quisq; scrutetur scripturas, & ad eas tanquam lydium lapi-dem, dem, quæcunque audit, examinet.
units.tr: 11 Rather, after the example of the Bereans, let everyone search the Scriptures, and test whatever he hears by them as by a touchstone.

units.la: 12 Qui sunt firmiores in fide, suscipiant infirmos cum omni lenita-te & tolerantiâ juxta præscriptum Pauli: Rom.16.1.
units.tr: 12 Those who are firmer in the faith should receive the weak with all gentleness and forbearance, according to the precept of Paul: Rom. 16:1.

units.la: 13 In omnium auribus resonet illud Christi Joh.13.34. Præceptum novum do vobis, ut alii alios diliga-tis, sicut, inquit, dilexi vos, ut vos e-tiam diligatis alii alios. & quod apostolus inculcat Rom.8.13. Non ergo amplius invicem judicemus: sed hoc judicate magis, ne ponatis offendiculum fratri vel scandalum.
units.tr: 13 Let the words of Christ, John 13:34, sound in the ears of all: "A new commandment I give you, that you love one another, as I have loved you, that you also love one another." And let the apostle's exhortation, Rom. 8:13, be heeded: "Let us therefore no longer judge one another, but judge this rather, that you put no stumbling block or occasion of offence in your brother's way."

units.la: 14 Et sanè ex hujus charitatis ne-glectu sunt omnia dulcissimi euan-gelii cursus impedimenta; Dixim[?] eo de argumento aliquid oratione de christiana charitate, quam, qui volet, legat & piè attendat.
units.tr: 14 Indeed, from neglect of this charity come all the hindrances to the course of the most sweet gospel. I have said something on this subject in the oration on Christian charity, which whoever wishes may read and consider devoutly.

units.la: 15 Dominus Jesus ingemiscenti ecclesiæ suæ succurrat, ex ignoran-tiâ peccantibus ignoscat; veritatè inquirentibus oculos ad videndum ejus lucem aperiat: eos qui scientes dulcissimæ veritatis luci contradi-cunt,
units.tr: 15 May the Lord Jesus come to the aid of his groaning Church, pardon those who sin through ignorance, open the eyes of those who seek the truth to see his light, and correct those who knowingly contradict the sweetest light of truth,

units.la: cunt; corrigat; præfractos & male-volos; confundat; & pacis studia o-minium mentibus aspiret, ut unũ tandem in ipso sentientes concor-dibus votis ejus nomen invocemus, & tandem æterna & cœlestia taber-nacula consequamur.
units.tr: correct them; confound the stubborn and ill-disposed; and breathe the zeal for peace into the minds of all, so that, at last, agreeing in him as one, we may call upon his name with harmonious prayers, and at last attain the eternal and heavenly tabernacles.

units.la: 16.
