Viri principes meminerint, quòd sint constituti à Deo nutricii ecclesiæ: ad proinde omnibus mo-dis conjunctis viribus ejus salutem promovere studeant, comprimis verò etiam episcopos carnales pro auctoritate sibi divinitus concessa increpent, moneant, jubeant, ut de-posita animorum acerbitate hoc u-num quærant, ut omnes & singuli in spiritu & veritate sincera ac pa-cata conscientia Deum rite colere possint.
units.tr: 16. Let the princes remember that they have been appointed by God as nursing fathers of the Church; therefore let them strive by every means, with united strength, to promote its welfare; and above all let them, with the authority divinely given to them, rebuke, admonish and command the carnal bishops, so that, laying aside bitterness of spirit, they may seek this one thing: that all and each may be able to worship God rightly, in spirit and truth, with a sincere and peaceful conscience.

units.la: 17. Ecclesiarum antistites patiâ-tur charitatem inter se redintegra-ri, & mutua odia, quibus diu satis ecclesia fuit turbata, deponant, à calumniis atq; invectivis abstineat, & Satyricorum libellorum, quibus hactenus terrarum orbem impleverunt, memoriam abolebant: & nihil aliud quàm simplicitatem doctrinæ atq; eloquiorum propheticorum & apostolicorum appetant & accuratè sequantur.
units.tr: 17. Let the leaders of the Churches allow charity to be restored among themselves, and lay aside the mutual hatreds by which the Church has long been sufficiently troubled; let them abstain from calumnies and invective, and let them abolish the memory of the satirical libels with which they have hitherto filled the world; and let them aim at and carefully follow nothing but the simplicity of doctrine and of the prophetic and apostolic words.

units.la: 18 Sanctè observetur quòd inculcavit laudatissimus Imperator Constantinus episcopis, quos Niceæ congregaverat: & legitur apud Theodoretum libr. 1. histor. cap. 1. Nihil, inquit, indignius, quàm hostibus fidei domitis, quum nemo inveniatur amplius qui rebellare audeat, ipsos inter se sacerdotes committi, jurgiis & conviciis se mutuo proscindentes: atq; eâ rerisum[?] præbe-re & voluptatem hostibus doctrinæ, præcipuè in disputationibus rerum divinarum ac fidei: in quibus tamen habent sanctissimi Spiritus doctrinam præscriptam: Evangelici enim & apostolici libri, nec nō & antiquissimorum Prophetarum oracula plenè instruunt nos, quid de voluntate Dei sentiendum nobis bis sit. proinde hostili posita dis-cordiâ literarum divinitus inspira-tarum testimoniis res in quæstione adductas dissolvamus.
units.tr: 18 Let it be carefully observed what the most praiseworthy Emperor Constantine impressed upon the bishops whom he had gathered at Nicaea. It is read in Theodoret, book 1 of the History, chapter 1: "Nothing," he said, "is more unworthy than that, now that the enemies of the faith have been subdued and no one is left who dares to rebel, the priests themselves should be set against one another, tearing each other apart with quarrels and insults, and so offer laughter and pleasure to the enemies of the doctrine, especially in disputes about divine and faith matters. Yet they have the teaching of the most holy Spirit laid down for them: the Gospel and apostolic books, and also the oracles of the most ancient Prophets, fully instruct us what we ought to think about the will of God. Therefore let us settle the questions raised, not by hostile discord, but by the testimonies of the divinely inspired writings."

units.la: 19 Comburantur ad ejusdem exemplum contentiosorum homi-num, licet doctissimorum libri, qui-bus pacem ecclesiæ hactenus tur-batam vidimus. Ita, namq; prædi-ctus Imperator cõburi jusit libel-los contentiosorum episcoporum, & memorabilem hanc adjecit sen-tentiam; Christum præcepisse, ut, qui veniam impetrare contendat, patri ipse veniam det. vide Socrat. histor. libr. 1. cap. 5.
units.tr: 19 In the same way, let the books of contentious men, however learned they may be, which we have seen to have disturbed the peace of the Church until now, be burned. For the aforesaid Emperor ordered the libels of the contentious bishops to be burned, and added this memorable saying: that Christ commanded that the one who seeks to obtain pardon should himself give pardon to the Father. See Socrates, Histories, book 1, chapter 5.

units.la: 20 Omnes & singuli pii; viri, fœ-minæ; docti, indocti, [?] seriis ad Deum precibus juvent antistites ecclesia-rum, & quantum possunt salutari-bus consiliis & auxiliis conjunctio-nem fraternam omnibus commē-dentae [?] suadeant.
units.tr: 20 All and each of the pious, men and women, learned and unlearned, should assist the bishops of the churches with earnest prayers to God, and, as far as they can, with salutary counsels and help, should urge brotherly unity, commending it to all.

units.la: 21 Cogitemus Dei mandatum esse, ut in fide & charitate invicem conjuncti vivamus, & adversus regnum Satanæ nostra vota, consilia ac studia conjungamus.
units.tr: 21 Let us consider that it is God's command that we live joined to one another in faith and love, and that we join our vows, counsels and efforts against the kingdom of Satan.

units.la: 22 Esto, non consentiant in omnibus quidam ex doctoribus ecclesiarum; sufficiat primum, si cernatur de fundamento doctrinæ christianæ consensus.
units.tr: 22 Granted, some of the teachers of the churches do not agree on everything; it is enough, first of all, if agreement is seen concerning the foundation of Christian doctrine.

units.la: 23 Deus semper pro suâ gratiâ servaturus est, qui superædificent aurum, argentum & lapides pretiosos. Quodsi vero etiam reperiantur, qui superædificant ligna, fœnum, stipulam; cum omni modestiâ ac mansuetudine, cum animi lenitate tolerent alii alios per charitatem: atque ita servare studeamus unitatem spiritus per vinculum pacis.
units.tr: 23 God, for his grace, will always preserve those who build upon it gold, silver and precious stones. But if indeed there are also found those who build upon it wood, hay and straw, let others bear with one another in love, with all modesty and gentleness, with a mild spirit, and so let us take care to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

units.la: 24 De fundamento audiatur apostolus Paulus 1. Corinth. 3.11. Fundamentum aliud nemo potest statuere, præter id, quod positum est, qui est Iesus Christus. Item Eph. 2. 20. Estis superstructi super fundamentum apostolorum & prophetarum, cuius imus angularis lapis est ipse Christus Iesus. Quibus addec ex act. 4.12.
units.tr: 24 On the foundation, let the Apostle Paul be heard, 1 Corinthians 3:11: "No one can lay any other foundation than that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ." Likewise Ephesians 2:20: "You are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, of which the chief cornerstone is Christ Jesus himself." To these let me add Acts 4:12.

units.la: Non edim[?] [illegible, ~12 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters] [illegible, ~20 letters]
units.tr: [illegible in the scan]

units.la: Non est in alio quóquam salus: nec enim aliud nomen est sub cœlo, ꝗ datum sit inter homines, per quod oporteat nos servari. & act. 10. 43. Huic etiam omnes prophetæ testi-monium dant, remissionem pecca-torum accepturum per nomen e-ius quemvis, qui crediderit in eum. vulgò in ecclesia fundamentum & capita doctrinæ christianæ dici so-lent Decalogus, symbolum apo-stolicum, oratio dominica, Institu-tio Baptismi & scœnæ.
units.tr: "There is salvation in no one else; for there is no other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved." And Acts 10:43: "To him all the prophets also bear witness, that through his name whoever believes in him shall receive forgiveness of sins." Commonly in the Church the foundation and heads of Christian doctrine are said to be the Decalogue, the Apostles' Creed, the Lord's Prayer, and the institution of Baptism and the Lord's Supper.

units.la: 25 De superædificatione docto-rum ecclesiæ super fundamentum audi Augustinum lib.1. contra Julian. cap.2. Alia sunt, inquit, in quibus inter se aliquando etiam doctissimi atque optimi regulæ catholicæ defensores, salvâ fidei compage, non consonant: & alius alio de unâ re meliùs aliquid dicit & veriùs. Item Augustanæ confessionis Apologiam artic. 7. de ecclesia. Et sanctorum patrum scripta testantur, quod interdũ sti-pulas etiâ ædificaverint supra fundamentum, sed quæ non evertunt fidem.
units.tr: 25 On the building up of the teachers of the Church upon the foundation, hear Augustine, book 1 against Julian, chapter 2: "There are other matters," he says, "on which at times even the most learned and best defenders of the catholic rule do not agree with one another, the bond of faith remaining intact; and one speaks better and more truly about one matter than another." Likewise the Apology of the Augsburg Confession, article 7, on the Church: "And the writings of the holy Fathers testify that at times they have even built stubble upon the foundation, but stubble which does not overthrow the faith."

units.la: 26 Imò verò nullum seculũ fuit ita felix, ut omnino consenserint ad unum omnes ecclesiæ doctores in omnibus, consule historias, & reperies etiam patrum dissensiones satis graves. Apud Sozom. libr. 6. hi-stor. cap. 15. legitur inter Basilium magnum et Eusebiũ cæsariensem adeo grave dissidium fuisse exortum, ut ille ecclesiâ desertâ in pontum secesserit. Ex epist. Aug. ep. 19. & alijs liquet, quàm acris altercatio fuerit inter Hieronymum senem presby-terum, & Augustinum juvenem episcopum de loco Gal. 2. 11. Ex Hie-ron. contra Ruffin. constat satis acriter fuisse litigatum de quibusdam scripturæ s. interpretationibus inter Hieronymum & Johannem episcopum Hierosolymitanum. Item inter eundem Hieronymũ & Rufinum de scriptis Origenis. Non minùs grave dissidium de libris Origenis intercessit Epiphanio cum Johan-
units.tr: 26 Indeed, no age has ever been so happy that all the teachers of the Church agreed in everything, without exception. Consult the histories, and you will find quite serious disagreements even among the Fathers. In Sozomen, book 6 of the History, chapter 15, we read that a dispute so grave arose between Basil the Great and Eusebius of Caesarea that the former, abandoning the Church, withdrew to Pontus. From the letter of Augustine, epistle 19, and others, it is clear how sharp the quarrel was between Jerome, an old presbyter, and Augustine, a young bishop, concerning the passage in Galatians 2:11. From Jerome against Rufinus it is established that there was a rather bitter dispute over certain interpretations of Holy Scripture between Jerome and John, bishop of Jerusalem; likewise between the same Jerome and Rufinus concerning the writings of Origen. No less serious a dissension arose between Epiphanius and John concerning the books of Origen.

units.la: 27 At nihilominus tamen christianam unitatem & concordiam in fide sanctè servarunt.
units.tr: 27 Nevertheless, they holily preserved Christian unity and concord in the faith.

units.la: 28 Quin verò etiam orthodoxi cum Novatianis, à quibus alioqui plurimum dissidebant, pium syncretismum contra Arianos fecerunt, propter communem fidem ὁμοούσιον apud Socrat. hist. lib. 5.
units.tr: 28 Indeed, the orthodox even made a pious union with the Novatians, from whom they otherwise differed greatly, against the Arians, on account of the common faith in the homoousion [ὁμοούσιον], as in Socrates, Histories, book 5.

units.la: 29 Quorum vestigiis insistentes duo laudatissimi doctrinæ salvificæ præcones Lutherus & Zwinglius dissidium inter Witebergenses & Helveticas ecclesias de quibusdam capitibus religionis Christianæ concitatum, postea quam Marpurgi convenissent, sepeliri voluerunt, & consensum in toto genere doctrinæ sanciverunt, aliisque tuendum commendarunt, unicâ tantum illâ quæstione excepta de præsentia corporis Christi in coenâ.
units.tr: 29 Following these footsteps, the two most praiseworthy heralds of the saving doctrine, Luther and Zwingli, when they had met at Marburg, wished to bury the dissension stirred up between the Wittenberg and the Swiss churches over certain heads of the Christian religion. They confirmed agreement in the whole range of doctrine, and commended it to others to be defended, with that one question excepted, concerning the presence of Christ's body in the Supper.

units.la: 30 Non minùs autem charitatem mutuam inter dissidentes fovendam esse decreverunt, ac singugulis ecclesiis: suam libertatem de s. coena quam commodissime loquendi salvam reliquerunt: satisq; esse judicarunt si animi coalescerent, & consensus articulorum summarius in ecclesiis vigeret.
units.tr: 30 They decided, however, that mutual charity is equally to be cherished among those who disagree, and among the individual churches. They left each church's freedom to speak of the Lord's Supper in the most suitable way, and judged it enough if their hearts came together and a summary agreement on the articles flourished in the churches.

units.la: [?] Legatur Lutheri epistola ad ecclesias Helveticas, quae extat in ejus operibus, verba ejus haec sunt: simpliciter tenemus verba: Hoc est corpus meum: Hoc est sanguis meus: veruntamen si, quod prius dixi, non omnino satis recte mentem mutuo percipimus: hoc in praesens optimum sit, ut invicem amici simus, & optima quaeq; mutuo de nobis invicem polliceamur, donec gluma & foeculenta aqua tandem subsidat. Item: Insuper, ut dilectio & amicabilis concordia inter nos perfecta vigeat, ex parte nostra nihil faciemus reliquum: cumprimis ego, quantum ad me, omnem offensam penitus ex animo delebo, vobisq; amorem & fidem omnem polliceor, quantumvis enim nos, qui hanc rem serio agimus, summa quæq; egerimus, semper tamen auxilio Dei & consilio majore indigebimus; quandoquidem Satan summus noster & concordiæ hostis, facile suos noverit invenire; per quos summa imis contutbet, ut nihil sit opus, nos diffidentiæ vel suspicionibus invicem indulgere, sed comprimis necessarium ut corda simul & dextras mutuò porrigamus, ne posteriora fiant deteriora prioribus.
units.tr: Let Luther's letter to the Swiss churches be read, which is found among his works. His words are these: "We simply hold to the words: 'This is my body'; 'This is my blood'. Yet if we have not understood each other's mind altogether rightly, as I said before, then for the present it would be best that we be friends with one another, and promise one another the best things about ourselves, until the dregs and muddy water finally settle." Likewise: "Moreover, so that love and friendly concord may flourish among us in perfect form, on our part we will leave nothing undone. Above all, I for my part will wipe out every offence completely from my heart, and I promise you all love and faith. For however much we who are seriously taking up this matter have accomplished the greatest things, we shall always need the help of God and a greater counsel; since Satan, our chief and the enemy of concord, will easily find his own people, through whom he may stir up the greatest troubles. Therefore there is no need for us to indulge in distrust or suspicions of one another, but above all it is necessary that we stretch out to one another both hearts and right hands together, lest the latter things become worse than the former."

units.la: 32 Similiter Euangelicæ ecclesiæ in Poloniâ, Bohemiâ, aliisq; locis, partim Augustanam, partim Bohemicam, partim Hussiticam, partim Helveticam confessionem profitentes sanctum in religione christianâ consensum sanciverunt, non obstantibus quorundam rituum atq; opinionum differentiis.
units.tr: 32 Likewise the evangelical churches in Poland, Bohemia and other places, professing partly the Augsburg Confession, partly the Bohemian, partly the Hussite, partly the Helvetic Confession, have confirmed a holy agreement in the Christian religion, notwithstanding some differences of rites and opinions.

units.la: 33 Et licet neque illic desint homines turbulenti, qui concordiam ecclesiarum suis calumniis, obtrectationibus, susurris, & variis contraditraditionibus, turbare conentur, interdum etiam nonnullis impo-nant, tamen exstiterunt hactenus viri pii, qui verbis & factis initum, consensum sancte semper tenen-dum omnibus summo studio com-mendent.
units.tr: 33 And although even there men are not lacking who, with their calumnies, detractions, whisperings and various contradictions, try to disturb the concord of the churches, and sometimes even impose on some people, nevertheless there have hitherto existed pious men who, by word and deed, most earnestly commend the agreement once entered into, to be always holily kept by all.

units.la: In formula consensus evangelicorum Sendomiriae in Polonia initi an. 1570. hæc leguntur. Convenimus, ut quemadmodum illi (vid. Augusta-nam confessionem profitentes) nos, (qui subscripserunt confessioni Helveticarum ecclesiarum) sic etiam nos illarum ecclesias eodem christiano amore prosequamur, & orthodoxas fateamur: extremumq; vale dicamus & altum silentium imponamus omnibus rixis, distractionibus, dissidiis, quibus euangelii cursus, non sine maxima multorum piorum offensione, impeditus est: & unde adversariis nostris no levis calumniandi & verae christianae religioni nostrae contradicendi occasio fuit subministrata: quin potius
units.tr: In the formula of agreement of the evangelicals, entered into at Sandomierz in Poland in the year 1570, these things are read: "We have agreed that just as those (who profess the Augsburg Confession) embrace us (who have subscribed to the Confession of the Helvetic churches), so also we should embrace their churches with the same Christian love, and acknowledge them as orthodox; and we should bid a final farewell and impose deep silence on all quarrels, distractions and dissensions, by which the course of the gospel has been impeded, not without the greatest offence to many pious people, and from which an occasion, not slight, of calumny against us and of contradicting our true Christian religion has been supplied to our adversaries; but rather..."

units.la: pacì & tranquillitati publicæ studere, charitatem mutuam exercere, & operas[?] mutuas ad ædificationem ecclesiæ pro fraterna conjunctione nostra præstare debemus.
units.tr: to cultivate peace and public tranquillity, to practise mutual charity, and to render mutual services for the building up of the Church, as our brotherly union requires.

units.la: Item Ritus autem & cerimonias uniuscujusq; ecclesiæ liberos relinquimus: non enim multum refert, qui ritus observentur, modò sarta tecta & incorrupta existat ipsa doctrina, & fundamentum fidei ac salutis nostræ: quemadmodum & ipsa confessio Augustana & Saxonica de eâ re docent.
units.tr: Likewise, we leave the rites and ceremonies of each church free. For it matters little which rites are observed, provided that the doctrine itself, the foundation of our faith and salvation, remains whole and uncorrupted. The Augsburg and Saxon Confessions also teach this on the matter.

units.la: Item Datis igitur junctisq; dextris sanctè promisimus & recepimus invicem omnes fidem & pacem colere, fovere, & indies ad ædificationem regni Dei magis magisq; amplificare velle: omnesq; occasiones distractionis ecclesiarum evitaturos.
units.tr: Likewise, therefore, with right hands given and joined, we have solemnly promised and mutually agreed that all of us will cherish and foster faith and peace, will wish to extend them more and more each day to the building up of the kingdom of God, and will avoid every occasion of division among the churches.

units.la: Utinam similiter nunc salutaria pacis & fraternæ conjunctionis consilia ineamus[?] ac promoveamus: quisque pro sua conditione & modulo
units.tr: Would that we now likewise enter upon and promote the salutary counsels of peace and brotherly union, each according to his station and ability.

units.la: Hæc pacis studia Deus omni benedictionum genere quam cumulatissimè pro sua immensa misericordia remunerabitur: si videlicet Dei gloriam atq; ecclesiæ salutem serio quærat & promovere studeant omnes.
units.tr: God will reward these labours for peace with every kind of blessing, most abundantly, in accordance with his immense mercy, provided that all earnestly seek the glory of God and the salvation of the Church and strive to advance them.

units.la: O beata itaq; terra, quæ gaudet consensu virorum piorum de vero Dei cultu, & sincerâ ipsorum concordiâ ac dilectione mutuâ. Eâ namq; nihil jucundius, nihil pulcrius, nihil item humano generi salutarius dici vel cogitari potest.
units.tr: O blessed land, which rejoices in the agreement of godly men concerning the true worship of God, and in their sincere harmony and mutual love. For nothing more pleasant, nothing more beautiful, and nothing more beneficial to the human race can be said or imagined.

units.la: Testatur id Psalies ps.133, ubi confert dulcissimâ illam membrorum ecclesiæ conjunctionem, balsamo fragrantissimo, quo ungebatur sacerdos summus, & rori fertilissimum Carmeli solum fœcundanti. Idem prædicant ministri evangelici in regno Poloniæ, postquam promulgassent consensum Sendo-miriensem, cujus paulo ante memini, in epistola ad principem Ludovicum comitem Palatinum Rheni, electorem. Nos,
units.tr: The Psalmist bears witness to this in Psalm 133, where he compares that most sweet union of the members of the Church to the most fragrant balm with which the high priest was anointed, and to the dew that makes fertile the very fruitful soil of Carmel. The evangelical ministers in the kingdom of Poland proclaim the same, after they had published the Consensus of Sandomierz, which I mentioned a little earlier, in a letter to the prince Ludwig, Count Palatine of the Rhine, elector. We,

units.la: Nos, inquiunt, qui in his Sarmaticis regionibus gregem Christi pasci-mus, quamvis diversos præceptores in perdiscenda unâ eademq; cœlesti doctrinâ habuerimus, alii Augustanæ, alii Bohemicæ, alii Helveticæ confessioni ritibúsq; assuefacti & addicti, quum aliquâ-diu sibimet quisq; in suo sensu placentes invicem contenderimus, &nō illepidū Antichristo spectaculum præbuerimus: tandem tum aucto[?]-ritate Spiritus S. pacem, concordi-am & amorem mutuum suadentis, tum etiam malis discordiæ per-moti, omnibus litibus finem impo-suimus, ac contendere jam in more non habemus. Cui cōcordiæ [NB] & amori mutuo Dominus ita be-nedicit, ut lætitiam ac fructum inde sequentem vix verbis satis declara-re possimus: nam non solùm illum illud in nostris conscientiis senti-mus; Ecce quàm bonum & jucun-dum fratres habitare in unum: sed etiam manifestè experimur, id ececclesiæ nostræ inter atrocissimos hostes, tam papistas quàm Arianos versanti, plurimùm conducere ad pacem externam, ad sublationem scandalorum, ad ædificationem ecclesiæ, & ad repressionem ac oppressionem hostium filii Dei, contra quos conjunctus exercitus Domini, triplici acie, quantò concordius, tantò fortius & præclarius cõtendit.
units.tr: "We," they say, "who feed the flock of Christ in these Sarmatian regions, though we have had different teachers in learning the one and the same heavenly doctrine, some accustomed and attached to the Augsburg Confession, some to the Bohemian, some to the Helvetic confession and its rites, have for some time contended with one another, each pleasing himself in his own opinion, and so provided Antichrist with no unpleasant spectacle. At last, moved both by the authority of the Holy Spirit urging peace, concord and mutual love, and also by the evils of discord, we have put an end to all strife, and we no longer have the habit of contending. [NB] The Lord blesses this concord and mutual love so richly that we can scarcely declare in words the joy and the fruit that follow from it. For we not only feel it in our consciences, 'Behold how good and pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together in unity,' but we also clearly experience that it greatly conduces to the external peace of our church, which lives among the most savage enemies, Papists as well as Arians; to the removal of scandals; to the edification of the church; and to the restraint and overthrow of the enemies of the Son of God, against whom the joined army of the Lord, in triple battle line, fights the more fittingly and gloriously the more harmoniously it is united."

units.la: Contrà, dissensionibus de religione & pugnis nihil tristius, nihil deformius vel perniciosus vitæ hominum evenire potest.
units.tr: On the other hand, nothing more sorrowful, nothing more disfiguring or more ruinous to human life can come about than disagreements over religion and quarrels.

units.la: At sentient tandem vindicem Dei manum, qui majores in dies disidiorum flammas accendunt.
units.tr: But they will at last feel the avenging hand of God, they who kindle ever greater flames of discord day by day.
